The reporting follow-up adds the public evidence records, their scientific summary guard and the supported capability command. Runtime changes after 1dc8cfb are limited to eleven factory docstrings; stripping docstrings gives identical runtime syntax trees. The complete follow-up suite passes 6,328 tests at 93.83% coverage, with 242 skips and 13 deselections. All 145 focused command, scientific-record and selector checks pass. A real quick command run completes four studies and ten forecasts, verifying data/source/artifact hashes, frozen winners, dependencies and native thread settings. A newly built wheel again passes 334 installed checks, and all runtime bytes match source, sdist and installed package. Strict docs and static checks pass. The final hosted checks are recorded on PR #465.

docs.title: Vanilla forecasting robustness
docs.text: The previous independent-trajectory study found no prediction regression against the accepted implementation. It also found that the friendly vanilla recipes fell short of the typical seven-to-eight Lyapunov-time goal. This continuation tests stronger recipes without choosing settings on those inspected test runs.

docs.title: What changes in the model
docs.text:
rd.ESN(..., input_to_readout=False) fits the prediction head on reservoir memory alone. The default True also supplies the current input. The same setting is available on classic_esn; ordinary construction keeps its default. Automatic vanilla tuning searches both choices with its existing budgets. OTT's augmented features are unchanged. See the model workflow for usage and the tuning reference for controls.

Changing this switch does not change initialized reservoir weights. The first two trials below compare identical settings and reservoir weights, differing only in the head's features. Subsequent trials vary several settings, so their results describe whole recipes rather than the effect of this switch alone.

docs.title: Validation before final testing
docs.text:
The checked-in runner is benchmarks/vanilla_robustness.py. It uses standard Optuna TPE and public Torch fit/forecast calls. Each candidate is fitted separately on three new trajectories per system, with three reservoir seeds and three nonoverlapping forecast starting points. A batch fit would share one readout across trajectories and would answer a different question.

Both systems use canonical Lorenz/Rössler parameters and TSDynamics DOP853 integration at rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12. The protocol records exact initial conditions, sampling intervals and solver settings before integration. The search attempts at most 24 configurations per system with 600 seconds of soft search time. An admitted configuration finishes all its seed/origin checks; neither pruning nor optional screening is enabled. Both controlled baseline trials must complete, even if the time budget expires before additional trials.

Search controls are width, spectral radius, leak, input strength, bias strength, recurrent degree, ridge strength and the input-to-readout choice. The numerical policy is fixed: float64 Torch SVD with an unpenalized intercept. Training-only standard scaling and full observed history are used throughout.

The objective is the median of the three trajectory medians at the 0.3 error threshold. Each trajectory median contains nine seed/origin forecasts. Per-step error is RMS error divided componentwise by training standard deviation, measured on raw[washout + 1 : train_observations], matching the preceding primary protocol. A forecast ends at its first error greater than or equal to the threshold, or its first nonfinite error. Both 0.3 and 0.5 results are retained.

Both winners are frozen before generating any final observations. Final tests compare the preceding primary vanilla recipe with the selected recipe on five fresh trajectories per system, three fresh seeds and three starting points. Each window spans ten Lyapunov times. Results at that limit are right-censored: they establish accuracy through the window, without estimating its later end. The independent unit is a trajectory, not each nested forecast.

docs.title: Reproduce the experiment
docs.text:
Install the repository's development, HPO and dynamics extras, and the pinned benchmark requirements, in an isolated environment. From the repository root:

python benchmarks/vanilla_robustness.py --output /tmp/resdag-vanilla-study

The output directory must not exist. --quick runs a small execution smoke; its short synthetic protocol is not forecast-quality evidence. --trials and --timeout allow explicit budgets; changing them defines a different experiment.

The runner freezes the runtime source and records source/helper hashes, dependency versions, IC and reservoir seed banks, generated observations, warning messages, completed and failed trials, controlled reservoir fingerprints, frozen winners, full error traces and prediction hashes. Partial final failures retain a failure receipt. Dataset hashes are checked before loading. Its saved runner.py is a provenance copy: rerun it from the original repository layout with the recorded runtime, helpers and dependencies. It is not a standalone installed application.

Timing observations in this study are exploratory. They do not establish a controlled CPU ranking or any CUDA performance claim. See the phase-five measurements for the separate speed evidence.

docs.title: Held-out results
docs.text:
The run completed all 48 validation trials: 24 per system, with 432 fits and 1,296 forecasts. Both selected recipes were frozen before the final bank was generated. Final evaluation used 60 separate fits and 180 forecasts, including each incumbent control, with no exclusions or failed fits.

The main statistic is the median of five independent trajectory medians. Each trajectory contributes nine forecasts from three initialization seeds and three starting points. The individual range shows the nested forecasts' spread; it is not a confidence interval. A ≥ sign means the forecast remained below the threshold through the ten-Lyapunov-time observation window.

System / recipe Median at 0.3 (LT) Median at 0.5 (LT) Individual range at 0.3 (LT) Censored at 0.3 Lorenz incumbent and selected recipe ≥10.016 ≥10.016 2.155–≥10.016 27 / 45 Rössler incumbent 3.013 3.810 0.849–9.225 0 / 45 Rössler selected recipe 6.750 7.154 1.677–≥10.001 1 / 45

All five trajectory medians at the main 0.3 threshold, in their recorded order:

  • Lorenz: [≥10.016, 5.995, ≥10.016, 9.654, ≥10.016].
  • Rössler incumbent: [3.013, 2.899, 3.810, 3.800, 2.485].
  • Rössler selected: [7.144, 6.253, 6.750, 8.779, 6.233].

Lorenz retained the existing primary recipe. Rössler improved from 3.01 to 6.75 LT on the fresh test bank, but the typical 7–8 LT goal at 0.3 remains unmet. The more forgiving 0.5 result does not replace that criterion. These are bounded vanilla-model accuracy results, not a comparison against other libraries or a guarantee for other systems.

Both winners use input_to_readout=True. In the controlled validation pair, Lorenz scored 10.016 LT with the input and 4.800 LT without it; Rössler scored 4.576 and 4.638 LT respectively. All other settings and initialized reservoirs were identical within each pair. The later Rössler gain comes from selecting a whole recipe; it cannot be attributed to the new switch alone. The default therefore remains unchanged, and tuning can still select either configuration.

The selected Rössler recipe is:

import torch
import resdag as rd

model = rd.ESN(
    input_size=3,
    reservoir_size=400,
    spectral_radius=0.316473400694296,
    leak_rate=0.6988018952693786,
    feedback_initializer=("random", {"input_scaling": 0.3162866539497749}),
    bias_scaling=0.029171927900014934,
    alpha=2.8843872485074098e-11,
    topology=("erdos_renyi", {"p": 6 / 400, "directed": True, "self_loops": True}),
    washout=500,
    seed=7849201,
    input_to_readout=True,
    readout="svd",
    dtype=torch.float64,
)

Use the recorded protocol's training length, washout, sampling interval and training-only scaling when reproducing these measurements. A parameter list alone does not reproduce an experiment; the download below records the full configuration and exact source.

docs.title: Failures and integrity
docs.text:
All validation fits completed, but 104 of the 648 Rössler validation forecasts became nonfinite. They remain in the report and are scored at their first invalid error, rather than being discarded. Lorenz validation and all 180 final forecasts were finite. No dataset-integrity failure or fit failure was observed. These are different conditions: a completed fit can still produce an unstable autonomous forecast.

After the API and persistence cleanup, a separate replay refitted all 60 final models. All 180 complete prediction arrays matched their recorded SHA-256 hashes byte for byte on this host. An independent NumPy calculation recovered every threshold crossing and error curve. This checks the adopted cleanup against the recorded experiment; it does not establish cross-device bitwise reproducibility.

Download the complete protocol, source manifest, frozen winners, every trial, error trace and prediction hash. The forecasting and animation guide uses the first predeclared held-out case for each system. Those display cases are fixed, include the complete recorded window and are not the headline aggregate.

docs.title: Verification status
docs.text: The scientific evaluation and exact replay are complete. The release-readiness record in the roadmap distinguishes local, installed-package and hosted verification. Phase five remains open for typical Rössler accuracy, comparative CPU speed and broader model/hardware scales.

docs.title: Phase four: artifacts and efficient training
docs.text: Status: Implemented, verified and merged in PR #463, commit 0b546d6. The roadmap tracks acceptance and delivery. Phase four includes the maintainer-requested SQ-01 training optimization as P4-06. Documentation and tests ship alongside each implementation.

docs.title: Agreed interfaces
docs.text:
• model.save("run.pt") saves the complete model. rd.load("run.pt") reconstructs its graph without the user remembering its architecture.
  • Use standard Torch serialization for tensors and device mapping, versioned declarative component recipes for portable construction, and an explicit registry for custom code installed by the application.
  • Offer an optional cloudpickle bundle for notebook-local classes/functions. Saving and loading bundled Python both require explicit trusted=True.
  • Preserve ordinary-forward reservoir memory by default, with include_state=False available. Preserve fitted preprocessing and observed forecasting history. Reservoir memory does not include delayed forecast queues, an iterator cursor or its clock.
  • model.save("run.svg"), .png, .pdf and .dot export diagrams through standard Graphviz/DOT. Inspection does not execute the graph or open viewers.
  • model.fit(data, targets=final_values, readout_targets={"stage1": intermediate_values}) trains hidden readouts without adding outputs. Internal target tensors use the complete input clock and the desired internal output units. Public preprocessing stays unchanged.

docs.title: One traversal for multiple readouts
docs.text:
The trainer owns a warmup-plus-training prefix and resets recurrence once. It executes operations in topological order. At a readout, it fits on the training suffix only, then forwards the full prefix using those fitted weights. Downstream reservoirs receive those actual predictions during warmup and training. Shared branches are reused, and cached values are released after their last consumer.

Normal PyTorch module calls preserve graph, container and leaf hooks. Standard nn.Sequential expresses nested ordering. Ambiguous custom containers and a readout object invoked at multiple graph positions are rejected before fitting; fanout from one readout invocation remains valid. Fitting a shared mutable graph concurrently is unsupported. Fit before wrapping a model with torch.compile. Custom outer forward bodies are rejected rather than bypassed; customize declared operations or hooks.

Temporal operations now see an uninterrupted prefix. Stochastic layers, including reservoir noise, consume random draws in a different order from the old replaying implementation; repeatability is tested, but old noisy fit results can change. The common Model.fit stages and commits on success; the raw trainer mutates in place.

docs.title: Verification boundaries
docs.text:
Independent regression/recurrence oracles check fitted coefficients, downstream features, final states and forecasts. Structural tests count calls and samples, exercise branching/merge liveness and verify hooks and failure cleanup. The controlled CPU benchmark reports fixed workload measurements, propagation/readout timing, variability and process peak memory. It is not a cross-library or GPU speed claim.

Artifact acceptance includes fresh-process reconstruction, ordinary-stream continuation, preprocessing/history/trajectory metadata, graph families, custom codecs, trusted notebook bundles, storage aliases, device mapping and clear version errors. Loading does not restore an optimizer, autograd history, live HPO database connection or an autonomous rollout cursor.

docs.title: Phase three: reliable tuning
docs.text: Status: Done — merged and released in 3.0.0. The roadmap records the implementation and verification. The common model.tune(...) lifecycle, joblib execution and automatic readout are released in 2.1.0. The continuation adds forecast-generation pruning, optional screening and memory planning, and safe raw-runner reuse. All local and locked/latest hosted acceptance gates pass in PR #462, merged as f8d7637. Release publication, post-merge CI and installed-package verification passed.

docs.title: Approved experience
docs.text:
Tuning builds candidate models, trains them, compares their autonomous forecasts and keeps the winning configuration. Basic ESNs and custom DAGs use the same command. Quick, balanced and thorough presets control the amount of work; balanced is the default. Advanced users retain their own Optuna samplers, search spaces and objectives.

The maintainer approved:

  • model.tune(data) reserves the last 20% chronologically for validation, then refits the winner on all supplied development data. Keep the final test data outside this call. Explicit splits remain available.
  • A custom DAG may supply a Python construction recipe for each candidate. Changing reservoir sizes can require changing the downstream readout width; the recipe rebuilds those connections together. Preset ESNs do this automatically.
  • The same outer model object receives the fitted winner. Its internal graph and parameters may change. Tune before creating a PyTorch optimizer.
  • The existing automatic-solver goal remains: choose a safe method, allow explicit overrides, and disclose precision, device and fallback decisions.
  • Balanced tuning checks every candidate with its full seed/origin bank by default. Optional screening first evaluates a smaller bank, then reevaluates the promoted candidates using the full bank before choosing a winner.
  • Transfer to another task reuses settings and scores them again. Copying completed scores requires an exact match of the recorded evaluation protocol.
  • An optional memory budget reduces concurrency and skips an oversized candidate before construction. Estimates never change its architecture or precision and are not operating-system allocation limits. Custom recipes provide their own estimates.

The fluent interface returns the same model, like fit. model.tuning_report exposes the full Optuna study, resolved winning settings, fixed seeds, validation windows, errors and timings. Candidate evaluation, final refitting and owned-storage cleanup finish before replacing the current model. Changing internal parameters requires creating any PyTorch optimizer afterward.

docs.title: Data and timing safeguards
docs.text:
Trials use the common Model.fit and Model.forecast behavior, including training-only preprocessing, named ports, prediction leads, feedback delays, device placement and trajectory timestamps. The older raw-graph HPO runner does not provide this common workflow by itself.

Validation boundaries must account for prediction distance. If training observations stop at sample 800 and an output predicts two samples ahead, the example originating at sample 799 has its label at 801. That example must not enter the training solve. All observations through 800 can still warm the reservoir. Final refitting must keep the last supplied observation as the forecast endpoint.

For trajectories, split the raw observations before interpolation. Otherwise PCHIP or cubic coefficients can depend on the validation suffix. Tensor targets need equally explicit alignment: each target row labels its input origin plus the declared prediction lead.

Every configuration faces the same initialization seeds and forecast starting points. Scoring scales stay fixed across forecast prefixes; recomputing them from a growing validation suffix changes the meaning of an early pruning score. Named outputs require explicit aggregation rather than silently scoring the first head.

The private streaming executor retains delayed-feedback queues and emits aligned forecast chunks. Scoring accumulates on the tensor device; only scalar checkpoint summaries cross to the parent for an Optuna pruning decision. Stopping closes the stream before more predictions are generated. Ordinary public forecast() retains its established optimized execution path.

Whole-forecast custom objectives still receive the complete prediction. They can prune between completed seed/origin runs, or supply a separate pruning_objective that explicitly accepts prefixes. A pruned or screened-only candidate cannot become the winner. History replay and custom objectives can retain growing histories or prediction prefixes; those memory costs are explicit.

docs.title: Winner and parallel policy
docs.text:
• The default reward is the length of the contiguous accurate forecast, using a normalized error threshold of 0.2 and fixed training-only scales.
  • Within an origin, batch cases use their median horizon; multiple heads use the weakest horizon. The trial uses the median across seeds and origins. Mean head aggregation and custom objectives remain available.
  • n_jobs=1 runs in the caller. More workers use joblib/loky with notebook recipe support and bounded submission windows. Failed attempts consume the configuration budget. A timeout stops new windows; already running work and the final refit finish normally.
  • Reusing a study requires the same recorded data/task, seeds, objective and construction recipe. Foreign evaluated scores are rejected. Standard Optuna queued configurations remain supported.
  • The parent owns sampling, storage and pruning decisions in both workflows. Workers receive prepared numerical jobs through joblib/loky. The raw runner no longer launches or monitors its own worker processes.
Preset New configurations Initialization seeds Forecast origins Quick 8 1 1 Balanced 24 3 3 Thorough 80 5 5

Each budget can be overridden. The default horizon is half the validation span and stays the same across presets. Origins can overlap and are not independent replicates. A custom DAG without a construction recipe retains its feature weights and uses one initialization; it does not pretend that copying the same weights produces independent reservoirs. Explicit validation remains outside the final refit. See the tuning guide.

The friendly ESN now defaults to readout="auto", with guarded primal/dual Cholesky, augmented QR and SVD routes. Forced methods keep their algorithm and requested alpha. Reports disclose precision, conditioning and any CPU bridge; finite precision still limits coefficient accuracy. The lower-level factories retain their explicitly documented readout defaults. See readout solvers.

docs.title: First correctness increment
docs.text:
The initial work repairs independent defects before adding the new lifecycle:

  • SVD ridge filter factors avoid squaring large finite singular values. The requested regularization is preserved. Non-finite or negative alpha and rcond are rejected at construction and before solving.
  • Study transfer skips missing/non-finite completed scores, including trials produced outside ResDAG. Matching multi-objective values remain intact.
  • Study summaries order their top trials in the actual objective direction.
  • Owned RDB sessions and persistent-database connection pools are released after run_hpo, even when setup or trial evaluation fails. A returned SQLite memory study retains its backing pool so its data survives. Path-based transfer releases its own source connections; caller-supplied studies retain their ownership. A cleanup failure cannot hide the original operation error.

Both tuning workflows now use managed finite joblib windows and parent-owned Optuna trials. Raw task binding also fingerprints materialized data and rechecks historical data on resume; opaque external resources need an explicit task context version. Active Python custom-layer implementations are included in provenance. Hashes guard recorded configuration, rather than proving arbitrary Python or native code semantically equivalent. Verification is recorded in the roadmap as each increment passes its checks.

docs.title: Phase two: the common model workflow
docs.text: Status: Done; merged through PR #460. See release verification in the roadmap. This page records current decisions and implementation boundaries. Start with the runnable common model guide or the shorter end-to-end guide.

docs.title: Agreed behavior
docs.text:
Basic ESNs and custom graphs share the same fit, forecast and state workflow. Unified tune and complete-artifact save commands remain phases three and four. Layers connect through the existing functional construction API: hidden = reservoir(input) and output = readout(hidden).

The common model is a PyTorch nn.Module:

  • model(x) applies scaling learned from training data and returns predictions in the original units. model.graph(x) exposes the raw underlying graph for pipelines that manage their own scaling.
  • Calls carry reservoir state by default. An explicit reset starts an unrelated sequence. Evaluation mode controls noise and other training behavior without implicitly resetting state.
  • One output returns a tensor. Multiple outputs return a dictionary using the names declared when constructing the model.
  • Ordinary forward calls retain PyTorch gradients and module hooks. Freezing reservoir weights still permits gradients to upstream modules.
  • Scaling statistics are registered buffers, so device/dtype conversions and checkpoints include them. Each input and target has its own preprocessing where their units or dimensions differ.

These decisions apply directly to the new major API. The maintainer chose no legacy wrapper or compatibility layer. Raw graph classes and trainers remain useful public building blocks for advanced workflows.

docs.title: Approved construction
docs.text:
The maintainer approved rd.Model(inputs={...}, outputs={...}). It wraps the existing symbolic graph in a common module with one registered graph child, reusing the current graph construction and execution infrastructure.

The following illustrates the implemented interface:

x = rd.reservoir_input(3)
h = reservoir(x)
y = readout(h)

model = rd.Model(inputs={"state": x}, outputs={"prediction": y})
model.fit(train)
prediction = model.forecast(history=observed, horizon=500)

The graph= form wraps an existing factory-built graph. The PyTorch ESN preset constructs one common workflow without requiring users to wire layers. Use input_size= or build() before attaching optimizers; an untouched lazy preset can instead infer width, dtype and device on its first fit.

Each graph is registered once, preserving parameter identities and avoiding duplicate checkpoint entries. See the ESN API changes.

docs.title: Current workflow
docs.text:
rd.Model accepts named symbolic inputs/outputs or an existing graph through graph=. It fits declared readout heads, returns original-unit forward and forecast predictions, and supports named targets and explicit recurrent state. Its state dictionary includes named-port/feedback metadata, fitted scaling and observed history. Loading validates their consistency before using them.

Declare every algebraically fitted readout as a named output and supply its target. An intermediate head can also feed a downstream reservoir; staged training fits it before collecting that reservoir's features. Unexposed internal fitted heads require the lower-level trainer's explicit targets.

Feedback connects named output/input ports with an explicit graph-step delay. prediction_lead separately records each head's target distance. Default self-feedback uses matching lead/delay, and forecasts always start at the first unseen physical sample. Pending warmup outputs prevent gaps for multi-step heads. Differing output/input scales are bridged through original units on the model device. See feedback and timing.

Custom framewise modules can declare supports_framewise=True. Pure temporal sequence operations can use execution="history": fitting and forecasting preserve the complete prefix. Fast models retain the optimized existing backend and compact warmup tail. Delayed rollout queues are reconstructed from history; reservoir state alone cannot resume such a rollout. See execution capabilities.

docs.title: Existing backend families
docs.text:
Model(graph=...) now also wraps ParallelESNModel and CoupledEnsembleESNModel. Small private adapters reuse their existing execution paths; the raw graph remains the sole registered graph child. Parallel ports represent full fields, and scaling precedes patch gathering. Coupled ports represent the shared member inputs and single aggregate output; each member's terminal readout name is resolved independently during fitting.

State, gradients, training-only scaling, checkpoint metadata and trajectory conversion use the same workflow. Parallel/coupled compiled forecasting is rejected before state changes because those raw forecast paths do not support the compile option. Their explicit-state paths keep their existing support. A reservoir hidden inside a custom coupled aggregator cannot participate in explicit-state or forecast execution; it is rejected before operations run. Ordinary stateful calls remain available.

Non-symbolic checkpoint schemas include patch geometry or ordered member interfaces, the aggregate selector/class, and persistent tensor name/shape signatures. They reject structural mismatches before copying tensors. Custom Python settings still belong to the compatible architecture supplied by the caller. Generic architecture reconstruction remains phase four.

The graph-tooling review records the evaluated standard tools. Functional construction stays in place; FX can capture a surrounding PyTorch pipeline using the documented leaf-module hook.

docs.title: Trajectory integration
docs.text:
The maintainer approved automatic, configurable resampling for uneven time axes, with uniform sampling as the normal case. A model fitted on a bare TSDynamics trajectory now returns a trajectory by default. The optional return_type="tensor" keeps forecasts on the model device; ordinary forward calls retain the Torch interface.

The trajectory's time axis defines sampling. Default interpolation preserves both endpoints and sample count; an explicit resample_dt creates an in-support grid ending at the latest observation. Later trajectory histories use the fitted interval and the same component names/order. Predictions begin at the immediate unseen time; optional warmup predictions start at history[max(prediction_leads.values()):], so every head shares the same physical timeline. New tensor histories require tensor output because they carry no absolute clock.

Named trajectory inputs align once on a shared grid inside their common observed range. The first declared model input supplies the default interval; resample_dt overrides it. Per-head trajectory targets are physical signals: an origin at t uses that head's label at t + prediction_lead * dt. Labels beyond the common observed endpoint are held out before interpolation. Fitting preserves the full input prefix and uses only jointly valid supervised rows after washout. Fast models retain a compact tail ending at the common observed endpoint; temporal models retain the full prefix.

Clock, per-port components and primitive source metadata survive current state-dictionary checkpoints without requiring TSDynamics at load time. Live producing-system objects remain transient. One output returns a trajectory; several return a dictionary with each target's own signal names and one shared future timeline. See the trajectory guide and named trajectories.

The common workflow packages the existing four normalization methods in an internal fitted PyTorch module. Statistics are learned only by an explicit fit operation, remain detached from training gradients, and do not update during inference. Transform and inverse operations preserve upstream gradients. Tests cover constant channels, refitting, checkpoint restoration, invalid data, and device/dtype behavior, including native MPS. The module is used internally by every supported Model family. Named input_transforms and output_transforms override individual ports with reversible Torch modules, including Standardize and nn.Identity. Fitting stages independent copies and preserves the original modules and parameters on successful commit. See custom preprocessing. Existing data-preparation defaults are unchanged. Minmax scaling now divides before multiplying, avoiding an intermediate overflow for large finite training ranges.

The workflow also guards explicit-state execution against reservoirs hidden inside containers or custom modules. Previously, such a call could change stored state and omit it from the returned state dictionary. The guard checks the entire execution plan before running any operation and provides a remedy: expose each reservoir as a separate functional graph node. Ordinary stateful graph calls and supported pointwise containers remain usable. See state management.

docs.title: Approved extensions
docs.text:
The maintainer approved these choices on 22 October 2026:

  • Custom preprocessing uses reversible changes of units that preserve signals. Temporal operations and transforms that add features belong inside the DAG.
  • Named TSDynamics inputs align automatically to a common sampling grid within their shared observed range. Resampling never extrapolates beyond observations. Targets use physical timestamps and each head's declared prediction lead.

Both extensions are implemented. Complete integrated and hosted verification passes; see the roadmap's completion record. The new major API uses current version-2 workflow/preset checkpoint metadata. Older common-workflow checkpoints require reconstruction and refitting; no compatibility converter is provided.

The public component recipes cover stable named seeds, registered initializers, recurrent cells, framewise transforms and the public ReadoutLayer.solve hook. User modules remain ordinary PyTorch components.

Tuning remains phase three. Complete model loading and diagram exports remain phase four. They will use the agreed common interface, with separate acceptance tests rather than placeholder methods.

docs.title: Related work
docs.text: Project

docs.title: Related work
docs.text: Reservoir computing has a healthy software landscape: NumPy-based libraries with broad method coverage and long histories, PyTorch research codebases attached to individual papers, and a maintained Julia stack. The closest neighbours are ReservoirPy (NumPy/SciPy), EchoTorch and RcTorch (PyTorch), and ReservoirComputing.jl (Julia). ResDAG takes a different set of trade-offs rather than competing feature-for-feature.

docs.title: Feature comparison
docs.text:
How ResDAG's surface area lines up against the four libraries above. A ✓ marks a documented, first-class capability; ~ a partial or undocumented one; — its absence. The point is positioning, not a scorecard — each library leads on the axes it was designed for.

Capability ResDAG ReservoirPy EchoTorch RcTorch ReservoirComputing.jl PyTorch-native (nn.Module) ✓ — ✓ ✓ — First-class GPU path ✓ ~ ~ ~ ~ NG-RC features ✓ ✓ — — ✓ Algebraic (ridge) readout ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Arbitrary DAG composition ✓ ✓ — — — Built-in ensembles ✓ — — — — Built-in HPO ✓ ✓ — ✓ —

The algebraic ridge readout is universal — it is the defining training step of reservoir computing — so the table separates on the rest: how the reservoir is composed, where it runs, and what is bundled around it. ReservoirPy is the broadest non-PyTorch neighbour (a Node/Model graph API, NG-RC, and hyperopt integration); ReservoirComputing.jl pairs NG-RC with the SciML ecosystem; the PyTorch codebases (EchoTorch, RcTorch) expose a single configurable reservoir rather than a composition surface, and both are no longer actively maintained. ResDAG is the one that treats reservoirs, readouts, and transforms as composable PyTorch parts wired into arbitrary DAGs.

For wall-clock numbers on identical architectures against ReservoirPy and ReservoirComputing.jl — training throughput, autoregressive generation, and forecast skill — see the benchmarks.

docs.title: What ResDAG optimizes for
docs.text:
Composition over configuration. Most reservoir software exposes a configurable pipeline: one reservoir, one readout, options on each. ResDAG exposes parts — reservoirs, readouts, transforms as PyTorch modules — and a functional API to wire them into arbitrary DAGs. Architectures from the literature (state augmentation, parallel reservoirs, multiple heads) are a few lines of composition instead of framework features.

PyTorch citizenship. Models are ordinary nn.Modules: they move with .to(device), serialize with state_dict(), embed in larger networks, and train with any optimizer. The algebraic one-pass fit and gradient descent are interchangeable paths over the same parameters, not separate systems.

GPU throughput. The sequence loop, the solver's precision strategy, and the training pass are engineered for CUDA; at research scale the GPU is an order of magnitude faster than the CPU path, and the regime is measured and documented, not assumed.

Documented mathematics. Every update equation, solver decision, and timing convention is written down against the code that implements it.

docs.title: Goals and decisions
docs.text:
• Autonomous dynamical-system forecasting is the easiest default workflow.
  • Presets and custom DAGs use the same fit, forecast, tune and save lifecycle.
  • Keep the expressive functional construction API, similar to building a Keras functional model. pytorch_symbolic remains supported while its limitations and available standard PyTorch alternatives are evaluated. Changing the backend must preserve that construction experience.
  • Prefer existing PyTorch, Optuna, Graphviz, SciPy and TSDynamics capabilities. Add a ResDAG abstraction only when a demonstrated requirement needs it.
  • Keep every component replaceable through public interfaces: initializers, cells, state, transforms, readouts, solvers, objectives and search spaces.
  • Automatic defaults must be dependable; users can force the solver, precision, device, preprocessing and execution choices.
  • Learn preprocessing from training data and return forecasts in original units. Keep preprocessing configurable and optional.
  • The common PyTorch workflow applies fitted preprocessing in model(x) and returns original units; model.graph(x) exposes the raw graph. Calls carry reservoir state by default. One output returns a tensor; several outputs return a dictionary keyed by their declared names.
  • Provide explicit delayed feedback connections and named inputs/outputs.
  • Keep TSDynamics optional, with first-class trajectory input/output.
  • Tuning has quick, balanced and thorough presets. Balanced is the default; the winning model is fitted and ready to forecast afterward.
  • Compare forecast accuracy, speed and memory together. Publish reproducible workload-specific results and distinguish measured hardware from skipped checks.
  • Breaking simplifications belong in a major release with migration guidance. Consult the maintainer before major implementation choices.

docs.title: Phase 1: correctness and verification
docs.text:
Preserve current public workflows while fixing incorrect behavior. Numerical corrections may change forecasts; explain those changes and review affected golden fixtures against independent references.

ID Status Work Acceptance checks / evidence P1-01 Done Stable batch and streaming readout statistics. Offset, rank-deficient and ill-conditioned fixtures agree with independently centered SVD/SciPy references; chunked fitting agrees with batch fitting. P1-02 Done Preserve working precision in incremental/RLS readouts; correct fresh RLS prior and FISTA convergence. .float() and factory construction retain the configured accumulation policy; fresh streaming parity; adversarial FISTA optimality; legacy checkpoints migrate explicitly. P1-03 Done Correct staged fitting when an upstream fitted readout drives downstream recurrent state. Fresh cascaded DAG agrees with a closed-form/stagewise oracle; ordinary one-stage fitting retains its fast path. P1-04 Done Correct inference mode, multi-head dtype preservation and divergent ensemble behavior. Repeatable noise-free inference; mode restoration; mixed float/integer output schemas preserved; finite-member and all-invalid policies tested. P1-05 Done Coherent sparse weight edits and live versus fixed cell settings. In-place weight changes affect actual recurrence; accepted configuration writes affect dynamics; fixed settings reject misleading edits. P1-06 Done Consistent initializer arguments, RNGs, precision, discovery and spectral scaling. Direct/name/tuple/object forms agree; required arguments work; local seeds are independent of unrelated draws; custom float64 is preserved; analytic spectral counterexamples pass. P1-07 Done Correct calibrated/vector-leak diagnostics and held-out memory-capacity evaluation. Actual-cell Jacobian/reference comparisons; caller state/modes preserved; held-out estimator validated with stated finite-sample limitations. P1-08 Done Repair current TSDynamics analysis integration and test it explicitly. Current supported TSDynamics analyses work; dependency-free tests run without the optional package; optional CI lane runs genuine integration tests. P1-09 Done Stop failed HPO evaluations masquerading as winners; validate transferred objective directions. Invalid evaluations are not selected as successful models; all-invalid studies fail clearly; incompatible transfer is rejected; error details remain accessible. P1-10 Done Repair generated initializer recipes and stale correctness/solver guidance. All 51 catalog recipes execute; defaults match implementations; examples teach held-out evaluation and training-only scaling. P1-11 Done Strengthen CI coverage and documentation selection. Docs-only changes select executable doc tests; optional integrations have a lane; full coverage remains near the established baseline; no performance thresholds weakened. P1-12 Done Review historical benchmark claims and record release verification. Historical results are clearly separated from current claims; full tests, strict docs, CPU gates, wheel/install checks and hosted CI recorded before release.

The regular graph now honors the requested degree, including odd degrees when the node count permits them. Cycle/jump overlaps add both contributions. These are intentional mathematical corrections approved for phase 1: regenerated weights and experiment results can change even with the same seed. Migration notes accompany both initializers.

Phase 1 did not change dataset normalization defaults, deep-stack seed schedules, feedback routing or the meaning of existing save() files. Later breaking changes are recorded in the major-release migration below.

docs.text:
The phase-two design note distinguishes agreed behavior, the agreed construction API, and implementation progress. The maintainer has approved rd.Model(inputs={...}, outputs={...}); later major choices still require consultation before implementation.

Current boundary: phase 1 orders algebraic fitting inside standard nn.Sequential, but the explicit-state and compiled backends cannot thread state through reservoirs hidden inside containers. Phase two rejects that case before running the graph, rather than changing stored state during a supposedly stateless call. Expose reservoirs as separate functional graph nodes for those execution paths. Ordinary stateful graph calls remain available.

P2-03 Done Named ports, branches/merges, multiple heads and explicit delayed feedback. P2-04 Done Coherent cell/state and execution semantics. Public framewise declaration and explicit full-history execution verified. P2-05 Done Training-only preprocessing owned by the convenient workflow. docs.title: Trajectory increment
docs.text:
The trajectory guide covers direct fit(trajectory), default trajectory forecasts, the explicit tensor option, configurable resampling and portable checkpoints. Uniform time axes are the normal case; irregular axes are resampled automatically with linear, PCHIP or cubic interpolation. Explicit sampling intervals preserve the last observed time and never extrapolate. Future histories use the fitted interval.

The integration adds independent physical-time oracles, source/clock/schema validation, real TSDynamics simulation, failed-refit isolation, legacy checkpoint and optional-dependency tests. Its runnable guide is included in the installed-dynamics CI lanes on Python 3.12–3.14, so missing optional packages cannot silently skip integration verification. This was an intermediate delivery; the completion record below covers the remaining phase-two work.

The adapter, workflow and guide comprise 81 checks, verified from a clean installed wheel against the minimum supported TSDynamics 6.0.2, and with the locked 6.0.3 locally. Native MPS fitting, device-local tensor forecasts, portable metadata, bfloat16 output conversion and strict documentation builds are covered. docs.text:

docs.title: SQ-01: one-pass training of cascaded-readout DAGs
docs.text:
Baseline problem. The previous trainer used fitting hooks inside repeated whole-graph warmup/training passes. This produced correct downstream states, but repeated upstream work whenever a fitted readout feeds another reservoir. For a chain of K comparable reservoir/readout stages, propagation can cost O(K² × T), where T is the sequence length. Phase-one correctness remains covered by P1-03; this phase-four task removes the unnecessary computation while preserving it.

Required execution. Initialize training states once using the current fit reset contract. Traverse the graph in topological order, pausing at each readout to fit it before continuing into its downstream dependencies:

  1. Run reservoir₁ through its warmup prefix, then its training samples, carrying state continuously between the two portions. Retain the resulting features.
  2. Fit readout₁ using only the training features and their aligned targets. Apply the fitted readout to both the warmup and training features.
  3. Continue from those outputs into reservoir₂. Its warmup now uses the fitted upstream mapping; continue through its training portion without resetting between warmup and training. Fit readout₂ and proceed in the same way.
  4. For branches, reuse computed outputs across consumers. Execute a merge only when all its inputs are available, and release retained tensors after their last consumer. Each reservoir node processes its sequence once.

This is one batch-training traversal of the DAG: a readout waits until its incoming training features are available, solves once, then forwards the full prefix using its fitted weights. It must not restart at the graph input, run downstream reservoirs prematurely, or substitute target values for the fitted upstream readout's actual outputs. Reuse the existing execution plan, fitting interfaces and PyTorch tensor operations; no replacement graph framework is needed. Preserve target alignment, washout, preprocessing, final state and failed-fit isolation across supported graph structures.

Acceptance checks.

  • Compare fitted weights, downstream features, final states and forecasts with an independent manual layer-by-layer reference. Include nonzero warmup, deliberately wrong initial upstream weights, multiple recurrent fitting boundaries, branches, shared ancestors, merges and supported containers.
  • Instrument reservoir calls and processed samples. Each reservoir graph node must consume exactly its warmup plus training samples once, and each readout must fit once. These structural checks must catch whole-graph replay even if a small wall-clock benchmark happens to pass.
  • Preserve the ordinary single-readout fast path and existing numerical, device/dtype, state-noise and failure-cleanup contracts. Unsupported opaque composites must fail clearly rather than silently assume an execution order.
  • Benchmark depths 1, 2, 4 and 8 at fixed sequence length, widths, dtype, device and thread count. Report propagation and readout-solving time separately, along with peak memory and repeat variability. Propagation work should grow with graph size rather than quadratically with cascade depth; do not hide regression by weakening existing performance thresholds.

Scheduling. Included in phase four at the maintainer’s request. Implementation and independent verification are complete. Coordinate trainer and execution plan changes with artifact work; consult the maintainer before introducing major public API or memory-policy changes.

docs.title: Phase 5: speed, memory and comparisons
docs.text:
The first increment fixes benchmark preparation and evaluates the same classical models before and after phase four. The maintainer approved 0.3 as the main per-step normalized RMS error limit, with 0.5 also reported. Normalization uses only training data. Report each seed/origin separately, then its median and spread; do not construct a horizon from the median error curve.

The target is a typical 7–8 Lyapunov-time forecast, rather than one selected successful run. This is an experiment target, not a current capability guarantee. The phase-five design separates accuracy regression, held-out tuning and cross-library comparison; public metric defaults are not changed by the benchmark repairs.

docs.title: Known baseline performance limits
docs.text:
Running all nine existing non-GPU benchmark cases on this Apple Silicon Mac with Torch 2.10.0, float64 CPU tensors and four intra-op threads exposed two timing assumptions outside the current CI benchmark directories. The seven other cases passed. An isolated import of unchanged main (a24e7a1) reproduced both failures with the same environment and identical test/kernel sources; branch/main timings below are separate runs, not a controlled speedup comparison.

Existing assertion Completion branch Unchanged main Required by current test CSR versus dense recurrent multiplication, size 2,000 / density 5% Dense/CSR time ratio 0.35× 0.44× Greater than 1.2× Parallel advance with 64 versus eight patches Large/small time ratio 8.44× 7.57× Less than 5×

The sparse assertion remains open performance work in P5-03. The parallel ratio was not reproduced in the latest controlled checks, so it remains a historical observation rather than a current reproduced failure. A separate single-frame optimization improves forecast latency with exact predictions; the current measurements are recorded below. Sparse crossover and batching claims must be measured for the actual hardware, dtype and batch regime; sparse="auto" uses fixed size/density heuristics rather than calibration. Users can force sparse=False where the dense operator wins. Keep the current thresholds visible until the policy and measurements are reviewed; widening them alone would not improve performance.

docs.title: All-PyTorch closeout
docs.text:
The larger-network acceptance covers an encoder → fitted RC → trainable head, including independent gradient equations, finite differences, repeated optimizer updates, carried/explicit state, ordinary state-dictionary reload, CPU mixed precision and full-graph AOT eager forward/backward capture. CPU and native MPS hot-path checks reject host scalar reads and cross-device tensors. CUDA cases remain skipped on this host; these checks do not establish GPU throughput. The implementation fixes CPU CSR autocast precision, compiled carried-state detachment and an older-Python/Torch typing-union capture failure. Execution remains in PyTorch.

The parallel CPU forecast specialization preserves the same recurrent arithmetic and falls back for hooks and custom behavior. Its public raw-data report binds frozen sources and all prediction/state hashes. A custom-readout multiple-inheritance regression protects the fallback as well. Two fresh-process ABBA blocks measure 2–9% lower forecast elapsed time in the tested workloads. The unchanged fit control varies from 1.5% faster to 7.6% slower, so the small forecast gains retain that measurement caveat.

The independent-trajectory study freezes six existing recipes, then runs 90 fits and 270 forecasts on ten new trajectories with no tuning. Primary OTT medians reach the ten-Lyapunov-time scoring limit on both systems. Friendly vanilla medians are 5.995 LT on Lorenz and 6.326 LT on Rössler at 0.3, below the 7–8 target. Two secondary state-only vanilla recipes reach the median test limit, but do not replace the primary results. Repeating all 90 fits and 270 forecasts on clean eb70bf11 gives identical fitted tensors, complete predictions, states and scores. See the current closeout results. An additional corrected-runtime replay loads all 90 original fitted checkpoints and reproduces all 270 forecasts, states, scores and error traces exactly, without another fit or readout solve.

The runnable experiment now writes a resolved manifest and exact replay data. Verification reloads saved DAGs and recomputes predictions/scores without reintegration, tuning or fitting; it does not remeasure the original timings. docs.title: First-increment accuracy evidence
docs.text:
These results precede the independent initialization-stream correction. They describe the original seeded models; newly built models require fresh checks. The continuation measurements report the new seed bank, including the unresolved vanilla Rössler shortfall.

See the historical protocol and results for fixed-training-scale scores at thresholds 0.3 and 0.5. Primary tuned medians are 9.11 / ≥10.02 Lyapunov times for vanilla/OTT Lorenz and 7.58 / ≥10.00 for vanilla/OTT Rössler. Each uses five reserved seeds and three unseen test starting points. The supplementary vanilla Rössler median is 6.33 and its pooled ten-seed median 6.76; robust 7–8 performance is therefore still an open goal for that recipe. Censored values are lower bounds. Neither these accuracy checks nor the untuned adapter smoke establishes a cross-library speed ranking.

docs.title: Continuation decisions and verification
docs.text:
The maintainer approved compressed weights as the only recurrent storage for sparse=True, an explicitly selected low-memory solver, and native PyTorch hooks during forecasting. Dense models and automatic solver choices retain their established behavior. See memory and sparse models, LSMR and migration notes.

The comparison protocol uses the common vanilla model family first, equal 600-second tuning budgets, three validation seeds/origins, and reserved final seeds 301–305. All six winners freeze before test access. Reused trajectories are held out from the new studies, but are historically known; one trajectory per system does not establish generalization across independently generated runs. Incomplete or late candidates cannot win, and final build/fit failures cannot be disguised as short but valid forecasts.

The full run completed on 1dc8cfb: 2,850 eligible complete configurations, six excluded deadline attempts, and 90 complete final forecasts, with all winners frozen first. All three Lorenz medians reach ≥10.016 Lyapunov times; Rössler medians are 9.628 / 9.639 / 9.701 for ResDAG, ReservoirPy and ReservoirComputing.jl. All selected models have 1,000 units. ResDAG is slower in these selected CPU workflows, so this is comparable accuracy without a speed-superiority claim. The measurement report retains full spread, both thresholds, timings, solver safeguards and complete downloadable records. Independent trajectories and broader profiling remain open.

Final implementation/test acceptance on 1dc8cfb: 6,267 local tests pass at 93.83% coverage; 334 installed-wheel checks pass with two unavailable CUDA skips. All 205 Python modules and the typing marker match source, wheel, sdist and installed package. All eight locked/latest full hosted lanes pass 6,018 tests each at 91.59–91.66% coverage. Both strict docs builds, six installed-TSDynamics lanes, configured CPU gates and the 76 Python / 18 real Julia benchmark contracts pass. See the full measurement record.

The new RNG fix separates ESN, gated and LIF default roles, preserves explicit initializer overrides, and documents changed newly seeded weights. Four fresh 24-attempt studies completed 70 configurations and recorded 26 failures, with no pruning. Each complete configuration received three seeds × three validation starts; all four winners froze before reserved seeds 401–405. Median horizons over 15 test forecasts are ≥10.016 for both Lorenz families, 4.203 for vanilla Rössler and ≥10.001 for OTT Rössler at the 0.3 limit. Vanilla Rössler therefore remains below the target. Full spread, controls, censoring, per-seed summaries and the 0.5 results are recorded separately. No retuning followed those tests.

Stored-model checks remain separate: 12 forecasts from four published 4.1.0 checkpoints and their fitted tensors are byte-identical on the corrected runtime. Before the stream change, source 4439e29 also preserved all 150 frozen tuned/control forecasts and all 50 initial/fitted model fingerprints exactly. That historical replay does not establish equal newly seeded weights after the intentional stream correction.

Two fresh-process ABBA runs use the same stored baseline weights in both revisions, 400 units, 1,501 training samples and 256 forecast steps. All forecast digests match. Pooled sparse-cycle fitting improves 1.11–1.13×, forecasting 1.14×, and retained tensor storage falls 1,321,042 → 37,842 bytes. Sparse random storage falls 1,351,978 → 58,466 bytes. One-thread dense forecasts are roughly 3–5% slower in this workload; four-thread medians are about 1% faster. Both runs, including the initially slower measurement, are retained. These are bounded CPU/Torch-thread observations, not native one-thread or process peak-RSS claims. Existing CPU gates pass unchanged; broader profiling remains open.

The CPU follow-up distinguishes adopted AutoReadout residual reuse and analytic CSR correctness fixes from rejected slicing experiments. The 18f78c83/dc695a6 matrices retain 728 timed executions of each operation, plus 104 discarded warmups of each operation. All case-local fitted/prediction/state hashes match, but a sharp change in execution conditions leaves the whole-workflow speed effect inconclusive. The separate within-process loop diagnostic also fails to establish a consistent benefit. The original sequence-loop and driver slicing are retained; these candidate measurements do not establish final adopted-runtime throughput.

The merged first increment's post-merge release run passed: all four Python 3.11–3.14 full suites passed 5,618 tests per lane at 91.44–91.50% coverage. The published 4.1.0 wheel's 200 runtime files match its release tag, and installed artifact/workflow checks passed 118 tests, with two unavailable-CUDA cases skipped. New continuation verification will be recorded separately; those release counts do not cover the unmerged implementation.

docs.title: Persistence and dependency audit
docs.text: This record covers the 24 October 2026 hygiene sweep. It distinguishes repaired library behavior from upstream dependency advisories; it is not a claim that arbitrary model files or Python plugins can be safely executed.

docs.title: Model and data files
docs.text:
Model.save and rd.load use a portable DAG description and tensor state. Installed custom classes are reconstructed through registered codecs. Loading runs those installed constructors: register code you trust. Notebook bundles are a separate, explicit trusted=True format. The save/load guide explains both forms.

Low-level ESNModel, parallel and coupled model weight checkpoints now use torch.load(weights_only=True), with no automatic unsafe fallback. Full Python model files require load_full(..., trusted=True) before any file read. This is an intentional API change. Unsupported objects, cyclic metadata and hidden Python attributes are rejected before ordinary saves. Serialization writes a temporary file beside the destination, flushes it and replaces the destination only on success; a failed write preserves the previous model.

These checks have malicious-payload, tensor-attribute, nested-metadata, fresh-process reload and failed-write regression tests. NumPy dataset loading retains allow_pickle=False. A restricted loader still does not impose a memory or CPU quota on hostile files; run externally supplied models and data with appropriate resource isolation.

docs.title: Dependency disposition
docs.text:
The sweep ran pip-audit against the installed full development environment, updated the affected non-numerical dependencies in uv.lock, and reran the audit. The remaining report contains two advisories for the locked Torch 2.10.0, with no suppression. Torch, NumPy, SciPy and TSDynamics versions are retained for reproducible scientific baselines. Ordinary pip installations can resolve newer versions; a separate CI matrix tests current compatible packages.

Material for MkDocs now requires 9.7.7 or newer. Its enabled search-suggestion feature was affected by a DOM XSS flaw; the upstream patch fixes it. See the upstream changelog and maintainer advisory. Black, pytest and Markdown extension minima are also raised to patched releases. The lock refresh includes certificate, HTTP, image, highlighting, template, file-lock and filesystem dependencies. Full tests and rendered documentation must pass with these actual versions before acceptance.

Remaining advisory Affected operation and decision CVE-2026-4538 / PYSEC-2026-139 The upstream report concerns Python unpickling through torch.export.load on .pt2 archives; no fixed version is listed by the audit. ResDAG does not call this loader or offer .pt2 loading. Its portable/raw checkpoints use the restricted Torch path described above. Upstream report. CVE-2025-3000 / PYSEC-2025-194 The report concerns scripting a Python class with torch.jit.script; the advisory lists 2.13.0 as fixed. ResDAG does not call that compiler on supplied classes. Keep the 2.10 baseline for comparisons, and use a current patched Torch release for applications that script custom Python classes. Upstream issue, advisory.

The retained baseline is not a clean dependency scan. New upstream fixes need review when the lock changes. PyTorch's security policy explains its trust boundary for models, TorchScript and local Python execution. Restricted checkpoint loading is available at the library's minimum Torch 2.10.0, which also contains the upstream restricted-unpickler repair described in GHSA-63cw-57p8-fm3p.

docs.title: Single-pass training benchmark
docs.text:
At a fixed CPU workload, fitting eight cascaded reservoir/readout stages took 236.195 ms with the staged trainer and 30.915 ms with the single-pass trainer. The median paired speedup was 7.64×. A single stage took essentially the same time. Fitted coefficients and final recurrent states were bit-identical in every comparison.

These are measurements from one Apple Silicon machine. The reproduction script and raw measurements record the workload, every timed repeat, structural counts and process memory. They introduce no performance thresholds.

docs.title: Workload and method
docs.text:
The baseline is the independently imported trainer from Git revision c0c61d09a22759f2d5c3f24c78d53803cd658778. Both trainers use the same reservoir and readout implementations. Each pair starts from fresh copies of identical model weights and uses the same data and targets.

  • CPU, float64, batch size 2, reservoir width 64, input/output width 4.
  • Warmup length 100 and supervised training length 500 at depths 1, 2, 4 and 8.
  • Reservoir spectral radius 0.7, leak rate 0.8, zero reservoir noise; ridge regularization 0.001.
  • macOS 27.0.1 on Apple Silicon, Python 3.14.8, PyTorch 2.10.0.
  • One intra-op thread and one inter-op thread.
  • Two discarded warmup pairs followed by seven measured pairs. Baseline/current execution order alternates. Model copying and data preparation are excluded from fit timing; lightweight instrumentation is included.

docs.title: Fit time
docs.text:
Depth Staged median ms (min–max) Single-pass median ms (min–max) Median paired speedup (min–max) 1 4.018 (3.968–4.229) 4.009 (3.970–4.119) 0.990× (0.976–1.059) 2 15.108 (14.960–15.461) 7.881 (7.687–8.009) 1.943× (1.868–1.968) 4 60.081 (59.363–60.445) 15.732 (15.419–16.554) 3.841× (3.626–3.877) 8 236.195 (235.554–236.796) 30.915 (30.402–31.131) 7.641× (7.566–7.769)

The depth-one paired ratio differs from 1 by about 1%, within the observed variation. Paired speedups are computed per repeat, so their median can differ from the ratio of the two separate time medians.

At depth eight, the component medians were:

Component Staged ms Single-pass ms Reservoir propagation 231.699 28.827 Readout fitting 1.879 1.719 Other fit overhead 2.630 0.412 Complete fit 236.195 30.915

Propagation sums reservoir forward durations. Readout fitting includes feature validation, the algebraic solve and coefficient installation. Other overhead is the per-repeat residual. Component medians need not sum to the total median.

docs.title: Computation counts
docs.text:
Each readout fits once in both implementations. The difference is repeated propagation: staged fitting reruns the whole graph after every recurrent readout dependency. Single-pass fitting propagates each reservoir through the complete warmup and training prefix once.

Depth Reservoir calls: staged → single-pass Processed batch samples: staged → single-pass 1 2 → 1 1,200 → 1,200 2 8 → 2 4,800 → 2,400 4 32 → 4 19,200 → 4,800 8 128 → 8 76,800 → 9,600

A processed batch sample is one trajectory at one timestep. At depth eight, the new traversal performs eight times less recurrent sample work. Shared branches reuse computed features, and intermediate values are released after their last consumer.

docs.title: Process memory
docs.text:
Memory was measured in a fresh process for each depth/mode, using the process high-water mark from resource.getrusage. The figures include imports, model construction, data and allocator state. Each cell contains one fit, and small process-to-process differences are visible before fitting.

Depth Staged absolute peak MiB Single-pass absolute peak MiB 1 226.516 227.234 2 225.609 227.469 4 228.531 226.031 8 230.734 227.641

At depth eight, the pre-fit high-water marks were 223.828 and 223.813 MiB, respectively. The measured increases were 6.906 and 3.828 MiB. These are process measurements for this workload; allocator behavior and different graph shapes can change the result.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv run python benchmarks/single_pass_training.py \
  --baseline-ref c0c61d0 --rss \
  --output benchmarks/results/single-pass-training-rerun.json

Omit --rss to collect timing and parity checks alone. --baseline-ref reads the historical trainer with git show into a temporary import; the working checkout stays in place. Use --help for repeat and depth controls.

The recorded working-trainer SHA-256 before and after the measured run is bb7e2ca68416f3ed5bca3817b74d102930beb19442e8dac6ec097dfb06bb3d7d. Those matching hashes establish that the working source stayed unchanged during measurement. The baseline has the separate Git identity recorded above.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Public package exports are declared in __all__ and shown by dir(). The reference covers normal model use and supported extension contracts, including custom cells, initializers, readouts and artifact codecs. Execution planners and fit-preparation helpers with a leading underscore are private. Torch's required checkpoint/representation hooks remain operational but are omitted from ordinary method listings. For prose-first treatments of the same components, start from Build and Work.

docs.title: Model artifacts
docs.text: Reference

docs.title: Model artifacts
docs.text:
Start with save, load and diagrams. The common Model.save / ESN.save methods select complete checkpoints or image formats by suffix. save_model also accepts supported raw graph families.

Portable artifacts use registered declarative configuration and tensor state. Loading defaults to Torch's restricted loader (weights_only=True) and does not import Python paths selected by the file. register_component and custom_objects supply application-trusted ComponentCodec constructors; register custom component types explicitly before portable loading.

An optional Python bundle requires trusted=True at both save and load. It can execute Python when loaded and needs compatible Python/package versions. Restricted loading reduces code-execution exposure but does not provide a resource sandbox for malformed or oversized files.

include_state=True retains recurrent memory. Setting it to False resets ordinary recurrent memory on reload while retaining fitted preprocessing and observed forecast history. Artifacts do not retain an autonomous forecast cursor, optimizer or autograd graph. return_metadata=True returns (model, metadata) from load; ordinary state_dict files still require a matching model and load_state_dict.

docs.title: artifacts
docs.text:
Complete model artifacts using standard Torch serialization.

Portable artifacts reconstruct registered components without loading embedded Python code. trusted=True explicitly enables an optional cloudpickle bundle. Ordinary state_dict remains the standard state-only PyTorch interface.

docs.title: ComponentCodec dataclass
docs.text:
ComponentCodec(
    name: str,
    cls: type,
    encode: Callable[[Any], Mapping[str, Any]],
    decode: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], Any],
    version: int = 1,
)

A versioned component constructor installed by the application.

encode(component) returns configuration, not its learned tensor state. decode(config) constructs that component. Nested registered modules and ordinary tensor/primitive configuration values are encoded automatically. Registering a codec trusts its Python functions; a model file cannot install or import a codec by itself.

docs.text:
Bases: ValueError

An artifact cannot be represented or reconstructed as requested.

docs.title: load
docs.text:
load(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    trusted: bool = False,
    map_location: Any = "cpu",
    custom_objects: Mapping[str, ComponentCodec] | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False
) -> Any

Reconstruct a saved model without knowing its original DAG.

The default uses Torch's restricted tensor/primitive loader and never imports artifact-selected Python paths. trusted=True permits Python unpickling; use it only for a file whose producer and contents you trust. Restricted loading reduces code execution exposure but does not prevent malformed-file memory/resource exhaustion. Device remapping follows standard torch.load.

Source code in src/resdag/artifacts/_api.py 
def load(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    trusted: bool = False,
    map_location: Any = "cpu",
    custom_objects: Mapping[str, ComponentCodec] | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """Reconstruct a saved model without knowing its original DAG.

    The default uses Torch's restricted tensor/primitive loader and never imports
    artifact-selected Python paths. `trusted=True` permits Python unpickling;
    use it only for a file whose producer and contents you trust. Restricted
    loading reduces code execution exposure but does not prevent malformed-file
    memory/resource exhaustion. Device remapping follows standard `torch.load`.
    """
    if type(trusted) is not bool:
        raise TypeError("trusted must be a bool")
    _initialize()
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode(False):
            payload = torch.load(path, map_location=map_location, weights_only=True)
    except pickle.UnpicklingError as error:
        raise ArtifactError(
            "Restricted loading rejected Python objects. For a trusted Python bundle only, explicitly pass trusted=True; never enable this for an unknown file."
        ) from error
    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or payload.get("format") != _FORMAT:
        raise ArtifactError(
            "This is not a complete ResDAG artifact; state_dict files require a matching model and load_state_dict"
        )
    if type(payload.get("version")) is not int or payload["version"] != _VERSION:
        raise ArtifactError(
            f"Unsupported ResDAG artifact version {payload.get('version')!r}; this installation supports version {_VERSION}"
        )
    if payload.get("trusted") and not trusted:
        raise ArtifactError(
            "This artifact contains executable Python; explicitly pass trusted=True only if its producer is trusted"
        )
    with torch.inference_mode(False), torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        if payload.get("trusted"):
            model = _trusted_decode(payload["python"], payload["tensors"], payload["generators"])
            if not isinstance(model, nn.Module):
                raise ArtifactError("Trusted artifact root is not a Torch module")
            for name, module in model.named_modules():
                _restore_live(module, payload["live"].get(name, {}))
        else:
            decoder = _Decoder(payload["components"], custom_objects)
            model = decoder.decode(payload["root"])
            if not isinstance(model, nn.Module):
                raise ArtifactError("Artifact root is not a Torch module")
            # Functional construction runs trace placeholders. Restore final
            # persistent and live state again after all parent graphs are built.
            for key, module in decoder.objects.items():
                if isinstance(module, nn.Module):
                    module.load_state_dict(
                        decoder.records[key]["state_dict"], strict=True, assign=True
                    )
                    _restore_live(module, decoder.records[key]["live"])
        _restore_behavior(model, payload["behavior"])
    meta = payload["metadata"]
    _plain(meta)
    return (model, meta) if return_metadata else model

docs.title: save_model
docs.text:
save_model(
    model: Module,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    trusted: bool = False,
    include_state: bool = True,
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
) -> Path

Save a complete model, preserving recurrent memory by default.

Portable files contain declarative registered configuration and tensor state. trusted=True uses the optional cloudpickle package to include Python components such as notebook-local classes and lambdas. Loading those files requires explicit trust and compatible Python/package versions.

include_state=False resets ordinary recurrent memory on reload. Fitted preprocessing and the observed history used by forecast are retained. Neither option saves an autonomous forecast cursor, optimizer or autograd graph.

Source code in src/resdag/artifacts/_api.py 
def save_model(
    model: nn.Module,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    trusted: bool = False,
    include_state: bool = True,
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Save a complete model, preserving recurrent memory by default.

    Portable files contain declarative registered configuration and tensor state.
    `trusted=True` uses the optional cloudpickle package to include Python
    components such as notebook-local classes and lambdas. Loading those files
    requires explicit trust and compatible Python/package versions.

    `include_state=False` resets ordinary recurrent memory on reload. Fitted
    preprocessing and the observed history used by `forecast` are retained.
    Neither option saves an autonomous forecast cursor, optimizer or autograd graph.
    """
    if not isinstance(model, nn.Module):
        raise TypeError("model must be a torch.nn.Module")
    if type(trusted) is not bool or type(include_state) is not bool:
        raise TypeError("trusted and include_state must be bool values")
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() not in (".pt", ".pth"):
        raise ArtifactError(
            "Complete model artifacts use .pt or .pth; diagram formats are .svg/.png/.pdf/.dot"
        )
    meta = dict(metadata or {})
    _plain(meta)
    _initialize()
    from resdag.core._execution import validate_fitting_forward
    from resdag.core.model import ESNModel

    for module in model.modules():
        if isinstance(module, ESNModel):
            try:
                validate_fitting_forward(module)
            except ValueError as error:
                raise ArtifactError(
                    "Saving a customized outer ESNModel.forward is unsupported; put the behavior inside a declared graph module."
                ) from error
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "format": _FORMAT,
        "version": _VERSION,
        "producer": {
            "resdag": version("resdag"),
            "torch": str(torch.__version__),
            "python": platform.python_version(),
        },
        "metadata": meta,
        "behavior": _behavior(model),
        "trusted": trusted,
    }
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        if trusted:
            cloudpickle = _cloudpickle()
            live = {
                name: _live_state(module, include_state) for name, module in model.named_modules()
            }
            code, tensors, generators = _trusted_encode(model, cloudpickle, include_state)
            payload.update(python=code, tensors=tensors, generators=generators, live=live)
        else:
            encoder = _Encoder(include_state)
            payload.update(root=encoder.encode(model), components=encoder.records)
        _atomic_save(payload, path)
    return path

docs.title: register_component
docs.text:
register_component(
    name: str,
    cls: type,
    *,
    encode: Callable[[Any], Mapping[str, Any]],
    decode: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], Any],
    version: int = 1
) -> type

Register an exact custom type for portable save/load.

Example:

rd.register_component(
    "my-project.Scale", Scale,
    encode=lambda layer: {"factor": layer.factor},
    decode=lambda config: Scale(**config),
)

Import the registration in a new process before loading. Subclasses need their own registration, so their custom behavior cannot disappear silently. Use a new version when the component's configuration contract changes.

Source code in src/resdag/artifacts/_registry.py 
def register_component(
    name: str,
    cls: type,
    *,
    encode: Callable[[Any], Mapping[str, Any]],
    decode: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], Any],
    version: int = 1,
) -> type:
    """Register an exact custom type for portable save/load.

    Example:

    ```text
    rd.register_component(
        "my-project.Scale", Scale,
        encode=lambda layer: {"factor": layer.factor},
        decode=lambda config: Scale(**config),
    )
    ```

    Import the registration in a new process before loading. Subclasses need
    their own registration, so their custom behavior cannot disappear silently.
    Use a new version when the component's configuration contract changes.
    """
    from ._api import _initialize

    _initialize()
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or name.startswith("resdag."):
        raise ValueError("Custom component name must be nonempty and not start with 'resdag.'")
    return _register(ComponentCodec(name, cls, encode, decode, version))

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Reference

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
Model adds named inputs/outputs, fitted scaling and fit/forecast operations around a functional graph. Start with the common model guide. ESNModel remains the underlying symbolic graph with lower-level training and state interfaces. For timestamped runs, see TSDynamics trajectories. Several ports use named trajectories; per-port unit conversions use custom preprocessing.

Use Feedback(output="prediction", input="state", delay=1) to declare a named recurrent connection. Prediction leads and feedback delays have separate meanings; see feedback and clocks.

forward_stateless returns predictions and a ReservoirStates mapping without changing stored recurrent state. Reuse the returned mapping for differentiable chunks. Raw graph as_module() returns a ReservoirModelModule that shares the complete graph and its parameters; ReservoirFeatureExtractor selects reservoir features instead. These adapters serve different pipeline needs.

Standard inherited PyTorch operations, including parameters, state_dict, load_state_dict, train, eval and to, remain available. Their inherited reference entries and checkpoint protocol hooks are omitted here.

docs.title: Core Model
docs.text:
This module provides the main model class and input helpers for building ESN architectures using the pytorch_symbolic library.

CLASS DESCRIPTION Model

Named functional graph with training-only scaling and a PyTorch lifecycle.

ESNModel

Extended SymbolicModel with ESN-specific methods for forecasting and reservoir state management.

ReservoirFeatureExtractor

nn.Sequential-friendly adapter that packages reservoir layers as a drop-in feature extractor for ordinary torch.nn pipelines.

Input

Alias for pytorch_symbolic.Input for defining model inputs.

FUNCTION DESCRIPTION reservoir_input

Convenience constructor for a per-feature symbolic input tensor with a placeholder time dimension. Preferred over hand-crafting ps.Input((T, F)) since the time dimension is purely a tracing hint inside reservoir models.

Examples:

Building a simple ESN:

>>> from resdag.core import ESNModel, reservoir_input
>>> from resdag.layers import ESNLayer
>>> from resdag.layers.readouts import CGReadoutLayer
>>>
>>> inp = reservoir_input(3)             # equivalent to ps.Input((1, 3))
>>> reservoir = ESNLayer(200, feedback_size=3)(inp)
>>> readout = CGReadoutLayer(200, 3)(reservoir)
>>> model = ESNModel(inp, readout)

Multi-input model:

>>> feedback = reservoir_input(3)
>>> driver = reservoir_input(5)
>>> reservoir = ESNLayer(200, feedback_size=3, input_size=5)(feedback, driver)
>>> readout = CGReadoutLayer(200, 3)(reservoir)
>>> model = ESNModel([feedback, driver], readout)
See Also

resdag.models : Premade ESN architectures. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting readouts.
