Number of delay taps (including the current input). k=1 means only the current input is used (no delay buffer).

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 2

s

Spacing between delay taps, in timesteps.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1

p

Polynomial degree for nonlinear feature construction. See cumulative for the two supported degree conventions.

Exact-degree convention (cumulative=False, the default): the nonlinear block contains all unique monomials of exactly degree p from the D = input_dim * k linear features — there are C(D + p - 1, p) of them. Lower-order cross terms (degrees 2, ..., p-1) are not included. For example, NGCell(p=3, include_linear=True) emits constant + linear + cubic with no quadratic terms. This is the historical resdag behaviour and matches Gauthier et al. (arXiv:2106.07688v2), whose Lorenz63 (Eq. 9) and double-scroll (Eq. 10) bases each use a single polynomial degree.

Cumulative-degree convention (cumulative=True): the nonlinear block contains every monomial of degree 2, ..., p (or 1, ..., p when include_linear=False), i.e. the full polynomial basis up to degree p. Many NVAR / NG-RC implementations (and configs ported from them) expect this "degree up to p" basis.

Note.

When p == 1 the degree-1 monomials are the linear features O_lin. To avoid emitting two identical blocks (which makes the readout design matrix rank-deficient), the nonlinear block is omitted whenever p == 1 and include_linear is True. With p == 1 and include_linear=False the degree-1 monomials are kept, since they are then the only delay-embedded features. More generally, whenever include_linear is True the degree-1 monomials are dropped from the nonlinear block (in both conventions), since they would duplicate O_lin; the cumulative basis therefore spans degrees 2, ..., p in that case.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 2

cumulative

Degree convention for the nonlinear block (see p). False keeps only exact-degree-p monomials (default, unchanged behaviour); True includes all monomials of every degree up to p (the cumulative / "degree up to p" basis).

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

include_constant

Whether to prepend a constant 1.0 feature to the output vector. Set True for Lorenz63 forecasting (Eq. 9).

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

include_linear

Whether to include the linear delay-embedded features O_lin in the output. Set True for both Lorenz63 and double-scroll (Eq. 9, 10).

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION feature_dim

Total dimension of the output feature vector O_total:

D = input_dim * k
# Degrees emitted in the nonlinear block.  Degree 1 is excluded
# whenever include_linear is True (those monomials == O_lin):
d_lo = 2 if include_linear else 1
degrees = range(d_lo, p + 1) if cumulative else [p]
degrees = [g for g in degrees if not (g == 1 and include_linear)]
n_nonlin = sum(C(D + g - 1, g) for g in degrees)
feature_dim = (
    int(include_constant)
    + int(include_linear) * D
    + n_nonlin
)

In the default exact-degree mode (cumulative=False) this reduces to int(include_constant) + int(include_linear) * D + C(D + p - 1, p), with the C(...) term dropped only in the p == 1 / include_linear=True duplicate-column case.

TYPE: int

state_size

Number of rows in the delay buffer: (k - 1) * s. When k=1 this is 0 and the buffer is empty.

TYPE: int

monomial_indices

Long tensor of shape (n_monomials, p) containing the column indices into O_lin for each monomial. Registered as a buffer. Each row lists the O_lin columns multiplied together to form one monomial. In exact-degree mode every row has p distinct index slots; in cumulative mode lower-degree monomials are right-padded with -1 sentinels (gathered from a prepended 1.0 column at runtime) so all rows share the same width p.

TYPE: Tensor

delay_indices

Long tensor of shape (k-1,) containing the row indices into the delay buffer for extracting the delay taps. Registered as a buffer.

TYPE: Tensor

Examples:

Basic usage (k=2, s=1, p=2):

>>> cell = NGCell(input_dim=3)
>>> x = torch.randn(4, 3)                          # (batch=4, d=3)
>>> state = cell.init_state(4, x.device, x.dtype)  # (4, 1, 3)
>>> features, new_state = cell([x], state)
>>> features.shape
torch.Size([4, 28])
>>> new_state.shape
torch.Size([4, 1, 3])

No-delay mode (k=1):

>>> cell = NGCell(input_dim=3, k=1)
>>> state = cell.init_state(1, 'cpu', torch.float32)
>>> features, new_state = cell([torch.randn(1, 3)], state)
>>> features.shape
torch.Size([1, 10])

def __init__(
    self,
    input_dim: int,
    k: int = 2,
    s: int = 1,
    p: int = 2,
    cumulative: bool = False,
    include_constant: bool = True,
    include_linear: bool = True,
) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    # NG-RC has no floating-point weights. An empty buffer records .to()
    # device/dtype choices for reset_state(batch_size=...) and state restore.
    self.register_buffer("_device_dtype_anchor", torch.empty(0), persistent=False)

    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"k must be >= 1, got {k}")
    if s < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"s must be >= 1, got {s}")
    if p < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"p must be >= 1, got {p}")

    self.input_dim = input_dim
    self.k = k
    self.s = s
    self.p = p
    self.cumulative = cumulative
    self.include_constant = include_constant
    self.include_linear = include_linear

    # D = total linear feature dimension
    linear_feature_dim = input_dim * k

    # Precompute delay-tap row indices into the buffer (shape: (k-1,)).
    # For j = 1, ..., k-1:  X_{i - j*s} lives at row (k-1-j)*s of the
    # buffer (which holds inputs chronologically oldest-first).
    if k > 1:
        delay_idx = torch.tensor([(k - 1 - j) * s for j in range(1, k)], dtype=torch.long)
    else:
        delay_idx = torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.long)
    self.register_buffer("delay_indices", delay_idx)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decide which monomial degrees the nonlinear block emits.
    #
    # Exact-degree mode (cumulative=False): only degree p.
    # Cumulative mode (cumulative=True):    every degree 1..p.
    #
    # When include_linear is True the degree-1 monomials are exactly the
    # columns of O_lin, so emitting them again would duplicate every linear
    # column and make the readout design matrix rank-deficient.  Drop
    # degree 1 from the nonlinear block in that case (this generalises the
    # historical p==1 special case to both conventions).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    degrees = range(1, p + 1) if cumulative else range(p, p + 1)
    emit_degrees = [g for g in degrees if not (g == 1 and include_linear)]

    # Build the monomial index rows.  Exact-degree mode keeps the historical
    # tight (n_monomials, p) layout with no padding.  Cumulative mode mixes
    # degrees, so every row is right-padded to width p with the -1 sentinel,
    # which is gathered from a prepended 1.0 column (the multiplicative
    # identity) at runtime — keeping a single vectorised gather/prod.
    raw_indices: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for g in emit_degrees:
        raw_indices.extend(
            itertools.combinations_with_replacement(range(linear_feature_dim), g)
        )

    self._pad_with_ones: bool = cumulative and len(emit_degrees) > 1
    if self._pad_with_ones:
        # Right-pad short monomials with the -1 ones-sentinel to width p.
        padded = [list(idx) + [-1] * (p - len(idx)) for idx in raw_indices]
        monomial_idx = (
            torch.tensor(padded, dtype=torch.long)
            if padded
            else torch.zeros(0, p, dtype=torch.long)
        )
    else:
        # Tight layout: every monomial already has exactly ``width`` factors.
        width = emit_degrees[0] if emit_degrees else p
        monomial_idx = (
            torch.tensor([list(idx) for idx in raw_indices], dtype=torch.long)
            if raw_indices
            else torch.zeros(0, width, dtype=torch.long)
        )
    self.register_buffer("monomial_indices", monomial_idx)

    n_monomials = len(raw_indices)

    # The nonlinear block is omitted entirely only when no degrees survive
    # the degree-1 filter (i.e. p == 1 and include_linear is True).
    self._emit_nonlinear: bool = len(emit_degrees) > 0

    # Total output dimension
    self._feature_dim: int = (
        int(include_constant)
        + int(include_linear) * linear_feature_dim
        + int(self._emit_nonlinear) * n_monomials
    )

    if self._feature_dim > 10_000:
        warnings.warn(
            f"NGCell: feature_dim={self._feature_dim} exceeds 10,000. "
            f"Consider reducing k, p, or input_dim to avoid combinatorial explosion. "
            f"(linear_feature_dim={linear_feature_dim}, n_monomials={n_monomials})",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

def forward(
    self,
    inputs: list[torch.Tensor],
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute the NG-RC feature vector for a single timestep.

    Parameters
    ----------
    inputs : list[torch.Tensor]
        Per-timestep input slices.  `inputs[0]` is the current input
        of shape `(batch, input_dim)`.  NG-RC has no driving inputs, so
        only `inputs[0]` is consumed (the wrapping
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.ngrc.NGReservoirLayer` rejects driving
        inputs before they reach the cell).
    state : torch.Tensor
        Delay buffer of shape `(batch, state_size, input_dim)`.

    Returns
    -------
    features : torch.Tensor
        Output feature vector `O_total` of shape
        `(batch, feature_dim)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor
        Updated delay buffer of shape `(batch, state_size, input_dim)`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `inputs[0]`'s trailing (feature) dimension does not equal
        `input_dim`.
    """
    x = inputs[0]
    self._check_input_dim(x)
    batch = x.shape[0]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Build O_lin (linear delay-embedded features, Eq. 5)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if self.k > 1:
        # Extract (k-1) delay taps from the buffer *before* update.
        # delay_indices selects rows so that taps[:,0,:] = X_{i-s},
        # taps[:,1,:] = X_{i-2s}, ..., taps[:,k-2,:] = X_{i-(k-1)s}.
        delay_indices = cast(torch.Tensor, self.delay_indices)
        taps = state[:, delay_indices, :]  # (batch, k-1, input_dim)
        # O_lin = [X_i || X_{i-s} || ... || X_{i-(k-1)s}]
        o_lin = torch.cat([x.unsqueeze(1), taps], dim=1).reshape(batch, self.k * self.input_dim)
    else:
        # k=1: no delay taps, just current input
        o_lin = x  # (batch, input_dim)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Update delay buffer (FIFO: drop oldest row, append current x)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if self.state_size > 0:
        # Keep the last state_size rows after appending x.
        new_state = torch.cat([state, x.unsqueeze(1)], dim=1)[:, -self.state_size :, :]
    else:
        new_state = state  # empty tensor, no change

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Nonlinear features (Eq. 6): polynomial monomials from O_lin.
    #
    # Exact-degree mode emits only degree-p monomials; cumulative mode emits
    # every degree up to p.  The gather/product is delegated to
    # :meth:`_build_nonlinear`, which handles the padded cumulative layout.
    # The block is omitted only when p == 1 and include_linear is True
    # (the degree-1 monomials are then exactly the columns of O_lin).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Assemble O_total = [c] ⊕ O_lin ⊕ O_nonlin (Eq. 9 / Eq. 10)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    parts: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    if self.include_constant:
        parts.append(torch.ones(batch, 1, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype))
    if self.include_linear:
        parts.append(o_lin)
    if self._emit_nonlinear:
        parts.append(self._build_nonlinear(o_lin))  # (batch, n_monomials)

    o_total = torch.cat(parts, dim=-1)  # (batch, feature_dim)

    return o_total, new_state

Compute NG-RC features for a whole sequence in a single vectorized pass.

This is the batch-forward fast path used by resdag.layers.reservoirs.ngrc.NGReservoirLayer.forward. It is numerically identical to scanning forward step-by-step (0.0 max-abs-diff, including the warmup region), but contains no per-timestep Python loop: the delay-embedded linear features are built from shifted, front-zero-padded slices of the input, every monomial is gathered over the full (batch, timesteps, *) tensor at once, and the constant-ones block is allocated a single time.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION x

Input sequence of shape (batch, timesteps, input_dim).

TYPE: Tensor

state

Incoming delay buffer of shape (batch, state_size, input_dim), chronologically oldest-first. This holds the (k-1)*s inputs immediately preceding x[:, 0] and supplies the delay taps for the first timesteps (zeros for a cold start).

RETURNS DESCRIPTION features

Output features O_total of shape (batch, timesteps, feature_dim).

TYPE: Tensor

new_state

Updated delay buffer of shape (batch, state_size, input_dim), holding the last state_size inputs of x (or, when the sequence is shorter than the buffer, carried-over history), so a subsequent streaming forward continues seamlessly.

def forward_sequence(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute NG-RC features for a whole sequence in a single vectorized pass.

    This is the batch-forward fast path used by
    `resdag.layers.reservoirs.ngrc.NGReservoirLayer.forward`.  It is
    numerically identical to scanning `forward` step-by-step
    (`0.0` max-abs-diff, including the warmup region), but contains no
    per-timestep Python loop: the delay-embedded linear features are built
    from shifted, front-zero-padded slices of the input, every monomial is
    gathered over the full `(batch, timesteps, *)` tensor at once, and the
    constant-ones block is allocated a single time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input sequence of shape `(batch, timesteps, input_dim)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Incoming delay buffer of shape `(batch, state_size, input_dim)`,
        chronologically oldest-first.  This holds the `(k-1)*s` inputs
        immediately preceding `x[:, 0]` and supplies the delay taps for
        the first timesteps (zeros for a cold start).

    Returns
    -------
    features : torch.Tensor
        Output features `O_total` of shape
        `(batch, timesteps, feature_dim)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor
        Updated delay buffer of shape `(batch, state_size, input_dim)`,
        holding the last `state_size` inputs of `x` (or, when the
        sequence is shorter than the buffer, carried-over history), so a
        subsequent streaming `forward` continues seamlessly.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `x`'s trailing (feature) dimension does not equal
        `input_dim`.

    See Also
    --------
    NGCell.forward : Single-step counterpart driving the streaming path.
    """
    self._check_input_dim(x)
    batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
    pad = self.state_size  # == (k - 1) * s

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Build O_lin for the whole sequence (Eq. 5).
    #
    # Prepend the incoming delay buffer (oldest-first) so the first
    # timesteps draw their delay taps from carried-over history; a cold
    # start contributes zeros, matching the per-step loop's empty buffer.
    # For delay tap j (0..k-1), X_{i-j*s} at output index i lives at
    # padded[:, pad + i - j*s, :], i.e. the length-T window starting at
    # column (pad - j*s).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if self.k > 1:
        padded = torch.cat([state, x], dim=1)  # (batch, pad + T, input_dim)
        taps = [
            padded[:, pad - j * self.s : pad - j * self.s + seq_len, :] for j in range(self.k)
        ]
        o_lin = torch.cat(taps, dim=-1)  # (batch, T, k * input_dim)
    else:
        # k=1: no delay taps, O_lin is just the current input.
        o_lin = x  # (batch, T, input_dim)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Updated delay buffer: the last ``pad`` rows of the padded stream
    #    (FIFO drop-oldest / append-current applied to the full sequence).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if pad > 0:
        new_state = torch.cat([state, x], dim=1)[:, -pad:, :]
    else:
        new_state = state  # empty buffer, unchanged

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Assemble O_total = [c] + O_lin + O_nonlin (Eq. 9 / Eq. 10).
    #    The constant-ones block is allocated once for the whole sequence;
    #    monomials are gathered over the full (batch, T, *) tensor in one op.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    parts: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    if self.include_constant:
        parts.append(torch.ones(batch, seq_len, 1, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype))
    if self.include_linear:
        parts.append(o_lin)
    if self._emit_nonlinear:
        parts.append(self._build_nonlinear(o_lin))  # (batch, T, n_monomials)

    o_total = torch.cat(parts, dim=-1)  # (batch, T, feature_dim)

    return o_total, new_state

def validate_state(self, state: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """
    Validate the 3-D delay-buffer layout used by NG-RC.

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : torch.Tensor
        Candidate state of shape `(batch, state_size, input_dim)`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `state` is not 3-D or its non-batch dimensions do not match
        `(state_size, input_dim)`.
    """
    expected = (self.state_size, self.input_dim)
    if state.dim() != 3 or state.shape[1:] != torch.Size(expected):
        raise ValueError(
            f"NGCell.validate_state: expected a 3-D delay buffer of shape "
            f"(batch, {self.state_size}, {self.input_dim}); "
            f"got tensor of shape {tuple(state.shape)}."
        )

docs.text:
ES2NCell(reservoir_size: int, feedback_size: int, beta: float = 0.9, **kwargs: object)

Bases: _SkipReservoirCell

Single-timestep Edge-of-Stability State Network (ES2N) update.

ES2N (Ceni & Gallicchio, arXiv:2308.02902) reconciles the Echo State
Property with long memory by writing the reservoir state as a **convex
combination** of a standard nonlinear ESN branch and a linear, input-free
*orthogonal* branch.  Its update (paper Eq. 5, adapted to resdag's separate
feedback / driving-input streams) is

$$
x_t = \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + W_{fb} x_{fb,t} + W_{in} u_t + b)
      + (1 - \beta)\,O\,x_{t-1}
$$

where $\phi$ is the activation, $O$ is a **fixed random
orthogonal** matrix (the skip / residual branch), $W_r$ is the
spectral-radius-scaled frozen recurrent matrix, $W_{fb}$ / $W_{in}$
the feedback / input weights, $b$ the random bias, and
$\beta \in (0, 1]$ the *proximity* hyperparameter.

The paper folds the feedback into the input term $u_t$; resdag keeps
feedback and driving inputs as separate projections, so the projectable
input part is $W_{fb} x_{fb,t} + W_{in} u_t + b$ and the recurrent
part is $W_r x_{t-1}$ (inside $\phi$) plus $O x_{t-1}$
(the skip).

Interpretation of `beta`:

* $\beta \to 0$ — the map approaches the orthogonal, norm-preserving
  linear map $x_t \approx O x_{t-1}$.  All Jacobian eigenvalues hover
  on the complex unit circle: the *edge of stability*, giving very long
  (near-lossless) memory (paper Thm. 3.5).
* $\beta = 1$ — the skip vanishes and the update reduces to a standard
  **non-leaky** ESN $x_t = \phi(W_r x_{t-1} + \cdots)$.

Because the proximity plays the memory-timescale role a leaky ESN gives to
its leak rate, ES2N takes **no** `leak_rate` argument (and no train-mode
`noise`, which is not part of the ES2N formulation).

Parameters

reservoir_size, feedback_size, input_size, spectral_radius, bias, \

bias_scaling, activation, trainable, feedback_initializer, input_initializer, \ topology, orthogonal_scaling, seed See resdag.layers.cells._skip_cell._SkipReservoirCell and resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell for the shared meanings. beta : float, default=0.9 Proximity to the edge of stability, in \((0, 1]\). Smaller values weight the orthogonal skip more heavily (longer memory, closer to the edge of chaos); 1.0 recovers a standard non-leaky ESN. A live knob validated on assignment (like a leak rate): cell.beta = ... takes effect on the next forward.

Attributes

skip_matrix : torch.Tensor
    Frozen orthogonal skip matrix `O` (see the base class).
weight_hh, weight_feedback, weight_input, bias_h
    Recurrent, feedback, input weights and bias (see
    `resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell`).

Examples

>>> import torch
>>> cell = ES2NCell(reservoir_size=64, feedback_size=3, beta=0.1)
>>> state = cell.init_state(2, torch.device("cpu"), torch.float32)
>>> out, new_state = cell([torch.randn(2, 3)], state)
>>> out.shape
torch.Size([2, 64])

    feedback_size: int,
    alpha: float = 0.5,
    beta: float = 0.9,
    **kwargs: object
)

Bases: _SkipReservoirCell

Single-timestep Residual Echo State Network (ResESN) update.

ResESN (Ceni & Gallicchio, 2024) generalises ES2N by **decoupling** the
skip and nonlinear branch weights: where ES2N ties them into a convex
combination $(1 - \beta,\ \beta)$, ResESN gives each branch an
independent scaling coefficient.  Its shallow-model update (Eq. 2 of
arXiv:2508.21172, adapted to resdag's separate feedback / driving-input
streams) is

$$
x_t = \alpha\,O\,x_{t-1}
      + \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + W_{fb} x_{fb,t} + W_{in} u_t + b)
$$

where $\phi$ is the activation, $O$ a **fixed random
orthogonal** matrix (the residual branch), $W_r$ the
spectral-radius-scaled frozen recurrent matrix, $W_{fb}$ /
$W_{in}$ the feedback / input weights, $b$ the random bias, and
$\alpha$ (skip) and $\beta$ (nonlinear) the two independent
scaling coefficients that replace the leaky-integrator leak rate.

Relationship to other models:

* $\alpha = 1 - \beta$ recovers **ES2N** (the convex combination).
* $O = I$ with $1 - \alpha = \beta$ recovers a **leaky ESN**.

Like ES2N, ResESN takes **no** `leak_rate` (the two branch weights
subsume it) and no train-mode `noise` (not part of the formulation).

Parameters

reservoir_size, feedback_size, input_size, spectral_radius, bias, \

bias_scaling, activation, trainable, feedback_initializer, input_initializer, \ topology, orthogonal_scaling, seed See resdag.layers.cells._skip_cell._SkipReservoirCell and resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell for the shared meanings. alpha : float, default=0.5 Scaling coefficient of the orthogonal skip (residual) branch. Must be finite. Larger values weight the linear memory branch more heavily; the Echo State Property holds under a contractivity condition analogous to a standard ESN's (see the paper). A live knob validated on assignment. beta : float, default=0.9 Scaling coefficient of the nonlinear branch. Must be finite. A live knob validated on assignment.

Attributes

    Frozen orthogonal skip matrix `O` (see the base class).
weight_hh, weight_feedback, weight_input, bias_h
    Recurrent, feedback, input weights and bias (see
    `resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell`).

Examples

>>> import torch
>>> cell = ResESNCell(reservoir_size=64, feedback_size=3, alpha=0.6, beta=0.4)
>>> state = cell.init_state(2, torch.device("cpu"), torch.float32)
>>> out, new_state = cell([torch.randn(2, 3)], state)
>>> out.shape
torch.Size([2, 64])

Bases: ReservoirCell

Single-timestep frozen light-gated (LiGRU) reservoir update — a reservoir GRU.

Owns all weight matrices and biases; frozen by default (trainable=False), like a classical ESN, so only a downstream readout is fitted. Sequence iteration is delegated to the enclosing resdag.layers.reservoirs.gated.GatedReservoirLayer.

The update is a reservoir adaptation of the Light Gated Recurrent Unit (Ravanelli et al. 2018):

\[ \begin{aligned} z_t &= \sigma(W_{iz}\,u_t + W_{hz}\,h_{t-1} + b_z), \\ \tilde{h}_t &= \phi(W_{ih}\,u_t + W_{hh}\,h_{t-1} + b_h), \\ h_t &= z_t \odot h_{t-1} + (1 - z_t) \odot \tilde{h}_t, \end{aligned} \]

where \(u_t = W_{fb}\,x_{fb,t} + W_{in}\,x_{in,t}\) is the drive (feedback plus optional driving input, projected exactly as in ESNCell), \(\sigma\) is the sigmoid update-gate nonlinearity, and \(\phi\) is the candidate nonlinearity ("relu" by default, the LiGRU choice). z gates retention: z→1 keeps h, z→0 writes the candidate.

Stability of a frozen gated reservoir

A frozen random GRU can saturate — a random update-gate pre-activation centred at 0 gives z ≈ 0.5, which over-writes the state every step and washes out memory (or, with an unfortunate draw, drives h to a constant). Two knobs keep it well-behaved:

  • update_gate_bias (default 2.0) biases the update gate toward retention: b_z = update_gate_bias makes z start near σ(2) ≈ 0.88, so a fresh reservoir keeps most of its state each step and the dynamics do not collapse. This mirrors the classic "initialise the forget-gate bias positive" trick for trainable gated RNNs.
  • spectral_radius scales the recurrent candidate weight \(W_{hh}\) (via the shared resdag machinery), controlling the echo of past state through the candidate path just as it does for an ESN.

Even so, a frozen gated reservoir often underperforms a plain ESN; the gated cell is usually most useful with trainable=True (a BPTT rollout that updates the gates), which this cell fully supports via the base trainable property.

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    bias_scaling: float = 1.0,
    update_gate_bias: float = 2.0,
    activation: str = "relu",
    gate_activation: str = "sigmoid",
    trainable: bool = False,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    topology: TopologySpec = None,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    *,
    recurrent_initializer: TopologySpec = None,
    bias_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    initial_state_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
    gate_recurrent_initializer: TopologySpec = None,
    gate_feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    gate_input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    gate_bias_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    gate_spectral_radius: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__()

    self.reservoir_size = reservoir_size
    self.feedback_size = feedback_size
    # Treat input_size == 0 the same as None (no driving-input weights),
    # matching ESNCell and the ott_esn/power_augmented factories.
    self.input_size = input_size if input_size else None
    self.topology = select_recurrent_spec(
        topology=topology, recurrent_initializer=recurrent_initializer
    )
    if dtype is not None and not dtype.is_floating_point:
        raise ValueError("Reservoir dtype must be floating point")
    if not bias and bias_initializer is not None:
        raise ValueError("bias_initializer requires bias=True")
    self.bias_initializer = bias_initializer
    self.initial_state_initializer = initial_state_initializer
    target_device = torch.device(device) if device is not None else torch.empty(0).device
    if target_device.type == "mps" and (dtype or torch.get_default_dtype()) == torch.float64:
        raise TypeError("MPS does not support float64; use float32 or CPU")
    # Initialize on CPU before a Metal transfer for portable RNG/linalg support.
    init_device = "cpu" if target_device is not None and target_device.type == "mps" else device
    self._factory_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"device": init_device, "dtype": dtype}
    if not bias and gate_bias_initializer is not None:
        raise ValueError("gate_bias_initializer requires bias=True")
    if not self.input_size and gate_input_initializer is not None:
        raise ValueError("gate_input_initializer requires input_size")
    if gate_spectral_radius is not None and (
        not torch.isfinite(torch.tensor(gate_spectral_radius)) or gate_spectral_radius < 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("gate_spectral_radius must be finite and non-negative")
    self.gate_recurrent_initializer = gate_recurrent_initializer
    self.gate_feedback_initializer = gate_feedback_initializer
    self.gate_input_initializer = gate_input_initializer
    self.gate_bias_initializer = gate_bias_initializer
    self.gate_spectral_radius = gate_spectral_radius
    self._separate_gate_drive = (
        gate_feedback_initializer is not None or gate_input_initializer is not None
    )
    self.spectral_radius = spectral_radius
    self.feedback_initializer = feedback_initializer
    self.input_initializer = input_initializer
    self.update_gate_bias = float(update_gate_bias)

    self._trainable = trainable
    self.seed = seed
    self._seed_int = coerce_seed_to_int(seed)
    if self._seed_int is None:
        self._seed_int = int(torch.randint(0, 2**63 - 1, (1,), device="cpu").item())

    self._activation_name = activation
    self.activation_fn = self._get_activation(activation)
    self._gate_activation_name = gate_activation
    self.gate_activation_fn = self._get_activation(gate_activation)

    self._bias = bias
    self.bias_scaling = bias_scaling

    self._initialize_weights()
    install_initial_state(
        self,
        self.initial_state_initializer,
        seed=_salt_seed(self._seed_int, 0x9E3779B9 * 7),
        state_size=self.state_size,
        reference=self.weight_feedback,
    )

    # Apply the requested freeze through the base property so construction
    # and post-init ``cell.trainable = ...`` share one code path.
    self.trainable = trainable
    if target_device is not None and target_device.type == "mps":
        self.to(target_device)

def forward(
    self,
    inputs: list[torch.Tensor],
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute the next gated state for a single timestep.

    Parameters
    ----------
    inputs : list[torch.Tensor]
        `inputs[0]` is the feedback slice `(batch, feedback_size)`;
        `inputs[1]` (if present) is the driving input
        `(batch, input_size)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current packed state of shape `(batch, state_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    output : torch.Tensor
        Next hidden state `h` of shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor
        Next packed state (identical to `output` for this single-state cell).
    """
    drive = self.project_inputs(inputs)
    return self.step(drive, state)

def project_inputs(self, inputs: list[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Precompute the input *drive* `u = W_fb x_fb + W_in x_in` for the sequence.

    This is the sequence-precomputable part of the gated update — it does
    **not** include the gate biases or the recurrent terms, which depend on
    the (per-step) state.  Works on both full
    `(batch, timesteps, features)` sequences (the layer fast path) and
    single-step `(batch, features)` slices (reused by `forward`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    inputs : list[torch.Tensor]
        `inputs[0]` feedback, `inputs[1]` (optional) driving input.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Drive `u` with the inputs' leading dims and trailing dimension
        `reservoir_size`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On a feedback/driving-input feature-dimension mismatch, or if a
        driving input is supplied to a cell built without `input_size`.
    """
    fb = inputs[0]
    if fb.shape[-1] != self.feedback_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Feedback size mismatch. Expected {self.feedback_size}, got {fb.shape[-1]}"
        )
    drive = F.linear(fb, self.weight_feedback)

    if len(inputs) > 1:
        if self.weight_input is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Reservoir was initialized without input_size, "
                "but driving input was provided in forward pass"
            )
        x = inputs[1]
        if x.shape[-1] != self.input_size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Driving input size mismatch. Expected {self.input_size}, got {x.shape[-1]}"
            )
        drive = drive + F.linear(x, self.weight_input)

    if self._separate_gate_drive:
        gate_feedback = (
            self.weight_gate_feedback
            if self.weight_gate_feedback is not None
            else self.weight_feedback
        )
        gate_drive = F.linear(fb, gate_feedback)
        if len(inputs) > 1:
            gate_input = (
                self.weight_gate_input
                if self.weight_gate_input is not None
                else self.weight_input
            )
            assert gate_input is not None
            gate_drive = gate_drive + F.linear(inputs[1], gate_input)
        return torch.cat((drive, gate_drive), dim=-1)
    return drive

def step(
    self,
    projected_t: torch.Tensor,
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Single-step gated update consuming a slice of `project_inputs`.

    Shape-static and branch-free (both gates are `σ` / `φ` of tensors),
    so it traces cleanly under `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` for the
    compiled forecast engine.

    Parameters
    ----------
    projected_t : torch.Tensor
        Per-timestep drive `u_t` of shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current packed state `(batch, state_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    output : torch.Tensor
        Next hidden state `h` of shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor
        Next packed state (identical to `output` here).
    """
    (h,) = _split_state(state, self.reservoir_size)
    if self._separate_gate_drive:
        candidate_drive, gate_drive = projected_t.split(self.reservoir_size, dim=-1)
    else:
        candidate_drive = gate_drive = projected_t

    # Update-gate pre-activation: drive + recurrent gate term + retention bias.
    z_pre = gate_drive + F.linear(h, self.weight_hz)
    if self.bias_z is not None:
        z_pre = z_pre + self.bias_z
    z = self.gate_activation_fn(z_pre)

    # Candidate pre-activation: drive + recurrent candidate term + bias.
    h_pre = candidate_drive + F.linear(h, self.weight_hh)
    if self.bias_h is not None:
        h_pre = h_pre + self.bias_h
    h_tilde = self.activation_fn(h_pre)

    # Retention convention: z→1 keeps h, z→0 writes the candidate.
    new_h = z * h + (1.0 - z) * h_tilde
    new_state = _pack_state(new_h)
    return new_h, new_state

Bases: ESNCell

Abstract base for reservoir cells that integrate $\dot h = f(h, u)$.

Extends `resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell` with fixed-step ODE
integration over each input interval.  Concrete subclasses implement only
`vector_field` (the $\dot h = f(h, u)$ term); this base supplies
the sub-stepping (`step`), the input projection (inherited
`ESNCell.project_inputs`), and the sequence-level `forward`.

The state update integrates one input interval — one timestep of the driving
sequence — with `substeps` fixed sub-steps of size `dt / substeps`,
holding the projected input drive $u$ constant across the interval
(zero-order hold).  Writing $g = \text{dt}/\text{substeps}$ for the
sub-step size, one **Euler** sub-step is

$$
h \leftarrow h + g \, f(h, u),
$$

and one classical **RK4** sub-step is the usual four-stage weighted average.
The recurrent / feedback / input weights, bias, spectral scaling and
freezing are all owned and initialized by `ESNCell`.

The forward-Euler step size of the Euler State Network is dt with substeps=1. substeps : int, default=1 Number of fixed integration sub-steps per input interval. Each has size dt / substeps. def forward(
    self,
    inputs: list[torch.Tensor],
    state: torch.Tensor,

    the vector field over one interval of length `dt`.

def step(
    self,
    projected_t: torch.Tensor,
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    r"""Integrate one interval from a precomputed projection slice.

    Consumes `projected_t` (`W_fb x_fb + W_in u + b` for this interval)
    and integrates the vector field over one interval.  For the fixed-step
    solvers the sub-step loop is static, so this traces cleanly under
    `torch.compile` (`fullgraph=True`), enabling the compiled
    forecast / teacher-forced engines.

    Parameters
    ----------
    projected_t : torch.Tensor
        Slice of `ESNCell.project_inputs`, shape
        `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current reservoir state, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    output : torch.Tensor
        Per-step output `(batch, output_size)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor

Bases: ContinuousReservoirCell

Single-timestep Euler State Network (EuSN) update.

EuSN (Gallicchio, arXiv:2203.09382) models the reservoir as an ODE

$$
\dot h(t) = \tanh\!\big(W_h\, h(t) + W_x\, x(t) + b\big),
$$

with $W_h$ **antisymmetric** ($W_h = -W_h^\top$), and integrates
it with a single forward-Euler step of size $\varepsilon$, subtracting
a small **diffusion** term $\gamma I$ from the recurrence for numerical
stability:

$$
h_t = h_{t-1} + \varepsilon\,
      \tanh\!\big((W_h - \gamma I)\, h_{t-1} + W_x\, x_t + b\big).
$$

The antisymmetric $W_h$ is a rotation generator (purely imaginary
eigenvalues), so $x \mapsto W_h x$ conserves the state norm; a small
Euler step of the resulting flow is therefore **near-norm-preserving** — a
stable, non-dissipative, long-memory regime with local Lyapunov exponents
near zero (the "edge of stability").  The diffusion $\gamma I$ adds a
tiny contraction that damps the forward-Euler discretization error and keeps
the recurrence from drifting outward over long sequences.

resdag construction

resdag keeps feedback and driving inputs as *separate* projections, so the
paper's $W_x x_t + b$ maps to resdag's precomputed drive
$W_{fb} x_{fb,t} + W_{in} u_t + b$ (the inherited
`resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell.project_inputs`).  The
antisymmetric $W_h$ is obtained **on the fly** from the frozen,
spectral-radius-scaled recurrent matrix `weight_hh` (`= W_r`) as
$W_r - W_r^\top$; the stored `W_r` is left untouched (cleaner than
baking antisymmetry into the buffer, and matching the paper's constraint
exactly).  The vector field is therefore

$$
f(h, u) = \tanh\!\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\, h + u\big),
$$

with $u$ the precomputed drive and one Euler sub-step of size
$\varepsilon$ (`dt=epsilon`, `substeps=1`).

Because the antisymmetric part $W_r - W_r^\top$ has purely imaginary
eigenvalues, a layer-level `spectral_radius` on `W_r` still controls the
*rotation rate* of the recurrence (the largest imaginary eigenvalue
magnitude), so the usual scaling knob remains meaningful.

Parameters

reservoir_size, feedback_size, input_size, bias, bias_scaling, activation, \

trainable, feedback_initializer, input_initializer, topology, seed See resdag.layers.cells.esn_cell.ESNCell. activation defaults to "tanh" (the EuSN nonlinearity); other activations are accepted for experimentation. epsilon : float, default=0.01 Forward-Euler step size \(\varepsilon\). Small values sit the reservoir near the edge of stability (near-norm-preserving); the paper sweeps \(\varepsilon \in \{10^{-5}, \dots, 1\}\). Stored as the base dt. gamma : float, default=0.01 Diffusion coefficient \(\gamma \ge 0\) subtracted as \(\gamma I\) from the antisymmetric recurrence. A small positive value damps the Euler discretization error; 0.0 recovers the purely norm-preserving (undamped) antisymmetric flow. A live knob validated on assignment. spectral_radius : float, optional Target rotation rate of the effective antisymmetric operator \(W_r - W_r^\top\) — its largest |imaginary eigenvalue|, the quantity that actually drives the dynamics — not the raw W_r. W_r is rescaled so the skew part hits this radius (see the notes on antisymmetric scaling below). None leaves W_r unscaled. substeps : int, default=1 Fixed integration sub-steps per interval (see ContinuousReservoirCell). 1 is the single forward-Euler step of the paper. solver : {'euler', 'rk4', 'torchdiffeq'}, default='euler' Integration scheme. Examples

>>> import torch
>>> cell = EuSNCell(reservoir_size=64, feedback_size=3, epsilon=0.01, gamma=0.01)
>>> state = cell.init_state(2, torch.device("cpu"), torch.float32)
>>> out, new_state = cell([torch.randn(2, 3)], state)
>>> out.shape
torch.Size([2, 64])

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    epsilon: float = 0.01,
    gamma: float = 0.01,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    bias_scaling: float = 1.0,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    substeps: int = 1,
    solver: str = "euler",
    torchdiffeq_method: str = "dopri5",
    rtol: float = 1e-6,
    atol: float = 1e-8,
    trainable: bool = False,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    topology: TopologySpec = None,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    *,
    recurrent_initializer: TopologySpec = None,
    bias_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    initial_state_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    # ``gamma`` is validated by its property setter (shared with live writes);
    # stash the backing field before super().__init__ so the setter is ready,
    # then re-validate below once the object is fully initialised.
    self._gamma: float = 0.0
    # ``spectral_radius`` here targets the *effective* antisymmetric operator
    # ``W_r - W_r^T`` (the rotation rate that actually drives the dynamics),
    # NOT the raw ``W_r``.  The two differ substantially: for a dense random
    # ``W_r`` scaled to radius rho, the skew part ``W_r - W_r^T`` has a much
    # larger imaginary rate (~2x+), which would push the forward-Euler step
    # far past the stable edge and make the state grow without bound.  So we
    # pass ``spectral_radius=None`` to the parent (leaving ``W_r`` un-scaled)
    # and rescale ``weight_hh`` below so ``W_r - W_r^T`` hits the target.
    self._target_skew_radius = spectral_radius
    super().__init__(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        input_size=input_size,
        spectral_radius=None,
        bias=bias,
        bias_scaling=bias_scaling,
        activation=activation,
        trainable=trainable,
        dt=epsilon,
        substeps=substeps,
        solver=solver,
        torchdiffeq_method=torchdiffeq_method,
        rtol=rtol,
        atol=atol,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        topology=topology,
        seed=seed,
        recurrent_initializer=recurrent_initializer,
        bias_initializer=bias_initializer,
        initial_state_initializer=initial_state_initializer,
        device=device,
        dtype=dtype,
    )
    # Record the requested target on the base ``spectral_radius`` slot so the
    # ``__repr__`` and any introspection report the meaningful (skew-operator)
    # value rather than ``None``.
    self.spectral_radius = spectral_radius
    if spectral_radius is not None:
        self._scale_skew_spectral_radius(spectral_radius)
    self.gamma = gamma

def vector_field(self, state: torch.Tensor, projected_u: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    r"""EuSN field $\tanh\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\,h + u\big)$.

    Antisymmetrizes the frozen recurrent matrix on the fly
    ($W_r - W_r^\top$), subtracts the diffusion $\gamma I$, adds
    the precomputed input drive `projected_u`, and applies the activation
    (`tanh` by default).

    Parameters
    ----------
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current state `h`, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    projected_u : torch.Tensor
        Precomputed input drive `u = W_fb x_fb + W_in u + b` for the
        interval, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        $\dot h$, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    """
    # Antisymmetric recurrence W_h = W_r - W_r^T, applied as h (W_r - W_r^T)^T
    # = h W_r^T - h W_r via F.linear conventions.  Compute h @ W_h^T directly:
    # W_h^T = (W_r - W_r^T)^T = W_r^T - W_r, so h @ W_h^T = h @ W_r^T - h @ W_r.
    w = self.weight_hh
    recurrent = state @ w.t() - state @ w
    pre = recurrent - self._gamma * state + projected_u
    return self.activation_fn(pre)

Bases: ReservoirCell, ABC

Abstract base for spiking reservoir cells (the LSM substrate).

Owns the machinery shared by every spiking neuron model — the packed multi-tensor state, the surrogate-gradient spike, the spike reset, and the low-pass readout trace — and delegates only the sub-threshold membrane dynamics to a concrete subclass through neuron_update.

Packed state layout

A spiking cell carries several (batch, reservoir_size) state tensors, packed side-by-side into one 2-D (batch, n_state_tensors * reservoir_size) tensor (the convention documented in resdag.layers.cells.gated_cell). The layout is fixed by the subclass via n_state_tensors; the last packed block is always the synaptic trace r (owned by this base), and the leading blocks are the subclass's neuron state, which ends with the previous step's spikes s (the recurrent input) — e.g. V then s, or I, V then s. Concretely:

  • first-order LIF (n_state_tensors = 3): [V | s | r];
  • CuBa-LIF (n_state_tensors = 4): [I | V | s | r].

neuron_update receives / returns only the neuron tensors (all but the trace); the base peels the trace off before the call and re-appends the updated trace after, so a subclass never handles the trace. Because those neuron tensors end with s, the membrane potential V is the second-to-last neuron tensor — this is what output="voltage" returns.

The surrogate-gradient spike

spike implements the straight-through estimator: an exact Heaviside forward with a fast-sigmoid surrogate backward (slope surrogate_beta). Subclasses call it from neuron_update to emit spikes from the (updated) membrane potential.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of spiking units (hidden dimension of each packed state tensor).

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir_size: int,
    v_threshold: float = 1.0,
    reset: str = "subtract",
    surrogate_beta: float = 10.0,
    trace_decay: float = 0.9,
    output: str = "trace",
) -> None:
    super().__init__()

    if reservoir_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"reservoir_size must be a positive integer, got {reservoir_size}")
    if reset not in _VALID_RESETS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown reset {reset!r}. Supported: {sorted(_VALID_RESETS)}.")
    if output not in _VALID_OUTPUTS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown output {output!r}. Supported: {sorted(_VALID_OUTPUTS)}.")

    self.reservoir_size = reservoir_size
    self.v_threshold = float(v_threshold)
    self.reset = reset
    self._output = output

    # ``surrogate_beta`` / ``trace_decay`` are live knobs validated by their
    # property setters (shared by the constructor and post-init writes).
    self._surrogate_beta: float = 10.0
    self._trace_decay: float = 0.0
    self.surrogate_beta = surrogate_beta
    self.trace_decay = trace_decay

Surrogate-gradient spike from a membrane potential (straight-through).

Forward is the exact Heaviside threshold (v - V_th > 0); backward flows through the fast-sigmoid surrogate \(\sigma(\beta (v - V_\text{th}))\). The surrogate + (hard - surrogate).detach() construction makes the returned tensor equal hard in value while carrying the surrogate's gradient — a pure composition of tensor ops (no custom torch.autograd.Function), so it traces fullgraph=True.

def spike(self, v: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    r"""Surrogate-gradient spike from a membrane potential (straight-through).

    Forward is the exact Heaviside threshold `(v - V_th > 0)`; backward
    flows through the fast-sigmoid surrogate
    $\sigma(\beta (v - V_\text{th}))$.  The
    `surrogate + (hard - surrogate).detach()` construction makes the
    returned tensor *equal* `hard` in value while carrying the surrogate's
    gradient — a pure composition of tensor ops (no custom
    `torch.autograd.Function`), so it traces `fullgraph=True`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    v : torch.Tensor
        Membrane potential, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Binary spike tensor (values in `{0, 1}`), same shape as `v`,
        with a surrogate gradient w.r.t. `v`.
    """
    shifted = v - self.v_threshold
    hard = (shifted > 0).to(v.dtype)
    surrogate = torch.sigmoid(self._surrogate_beta * shifted)
    return surrogate + (hard - surrogate).detach()

def apply_reset(self, v: torch.Tensor, spikes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    r"""Reset the membrane potential on the neurons that just spiked.

    `'subtract'` (soft): $V \leftarrow V - V_\text{th}\,s$ — keeps the
    supra-threshold overshoot, the standard LIF reset.  `'zero'` (hard):
    $V \leftarrow V (1 - s)$ — clamps the membrane to zero on a spike.
    The branch is a Python attribute compare fixed at construction, so it is
    static under `torch.compile`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    v : torch.Tensor
        Post-integration membrane potential, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    spikes : torch.Tensor
        Spike tensor from `spike`, same shape.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        The reset membrane potential.
    """
    if self.reset == "zero":
        return v * (1.0 - spikes)
    return v - self.v_threshold * spikes

def update_trace(self, trace: torch.Tensor, spikes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    r"""Low-pass the spike train into the readout trace.

    $r_t = \kappa\, r_{t-1} + s_t$ with $\kappa$ = `trace_decay`.
    The trace is the real-valued synaptic response a readout regresses on.

    Parameters
    ----------
    trace : torch.Tensor
        Previous trace `r_{t-1}`, shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    spikes : torch.Tensor
        Current spikes `s_t`, same shape.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Updated trace `r_t`.
    """
    return self._trace_decay * trace + spikes

def forward(
    self,
    inputs: list[torch.Tensor],
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Advance one timestep: project inputs, then `step`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    inputs : list[torch.Tensor]
        `inputs[0]` feedback `(batch, feedback_size)`; `inputs[1]`
        (optional) driving input `(batch, input_size)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current packed state `(batch, state_size)`.

    output : torch.Tensor
        Readable per-step output `(batch, reservoir_size)` (see
        `output`).

    projected = self.project_inputs(inputs)

def step(
    self,
    projected_t: torch.Tensor,
    state: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    r"""Single-step spiking update from a precomputed input drive.

    Peels the trailing trace `r` off the packed state, hands the neuron
    tensors + drive to `neuron_update`, low-passes the returned spikes
    into the new trace, and re-packs.  Branch-free apart from the static
    reset / output selection, so it traces `fullgraph=True` for the
    compiled forecast / teacher-forced engines.

    Parameters
    ----------
    projected_t : torch.Tensor
        Precomputed input drive for this step, shape
        `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    state : torch.Tensor
        Current packed state `(batch, state_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    output : torch.Tensor
        Readable per-step output `(batch, reservoir_size)`.
    new_state : torch.Tensor
        Updated packed state `(batch, state_size)`.
    """
    tensors = _split_state(state, self.reservoir_size)
    neuron_state = tensors[:-1]
    trace = tensors[-1]

    new_neuron_state, spikes = self.neuron_update(neuron_state, projected_t)
    new_trace = self.update_trace(trace, spikes)

    new_state = _pack_state(*new_neuron_state, new_trace)
    # The neuron tensors always END with the current spikes ``s``
    # (``[V | s]`` or ``[I | V | s]``), so the membrane potential ``V`` is the
    # *second-to-last* neuron tensor — that is what the "voltage" mode reads.
    v = new_neuron_state[-2]
    output = self._select_output(new_trace, v, spikes)
    return output, new_state

Single-timestep leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) reservoir cell.

Owns the frozen recurrent weight W_rec (topology-initialised and spectral-radius scaled like an ESN), the feedback / driving-input weights and the bias. The sub-threshold dynamics are a discretised leaky integrator; the surrogate spike, reset, and readout trace are inherited from resdag.layers.cells.spiking_cell.SpikingReservoirCell.

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    tau_mem: float = 20.0,
    tau_syn: float = 10.0,
    dt: float = 1.0,
    synaptic_current: bool = False,
    v_threshold: float = 1.0,
    reset: str = "subtract",
    surrogate_beta: float = 10.0,
    trace_decay: float = 0.9,
    output: str = "trace",
    spectral_radius: float | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    bias_scaling: float = 1.0,
    trainable: bool = False,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    topology: TopologySpec = None,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    *,
    recurrent_initializer: TopologySpec = None,
    bias_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    initial_state_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    # First-order LIF packs [V | s | r] (3 tensors); CuBa-LIF packs
    # [I | V | s | r] (4).  Set the count BEFORE super().__init__ so
    # ``state_size`` is correct the moment the base needs it.
    self.synaptic_current = bool(synaptic_current)
    self.n_state_tensors = 4 if self.synaptic_current else 3

    super().__init__(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        v_threshold=v_threshold,
        reset=reset,
        surrogate_beta=surrogate_beta,
        trace_decay=trace_decay,
        output=output,
    )

    self.feedback_size = feedback_size
    # Treat input_size == 0 the same as None (no driving-input weights),
    # matching ESNCell and the premade factories.
    self.input_size = input_size if input_size else None
    self.tau_mem = float(tau_mem)
    self.tau_syn = float(tau_syn)
    self.dt = float(dt)

    self.topology = select_recurrent_spec(
        topology=topology, recurrent_initializer=recurrent_initializer
    )
    if dtype is not None and not dtype.is_floating_point:
        raise ValueError("Reservoir dtype must be floating point")
    if not bias and bias_initializer is not None:
        raise ValueError("bias_initializer requires bias=True")
    self.bias_initializer = bias_initializer
    self.initial_state_initializer = initial_state_initializer
    target_device = torch.device(device) if device is not None else torch.empty(0).device
    if target_device.type == "mps" and (dtype or torch.get_default_dtype()) == torch.float64:
        raise TypeError("MPS does not support float64; use float32 or CPU")
    # Initialize on CPU before a Metal transfer for portable RNG/linalg support.
    init_device = "cpu" if target_device is not None and target_device.type == "mps" else device
    self._factory_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"device": init_device, "dtype": dtype}
    self.spectral_radius = spectral_radius
    self.feedback_initializer = feedback_initializer
    self.input_initializer = input_initializer
    self._bias = bias
    self.bias_scaling = bias_scaling

    self.seed = seed
    self._seed_int = coerce_seed_to_int(seed)
    if self._seed_int is None:
        self._seed_int = int(torch.randint(0, 2**63 - 1, (1,), device="cpu").item())
    self._trainable = trainable

    self._initialize_weights()
    install_initial_state(
        self,
        self.initial_state_initializer,
        seed=_salt_seed(self._seed_int, 0x9E3779B9 * 7),
        state_size=self.state_size,
        reference=self.weight_feedback,
    )

    # Apply the requested freeze through the base property so construction and
    # post-init ``cell.trainable = ...`` share one code path.
    self.trainable = trainable

This is the input-dependent part of the neuron drive — the recurrent spike term W_rec s is added inside neuron_update from the previous spikes carried in state. Works on full (batch, timesteps, features) sequences (the layer fast path) and on single-step (batch, features) slices.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION inputs

def project_inputs(self, inputs: list[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Precompute the analog input drive `W_fb x_fb + W_in u + b`.

    This is the *input-dependent* part of the neuron drive — the recurrent
    spike term `W_rec s` is added inside `neuron_update` from the
    previous spikes carried in state.  Works on full
    `(batch, timesteps, features)` sequences (the layer fast path) and on
    single-step `(batch, features)` slices.

    Parameters
    ----------
    inputs : list[torch.Tensor]
        `inputs[0]` feedback; `inputs[1]` (optional) driving input.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Input drive with the inputs' leading dims and trailing dimension
        `reservoir_size`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On a feedback / driving-input feature-dimension mismatch, or if a
        driving input is supplied to a cell built without `input_size`.
    """
    fb = inputs[0]
    if fb.shape[-1] != self.feedback_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Feedback size mismatch. Expected {self.feedback_size}, got {fb.shape[-1]}"
        )
    drive = F.linear(fb, self.weight_feedback)

    if len(inputs) > 1:
        if self.weight_input is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Reservoir was initialized without input_size, "
                "but driving input was provided in forward pass"
            )
        x = inputs[1]
        if x.shape[-1] != self.input_size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Driving input size mismatch. Expected {self.input_size}, got {x.shape[-1]}"
            )
        drive = drive + F.linear(x, self.weight_input)

    if self.bias_h is not None:
        drive = drive + self.bias_h

    return drive

Advance the LIF (or CuBa-LIF) membrane one step and emit spikes.

The recurrent spike term \(W_\text{rec} s_t\) is added here (from the previous spikes s carried in neuron_state), completing the drive projected_input + W_rec s. Branch-free apart from the static synaptic_current / reset selection, so it traces fullgraph=True.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION neuron_state

(V, s) for first-order LIF or (I, V, s) for CuBa-LIF, each of shape (batch, reservoir_size). s is the previous step's spikes (recurrent input); I / V the current / membrane states.

TYPE: tuple of torch.Tensor

projected_input

Precomputed analog drive W_fb x_fb + W_in u + b, shape (batch, reservoir_size).

TYPE: Tensor

RETURNS DESCRIPTION new_neuron_state

(V_new, s_new) or (I_new, V_new, s_new) in packing order.

TYPE: tuple of torch.Tensor

spikes

The spikes emitted this step (== s_new), carrying the surrogate gradient.

def neuron_update(
    self,
    neuron_state: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...],
    projected_input: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], torch.Tensor]:
    r"""Advance the LIF (or CuBa-LIF) membrane one step and emit spikes.

    The recurrent spike term $W_\text{rec} s_t$ is added here (from the
    previous spikes `s` carried in `neuron_state`), completing the drive
    `projected_input + W_rec s`.  Branch-free apart from the static
    `synaptic_current` / reset selection, so it traces `fullgraph=True`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    neuron_state : tuple of torch.Tensor
        `(V, s)` for first-order LIF or `(I, V, s)` for CuBa-LIF, each of
        shape `(batch, reservoir_size)`.  `s` is the previous step's
        spikes (recurrent input); `I` / `V` the current / membrane states.
    projected_input : torch.Tensor
        Precomputed analog drive `W_fb x_fb + W_in u + b`, shape
        `(batch, reservoir_size)`.

    Returns
    -------
    new_neuron_state : tuple of torch.Tensor
        `(V_new, s_new)` or `(I_new, V_new, s_new)` in packing order.
    spikes : torch.Tensor
        The spikes emitted this step (`== s_new`), carrying the surrogate
        gradient.
    """
    # Complete the drive with the recurrent spike-coupling term.
    recurrent = F.linear(neuron_state[-1], self.weight_rec)
    drive = projected_input + recurrent

    if self.synaptic_current:
        i_prev, v_prev = neuron_state[0], neuron_state[1]
        i_new = self.alpha * i_prev + drive
        v_pre = self.beta * v_prev + (1.0 - self.beta) * i_new
        spikes = self.spike(v_pre)
        v_new = self.apply_reset(v_pre, spikes)
        return (i_new, v_new, spikes), spikes

    v_prev = neuron_state[0]
    v_pre = self.beta * v_prev + (1.0 - self.beta) * drive
    spikes = self.spike(v_pre)
    v_new = self.apply_reset(v_pre, spikes)
    return (v_new, spikes), spikes

Bases: ProjectedInputCell

Coupled nonlinear oscillators, frozen by default.

Uses the explicit-damping variant of equation (3) in the coRNN paper:

v_new = v + dt * (tanh(W_hh h + W_hv v + W_fb x + W_in u + b)
                  - gamma*h - epsilon*v)
h_new = h + dt * v_new

The packed state is cat([h, v], -1) with width 2*reservoir_size; the output is position h_new with width reservoir_size. recurrent_initializer configures the position matrix weight_hh; velocity_initializer configures the velocity matrix weight_hv. spectral_radius scales only the position matrix, respecting a builder's rescaling policy. It does not guarantee stability of the oscillator update. dt, gamma and epsilon are finite positive/nonnegative scalars. Both recurrent matrices default to uniform(-1/sqrt(size), 1/sqrt(size)). Input projections default to uniform(-1, 1). Weights are initialized directly in dtype on device (MPS initializes on CPU then transfers once). trainable=True enables ordinary backpropagation.

Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.00951

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    *,
    dt: float = 0.1,
    gamma: float = 1.0,
    epsilon: float = 1.0,
    recurrent_initializer: RecurrentInitializerSpec = None,
    velocity_initializer: RecurrentInitializerSpec = None,
    topology: TopologySpec = None,
    spectral_radius: float | None = None,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    bias_scaling: float = 1.0,
    trainable: bool = False,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    device = torch.device(device) if device is not None else torch.get_default_device()
    size = positive_size("reservoir_size", reservoir_size)
    dt = finite_scalar("dt", dt, positive=True)
    gamma = finite_scalar("gamma", gamma)
    epsilon = finite_scalar("epsilon", epsilon)
    if spectral_radius is not None:
        spectral_radius = finite_scalar("spectral_radius", spectral_radius)
    position_spec = select_recurrent_spec(
        topology=topology, recurrent_initializer=recurrent_initializer
    )
    super().__init__(
        size,
        feedback_size,
        input_size,
        bias=bias,
        bias_scaling=bias_scaling,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        seed=seed,
        device=device,
        dtype=dtype,
    )
    self.reservoir_size = size
    self.dt = dt
    self.gamma = gamma
    self.epsilon = epsilon
    self.spectral_radius = spectral_radius
    self.weight_hh = nn.Parameter(
        torch.empty(size, size, device=self.weight_feedback.device, dtype=dtype),
        requires_grad=False,
    )
    self.weight_hv = nn.Parameter(
        torch.empty(size, size, device=self.weight_feedback.device, dtype=dtype),
        requires_grad=False,
    )
    for weight, spec, offset, radius in (
        (self.weight_hh, position_spec, 41, spectral_radius),
        (self.weight_hv, velocity_initializer, 53, None),
    ):
        initializer = resolve_recurrent_initializer(spec, seed=role_seed(seed, offset))
        with torch.no_grad():
            if initializer is None:
                bound = 1.0 / math.sqrt(size)
                nn.init.uniform_(
                    weight,
                    -bound,
                    bound,
                    generator=create_torch_generator(role_seed(seed, offset), weight.device),
                )
                if radius is not None:
                    weight.copy_(scale_to_spectral_radius(weight, radius))
            else:
                weight.copy_(initializer.initialize(weight, spectral_radius=radius))
            if not torch.isfinite(weight).all():
                raise ValueError("Recurrent initializer produced non-finite weights")
    self.trainable = trainable
    if device is not None and torch.device(device).type == "mps":
        self.to(device)

step(projected_t: Tensor, state: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]

Return updated positions and packed position/velocity state for one frame.

Source code in src/resdag/layers/cells/cornn_cell.py 
def step(self, projected_t: Tensor, state: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return updated positions and packed position/velocity state for one frame."""
    self._check_step(projected_t, state, self.reservoir_size)
    h, v = state.split(self.reservoir_size, dim=-1)
    force = torch.tanh(projected_t + F.linear(h, self.weight_hh) + F.linear(v, self.weight_hv))
    new_v = v + self.dt * (force - self.gamma * h - self.epsilon * v)
    new_h = h + self.dt * new_v
    return new_h, torch.cat((new_h, new_v), dim=-1)

LegendreDelayCell(
    order: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    *,
    theta: float = 100.0,
    dt: float = 1.0,
    memory_channels: int | None = None,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    device: device | str | None = None,
    dtype: dtype | None = None
)

Bases: ProjectedInputCell

Linear Legendre delay network (LDN), rather than a full nonlinear LMU.

Implements equations (1), (2), and (4) of Voelker et al., NeurIPS 2019. The analytic continuous matrices are fixed buffers, with theta already divided into continuous_A and continuous_B. An augmented matrix exponential computes exact zero-order-hold A/B for interval dt; no matrix inverse or Euler approximation is used.

order is the number of Legendre coefficients per channel. memory_channels=None uses feedback_size + (input_size or 0) channels, one for each input dimension; their default encoders concatenate the raw feedback and driver. When channels equal that sum, identity encoders are also used by default. Other channel counts use random linear encoders with uniform bounds 1/sqrt(total input width). Explicit feedback/input initializer specs override the respective encoder.

State and output both have width memory_channels * order. They flatten (batch, memory_channels, order) in channel-major order. theta is a memory window in the same time units as dt (default dt=1 means samples). trainable=True trains only input encoders; the memory dynamics stay fixed. The linear memory should be followed by nonlinear features/model components when the task needs nonlinear predictions.

The scaled continuous matrix 1-norm must not exceed 2**20; extreme dt/theta ratios or orders beyond this numerical bound are rejected before exponentiation. MPS construction initializes on CPU then moves once.

Reference: https://papers.nips.cc/paper/9689-legendre-memory-units-continuous-time-representation-in-recurrent-neural-networks

Source code in src/resdag/layers/cells/legendre_delay_cell.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    order: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    *,
    theta: float = 100.0,
    dt: float = 1.0,
    memory_channels: int | None = None,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec = None,
    trainable: bool = False,
    seed: SeedLike = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
) -> None:
    device = torch.device(device) if device is not None else torch.get_default_device()
    order = positive_size("order", order)
    positive_size("feedback_size", feedback_size)
    if input_size is not None:
        positive_size("input_size", input_size)
    total_width = feedback_size + (input_size or 0)
    channels = (
        total_width
        if memory_channels is None
        else positive_size("memory_channels", memory_channels)
    )
    theta = finite_scalar("theta", theta, positive=True)
    dt = finite_scalar("dt", dt, positive=True)
    super().__init__(
        channels,
        feedback_size,
        input_size,
        bias=False,
        bias_scaling=0.0,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        seed=seed,
        device=device,
        dtype=dtype,
    )
    self._order = order
    self._memory_channels = channels
    self.reservoir_size = order * channels
    self._theta = theta
    self._dt = dt
    with torch.no_grad():
        if channels == total_width:
            encoder = torch.eye(
                channels, device=self.weight_feedback.device, dtype=self.weight_feedback.dtype
            )
            if feedback_initializer is None:
                self.weight_feedback.copy_(encoder[:, :feedback_size])
            if input_initializer is None and self.weight_input is not None:
                self.weight_input.copy_(encoder[:, feedback_size:])
        else:
            scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(total_width)
            if feedback_initializer is None:
                self.weight_feedback.mul_(scale)
            if input_initializer is None and self.weight_input is not None:
                self.weight_input.mul_(scale)
    # Half/bfloat matrix_exp is not numerically supported. Compute once in
    # float32 then cast; requested float64 remains float64 throughout.
    parameter_dtype = self.weight_feedback.dtype
    work_dtype = torch.float64 if parameter_dtype == torch.float64 else torch.float32
    i = torch.arange(order, device=self.weight_feedback.device)
    rows, columns = i[:, None], i[None, :]
    sign = torch.where((rows - columns + 1).remainder(2) == 0, 1.0, -1.0)
    A = ((2 * rows + 1).to(work_dtype) * torch.where(rows < columns, -1.0, sign)) / theta
    B = ((2 * i + 1).to(work_dtype) * torch.where(i.remainder(2) == 0, 1.0, -1.0)) / theta
    if not torch.isfinite(A).all() or not torch.isfinite(B).all():
        raise ValueError(
            "theta/order produce non-finite continuous memory dynamics in the requested dtype"
        )
    augmented = torch.zeros(order + 1, order + 1, device=A.device, dtype=work_dtype)
    augmented[:order, :order] = A
    augmented[:order, order] = B
    scaled = augmented * dt
    # A finite elementwise matrix can still overflow norm estimation or
    # require an unreasonable number of scaling/squaring iterations. Bound
    # the numerical work before entering the backend (which may otherwise
    # hang on Inf or extreme finite inputs). Ordinary memory-window ratios
    # are many orders below this limit.
    norm = torch.linalg.matrix_norm(scaled, ord=1)
    if not torch.isfinite(norm) or norm > 2**20:
        raise ValueError(
            "dt/theta/order exceed the supported ZOH matrix 1-norm (2**20); "
            "reduce dt/theta or order"
        )
    if order == 1:
        # The order-1 system is a scalar leaky integrator. Its closed form
        # also avoids roundoff in matrix_exp's small 2x2 approximation.
        exponent = A[0, 0] * dt
        discrete_A = exponent.exp().reshape(1, 1)
        discrete_B = -exponent.expm1().reshape(1)
    else:
        transition = torch.matrix_exp(scaled)
        discrete_A = transition[:order, :order]
        discrete_B = transition[:order, order]
    self.continuous_A: Tensor
    self.continuous_B: Tensor
    self.register_buffer("continuous_A", A.to(parameter_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("continuous_B", B.to(parameter_dtype))
    self.register_buffer("A", discrete_A.to(parameter_dtype).contiguous())
    self.register_buffer("B", discrete_B.to(parameter_dtype).contiguous())
    if any(
        not torch.isfinite(value).all()
        for value in (self.continuous_A, self.continuous_B, self.A, self.B)
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "theta/dt/order produce non-finite memory dynamics in the requested dtype"
        )
    self.trainable = trainable
    if device is not None and torch.device(device).type == "mps":
        self.to(device)

Advance one zero-order-hold interval and return readable and carried memory.

def step(self, projected_t: Tensor, state: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Advance one zero-order-hold interval and return readable and carried memory."""
    self._check_step(projected_t, state, self.memory_channels)
    memory = state.reshape(state.shape[0], self.memory_channels, self.order)
    new_memory = memory @ self.A.T + projected_t.unsqueeze(-1) * self.B
    output = new_memory.reshape(state.shape[0], self.state_size)
    return output, output

Bases: ReservoirCell

Use an existing nn.GRUCell or nn.LSTMCell in a ResDAG graph.

Deep-copies the supplied standard cell, preserving its parameters, device, and dtype. trainable=False freezes the copy; the caller's cell is never changed. Its input_size must equal feedback_size + (input_size or 0). Inputs are ordered feedback then optional driver. LSTM state is packed cat([h, c], -1) of width 2*hidden_size; GRU state is h. Both expose only h as output. This permits imported/pretrained cells and ordinary gradient training without requiring a separate RNN implementation.

Input gate projections are batched across the entire sequence; recurrent updates implement the documented PyTorch equations, including GRU's reset gate placement around the hidden new-gate projection and its bias. A frozen GRU/LSTM is not guaranteed to have the echo state property.

References: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.GRUCell.html and https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LSTMCell.html

def __init__(
    self,
    cell: nn.GRUCell | nn.LSTMCell,
    feedback_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    *,
    trainable: bool = False,
) -> None:

        raise TypeError("cell must be a standard torch.nn.GRUCell or torch.nn.LSTMCell")

def step(self, projected_t: Tensor, state: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Advance one projected frame and return hidden output and carried state."""
    self.validate_state(state)
    gates = 4 if self._is_lstm else 3
    if projected_t.ndim != 2 or projected_t.shape != (
        state.shape[0],
        gates * self.reservoir_size,
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Projected timestep must have shape (batch, {gates * self.reservoir_size})"
        )
    cell = self.recurrent_cell
    h = state[:, : self.reservoir_size]
    recurrent = F.linear(h, cell.weight_hh, cell.bias_hh)
    if self._is_lstm:
        i, f, g, o = (projected_t + recurrent).chunk(4, dim=-1)
        c = state[:, self.reservoir_size :]
        new_c = f.sigmoid() * c + i.sigmoid() * g.tanh()
        new_h = o.sigmoid() * new_c.tanh()
        return new_h, torch.cat((new_h, new_c), dim=-1)
    ir, iz, inn = projected_t.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    hr, hz, hn = recurrent.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    reset = (ir + hr).sigmoid()
    update = (iz + hz).sigmoid()
    candidate = (inn + reset * hn).tanh()
    # Match native arithmetic ordering, including promotion under autocast.
    new_h = candidate + update * (h - candidate)
    return new_h, new_h
