def deep_esn(
    reservoir_sizes: Sequence[int] | int,
    n_layers: int | None = None,
    feedback_size: int = 1,
    output_size: int = 1,
    *,
    concat_all_states: bool = True,
    interlayer_scaling: float = 0.5,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float | Sequence[float] = 1.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a Deep (hierarchical, stacked-reservoir) Echo State Network.

    Stacks `N` reservoir layers so that layer `i`'s state sequence is the
    feedback input of layer `i + 1`.  The readout, by default, is fitted on the
    **concatenation of all layers' states** — the standard DeepESN readout — so
    it can exploit the progressively slower, more structured memory timescales
    the deeper layers develop.  Set `concat_all_states=False` to read out from
    the last layer alone.

    Architecture (`concat_all_states=True`):

    ```text
    Input -> Reservoir_1 -> Reservoir_2 -> ... -> Reservoir_N
                 |              |                     |
                 +--------------+----- Concatenate ---+---> Readout
    ```

    Only the first layer receives the raw feedback; every subsequent layer's
    feedback dimension is the previous layer's `reservoir_size`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_sizes : sequence of int or int
        Per-layer reservoir sizes as a list (one entry per layer), or a single
        int broadcast to all `n_layers` layers.  When a single int is given,
        `n_layers` is required.
    n_layers : int or None, optional
        Number of stacked layers.  Required when `reservoir_sizes` is a single
        int; ignored (but must be consistent) when `reservoir_sizes` is a list.
    feedback_size : int, default=1
        Number of feedback features driving the *first* layer (the input
        dimension of the model).
    output_size : int, default=1
        Number of output features.  For autoregressive `forecast`, this
        must equal `feedback_size` (the first model output is fed back).
    concat_all_states : bool, default=True
        When `True` (the standard DeepESN readout) the readout sees the
        concatenation of every layer's state, so its `in_features` is
        `sum(reservoir_sizes)`.  When `False` the readout sees only the last
        layer's state, so `in_features` is `reservoir_sizes[-1]`.
    interlayer_scaling : float, default=0.5
        Magnitude of the inter-layer coupling weights (layers `2..N`).  Each
        deeper layer's feedback is the *previous layer's high-dimensional state*,
        so the default `uniform(-1, 1)` feedback weights would over-saturate the
        `tanh`; scaling them down (via a `uniform(-interlayer_scaling, interlayer_scaling)` initializer) keeps the deeper reservoirs in their
        useful dynamic range.  Applied only when `feedback_initializer` is left
        as `None`; an explicit `feedback_initializer` is used verbatim on
        every layer and this knob is ignored.  The first layer always uses the raw
        (unscaled) input path.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights, shared by every layer.  Accepts a
        registry name, a `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights of every layer.
    leak_rate : float or sequence of float, default=1.0
        Leaky-integration rate.  A scalar is shared by every layer; a list (one
        entry per layer) sets a per-layer schedule.  The DeepESN literature
        recommends leak rates that **decrease with depth** — fast dynamics near
        the input, slow dynamics deep in the stack — e.g.
        `leak_rate=[1.0, 0.7, 0.4]` for a 3-layer network.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights, shared by every layer.  Same
        accepted forms as `topology`.
    activation : str, default="tanh"
        Activation function for every layer (`"tanh"`, `"relu"`,
        `"sigmoid"`, `"identity"`).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether every reservoir layer uses a bias term.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regression regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the readout uses a bias term.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to **every**
        `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        The assembled deep ESN, ready for training and forecasting.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the layer stack is empty, a reservoir size is not a positive integer,
        `reservoir_sizes` is a scalar without `n_layers`, the per-layer
        `leak_rate` schedule length does not match the number of layers, or
        `output_size` is not a positive integer.

    Notes
    -----
    The stack is *untrained* like a standard ESN — depth adds temporal richness
    without any extra gradient training; only the readout is fitted (by ridge
    regression).  Depth is not a free win over a single wide reservoir: on a
    short, single-timescale task (e.g. a brief Lorenz-63 window) a single
    `classic_esn` of the combined width usually forecasts *further*, because
    one large reservoir already spans the needed dynamics.  DeepESN pays off on
    **multi-timescale / hierarchical** signals — where a decreasing-with-depth
    leak schedule (see `leak_rate` below) lets successive layers specialise on
    progressively slower dynamics (Gallicchio & Micheli 2017; the layer-specific
    time-scale separation of Frontiers in AI 2024).  Reach for it when the signal
    has structure at several timescales, not as a drop-in replacement for a wide
    ESN.

    Examples
    --------
    A 3-layer stack of equal width with a decreasing-with-depth leak schedule::

    >>> from resdag.models import deep_esn
    >>> model = deep_esn(
    ...     reservoir_sizes=300,
    ...     n_layers=3,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     leak_rate=[1.0, 0.6, 0.3],
    ...     spectral_radius=0.9,
    ... )

    Explicit per-layer sizes (narrowing with depth), reading out from the last
    layer only::

    >>> model = deep_esn(
    ...     reservoir_sizes=[400, 200, 100],
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     concat_all_states=False,
    ... )

    Training and forecasting are identical to any other premade model::

    >>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
    >>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
    >>> trainer.fit(
    ...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
    ...     train_inputs=(train,),
    ...     targets={"output": target},
    ... )
    >>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup, horizon=500)

    See Also
    --------
    classic_esn : Single-reservoir ESN with input concatenation.
    hybrid_esn : Physics-prior hybrid ESN.
    resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting the readout.
    """
    sizes = _resolve_reservoir_sizes(reservoir_sizes, n_layers)
    leak_rates = _broadcast_leak_rates(leak_rate, len(sizes))

    if not isinstance(output_size, int) or output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"deep_esn: output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}.")

    # Resolve the readout spec up front so an invalid one fails before any
    # partial construction.

    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )

    # Build the stack: layer i takes the previous layer's state as its feedback,
    # so its feedback dimension is the previous reservoir_size (feedback_size for
    # the first layer). Collect every layer's state for the concat-all readout.
    layer_states = []
    prev_output = inp
    prev_feedback_size = feedback_size
    for i, (size, layer_leak) in enumerate(zip(sizes, leak_rates)):
        # First layer sees the raw input (user's feedback_initializer); deeper
        # layers see a high-dimensional reservoir state, so scale their coupling
        # down (unless the user pinned an explicit feedback_initializer).
        if i == 0 or feedback_initializer is not None:
            layer_feedback_init = feedback_initializer
        else:
            layer_feedback_init = (
                "uniform",
                {"low": -interlayer_scaling, "high": interlayer_scaling},
            )
        state = ESNLayer(
            reservoir_size=size,
            feedback_size=prev_feedback_size,
            topology=topology,
            spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
            leak_rate=layer_leak,
            feedback_initializer=layer_feedback_init,
            activation=activation,
            bias=bias,
            trainable=trainable,
            **reservoir_kwargs,
        )(prev_output)
        layer_states.append(state)
        prev_output = state
        prev_feedback_size = size

    # Standard DeepESN readout: concatenate every layer's state. When
    # concat_all_states is False, read out from the last layer alone.
    if concat_all_states and len(layer_states) > 1:
        features = Concatenate()(*layer_states)
        readout_in_features = sum(sizes)
    else:
        features = layer_states[-1]
        readout_in_features = sizes[-1]

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device"), dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"))(features)

    return ESNModel(inp, readout_layer)

    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    epsilon: float = 0.01,
    gamma: float = 0.01,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    substeps: int = 1,
    solver: str = "euler",
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",

) -> ESNModel

Build an Euler State Network (EuSN) model.

EuSN (Gallicchio, arXiv:2203.09382) replaces the leaky-ESN state update with one forward-Euler step of an ODE whose recurrent matrix is antisymmetric (norm-preserving) minus a small diffusion term:

\[ h_t = h_{t-1} + \varepsilon\, \tanh\!\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\, h_{t-1} + \cdots\big). \]

Small \(\varepsilon\) and \(\gamma\) sit the reservoir near the edge of stability (non-dissipative, long memory). This factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as resdag.models.classic_esn:

Input -> EuSN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of units in the reservoir.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).

TYPE: int

output_size

Number of output features.

TYPE: int

epsilon

Forward-Euler step size \(\varepsilon\). Smaller values sit the reservoir closer to the edge of stability (longer, near-lossless memory).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.01

gamma

Diffusion coefficient \(\gamma \ge 0\) damping the Euler discretization error. 0.0 recovers the undamped antisymmetric flow.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.01

input_size

Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver is kept out of the input concatenation. None (default) builds a feedback-only model.

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

input_initializer

Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

topology

Topology for the recurrent weights W_r (antisymmetrized on the fly by the cell). Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target rotation rate for W_r (largest imaginary-eigenvalue magnitude of the antisymmetric part).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

substeps

Fixed integration sub-steps per interval. 1 is the single forward-Euler step of the paper.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1

solver

Integration scheme. 'euler' is the paper's method; 'rk4' and the adaptive 'torchdiffeq' (requires resdag[ode]) integrate the same field more accurately.

TYPE: (euler, rk4, torchdiffeq) DEFAULT: 'euler'

feedback_initializer

Initializer for the feedback weights.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

activation

Activation of the vector field (tanh is the EuSN choice).

TYPE: (tanh, relu, sigmoid, identity) DEFAULT: 'tanh'

bias

Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

readout

A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

readout_alpha

Ridge regularization for the readout.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

readout_bias

Whether to use a bias in the readout.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout_name

Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

readout_kwargs

Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

**reservoir_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer (e.g. bias_scaling, seed, torchdiffeq_method).

TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION `resdag.core.ESNModel`

Configured EuSN model ready for training and inference.

Examples:

>>> from resdag.models import eusn
>>> model = eusn(
...     reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3,
...     epsilon=0.01, gamma=0.01,
... )

    output_size: int,
    epsilon: float = 0.01,
    gamma: float = 0.01,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    substeps: int = 1,
    solver: str = "euler",
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    r"""Build an Euler State Network (EuSN) model.

    EuSN (Gallicchio, arXiv:2203.09382) replaces the leaky-ESN state update with
    one forward-Euler step of an ODE whose recurrent matrix is antisymmetric
    (norm-preserving) minus a small diffusion term:

    $$
    h_t = h_{t-1} + \varepsilon\,
          \tanh\!\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\, h_{t-1} + \cdots\big).
    $$

    Small $\varepsilon$ and $\gamma$ sit the reservoir near the edge
    of stability (non-dissipative, long memory).  This factory wires the same
    input-concatenation architecture as `resdag.models.classic_esn`:

    ```text
    Input -> EuSN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    epsilon : float, default=0.01
        Forward-Euler step size $\varepsilon$.  Smaller values sit the
        reservoir closer to the edge of stability (longer, near-lossless
        memory).
    gamma : float, default=0.01
        Diffusion coefficient $\gamma \ge 0$ damping the Euler
        discretization error.  `0.0` recovers the undamped antisymmetric flow.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver is kept out of
        the input concatenation.  `None` (default) builds a feedback-only
        model.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when
        `input_size` is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights `W_r` (antisymmetrized on the fly
        by the cell).  Accepts a registry name, a `(name, params)` tuple, a
        callable, or a pre-configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target rotation rate for `W_r` (largest imaginary-eigenvalue magnitude
        of the antisymmetric part).
    substeps : int, default=1
        Fixed integration sub-steps per interval.  `1` is the single
        forward-Euler step of the paper.
    solver : {'euler', 'rk4', 'torchdiffeq'}, default='euler'
        Integration scheme.  `'euler'` is the paper's method; `'rk4'` and
        the adaptive `'torchdiffeq'` (requires `resdag[ode]`) integrate the
        same field more accurately.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights.
    activation : {'tanh', 'relu', 'sigmoid', 'identity'}, default='tanh'
        Activation of the vector field (`tanh` is the EuSN choice).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer` (e.g. `bias_scaling`,
        `seed`, `torchdiffeq_method`).

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured EuSN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import eusn
    >>> model = eusn(
    ...     reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3,
    ...     epsilon=0.01, gamma=0.01,
    ... )

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.es2n : Edge-of-Stability State Network (discrete orthogonal skip).
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer : The reservoir layer.
    """
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=None,
        concat_input=True,
        input_size=input_size,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        reservoir_cls=EuSNLayer,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        readout=readout,
        readout_alpha=readout_alpha,
        readout_bias=readout_bias,
        readout_name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
        epsilon=epsilon,
        gamma=gamma,
        substeps=substeps,
        solver=solver,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

gated_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,

    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

Build a gated ("reservoir GRU") ESN model.

The reservoir is a frozen (or trainable) LiGRU-style gated recurrent cell. The raw input is concatenated with the reservoir output before the readout, following the classic-ESN wiring:

Input -> GatedReservoirLayer -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of units in the reservoir.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Number of feedback features (input dimension).

TYPE: int

output_size

Number of output features.

TYPE: int

input_size

Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver feeds the reservoir but is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout in_features stays feedback_size + reservoir_size.

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

input_initializer

Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

topology

Topology for the recurrent candidate weight. The update-gate recurrent weight is always dense-random.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Desired spectral radius for the recurrent candidate weight.

update_gate_bias

Retention bias on the update gate (keeps a frozen gated reservoir from washing out its memory). See resdag.layers.cells.gated_cell.GatedReservoirCell.

activation

Candidate nonlinearity (LiGRU default is "relu").

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "relu"

Update-gate nonlinearity.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "sigmoid"

feedback_initializer

Initializer for feedback weights.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

bias

Whether to use gate biases in the reservoir.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether reservoir weights are trainable. A frozen gated reservoir often underperforms an ESN; True (BPTT through the gates) is frequently the more useful setting. Note the ReLU candidate is unbounded, so a frozen autoregressive forecast that drifts off the attractor can grow large in magnitude (not merely track poorly) — prefer trainable=True for closed-loop forecasting.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

concat_input

Whether to concatenate the raw input with the reservoir output before the readout.

readout

A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

readout_alpha

Ridge regularization for the readout.

readout_bias

Whether to use bias in the readout.

readout_name

Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

**reservoir_kwargs

If readout is neither a known string key nor a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass.

>>> model = gated_esn(200, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, trainable=True)

def gated_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    update_gate_bias: float = 2.0,
    activation: str = "relu",
    gate_activation: str = "sigmoid",
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    concat_input: bool = True,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a gated ("reservoir GRU") ESN model.

    The reservoir is a frozen (or trainable) LiGRU-style gated recurrent cell.
    The raw input is concatenated with the reservoir output before the readout,
    following the classic-ESN wiring:

    ```text
    Input -> GatedReservoirLayer -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver feeds the
        reservoir but is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout
        `in_features` stays `feedback_size + reservoir_size`.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when `input_size`
        is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent **candidate** weight.  The update-gate
        recurrent weight is always dense-random.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Desired spectral radius for the recurrent candidate weight.
    update_gate_bias : float, default=2.0
        Retention bias on the update gate (keeps a frozen gated reservoir from
        washing out its memory).  See
        `resdag.layers.cells.gated_cell.GatedReservoirCell`.
    activation : str, default="relu"
        Candidate nonlinearity (LiGRU default is `"relu"`).
    gate_activation : str, default="sigmoid"
        Update-gate nonlinearity.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for feedback weights.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use gate biases in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether reservoir weights are trainable.  A frozen gated reservoir often
        underperforms an ESN; `True` (BPTT through the gates) is frequently the
        more useful setting.  Note the ReLU candidate is unbounded, so a *frozen*
        autoregressive forecast that drifts off the attractor can grow large in
        magnitude (not merely track poorly) — prefer `trainable=True` for
        closed-loop forecasting.
    concat_input : bool, default=True
        Whether to concatenate the raw input with the reservoir output before the
        readout.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.gated.GatedReservoirLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured gated ESN model ready for training and inference.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `output_size` is not a positive integer, or `readout` is an
        unknown string key.
    TypeError
        If `readout` is neither a known string key nor a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass.

    Examples
    --------
    Trainable gated ESN on a 3-D signal:

    >>> from resdag.models import gated_esn
    >>> model = gated_esn(200, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, trainable=True)

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.classic_esn : The ungated classic ESN with the same wiring.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.gated.GatedReservoirLayer : The gated reservoir layer.
    """
    if output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}")

    # Resolve the readout up front so an invalid spec fails before construction.

    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )
    driver = (
        reservoir_input(
            input_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
        )
        if input_size
        else None
    )

    reservoir = GatedReservoirLayer(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        input_size=input_size,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        update_gate_bias=update_gate_bias,
        activation=activation,
        gate_activation=gate_activation,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    output: SymbolicTensor = reservoir(inp) if driver is None else reservoir(inp, driver)
    model_inputs = inp if driver is None else [inp, driver]

    if concat_input:
        output = Concatenate()(inp, output)
        readout_in_features = feedback_size + reservoir_size
    else:
        readout_in_features = reservoir_size

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir.weight_feedback.device, dtype=reservoir.weight_feedback.dtype)(output)

    return ESNModel(model_inputs, readout_layer)

docs.title: KnowledgeModel
docs.text:
KnowledgeModel(fn: KnowledgeFn | Module, model_out_size: int)

Bases: Module

Wrap a knowledge-based expert f(u) -> u_next as a DAG layer.

Adapts an arbitrary one-step-ahead predictor — a plain callable or another torch.nn.Module (e.g. one Euler/RK step of an approximate ODE) — so it slots into a pytorch_symbolic model and is re-evaluated on the current feedback at every timestep, including the autoregressive forecast loop where the reservoir feeds the model its own previous prediction.

The wrapped callable is applied directly to the (batch, time, features) (or single-step (batch, 1, features)) tensor and must broadcast over the leading batch/time axes, operating feature-wise on the last dimension — the standard PyTorch idiom. Its output feature dimension, model_out_size, may differ from the input dimension (though it is typically equal, since the expert predicts the next state).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION fn

The knowledge model. Called as fn(u) with u of shape (batch, time, features) and must return a tensor of shape (batch, time, model_out_size) — i.e. it may change only the last (feature) dimension. A crude approximate integrator is enough; it does not need to be accurate, only informative.

TYPE: callable or Module

model_out_size

Feature dimension of fn's output. Used by hybrid_esn to size the concatenations and the informed input split; validated at call time.

TYPE: int

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION fn

The wrapped knowledge model. Registered as a submodule when it is an torch.nn.Module, so its parameters/buffers move with .to().

TYPE: callable or Module

model_out_size

The declared output feature dimension.

TYPE: int

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

At forward time, if fn's output rank does not match its input or its last dimension is not model_out_size.

Examples:

A rough Lorenz-63 Euler step used as a physics prior::

>>> import torch
>>> from resdag.models import KnowledgeModel
>>> def lorenz_euler(u, dt=0.02, sigma=10.0, rho=28.0, beta=8.0 / 3.0):
...     x, y, z = u[..., 0], u[..., 1], u[..., 2]
...     dx = sigma * (y - x)
...     dy = x * (rho - z) - y
...     dz = x * y - beta * z
...     return u + dt * torch.stack([dx, dy, dz], dim=-1)
>>> expert = KnowledgeModel(lorenz_euler, model_out_size=3)
>>> u = torch.randn(4, 50, 3)
>>> expert(u).shape
torch.Size([4, 50, 3])
See Also

hybrid_esn : The factory that wires this expert into a hybrid ESN.

RAISES DESCRIPTION TypeError

If fn is not callable.

ValueError

If model_out_size is not a positive integer.

Source code in src/resdag/models/hybrid_esn.py 
def __init__(self, fn: KnowledgeFn | nn.Module, model_out_size: int) -> None:
    """Store the callable and its declared output dimension.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `fn` is not callable.
    ValueError
        If `model_out_size` is not a positive integer.
    """
    super().__init__()
    if not callable(fn):
        raise TypeError(f"KnowledgeModel: fn must be callable, got {type(fn).__name__}.")
    if not isinstance(model_out_size, int) or model_out_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"KnowledgeModel: model_out_size must be a positive integer, "
            f"got {model_out_size!r}."
        )
    # Registering an nn.Module submodule under ``fn`` means its parameters and
    # buffers are discovered by ``.parameters()`` / moved by ``.to(...)``. A
    # plain callable is stored as a bare attribute (no parameters to track).
    self.fn = fn
    self.model_out_size = model_out_size

    """Apply the knowledge model to the current state `u`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    u : torch.Tensor
        Current state of shape `(batch, time, features)` (or the single-step
        `(batch, 1, features)` slice used during autoregressive forecasting).

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        The one-step-ahead prediction of shape
        `(batch, time, model_out_size)`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the wrapped model's output rank differs from `u` or its last
        dimension is not `model_out_size`.
    """
    out = self.fn(u)
    if out.shape[:-1] != u.shape[:-1] or out.shape[-1] != self.model_out_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"KnowledgeModel: fn(u) must return shape "
            f"{(*u.shape[:-1], self.model_out_size)} (same batch/time as the "
            f"input, last dim = model_out_size={self.model_out_size}); got "
            f"{tuple(out.shape)} for input {tuple(u.shape)}."
        )
    return out

hybrid_esn(
    knowledge_model: KnowledgeModel | KnowledgeFn | Module,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    *,
    model_out_size: int | None = None,
    gamma: float = 0.5,
    input_scaling: float = 0.1,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

Build a hybrid physics-prior ESN (Pathak et al. 2018).

Combines a reservoir with an imperfect knowledge-based expert K. The expert's one-step-ahead prediction K(u) is concatenated with the raw input to drive the reservoir, and concatenated with the reservoir state before the readout, so the reservoir only has to learn the residual the expert gets wrong.

Architecture:

             +---------------- K(u) --------------------+
             |                                          |
Input -- u --+--> Concatenate([u, K(u)]) --> Reservoir  |
                                                 |       v
                                                 +--> Concatenate([h, K(u)]) --> Readout

The reservoir's input weights use the informed split (resdag.init.input_feedback.InformedInputInitializer): a fraction gamma of the units are wired to the raw-state block u and 1 - gamma to the knowledge-model block K(u).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION knowledge_model

The knowledge-based expert. A bare callable / torch.nn.Module f(u) -> u_next is wrapped in a KnowledgeModel automatically (using model_out_size, defaulting to feedback_size); pass a pre-built KnowledgeModel to control its declared output size.

TYPE: KnowledgeModel, callable, or torch.nn.Module

reservoir_size

Number of units in the reservoir.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Number of feedback features (the input dimension of the model, u).

TYPE: int

output_size

Number of output features. For autoregressive forecast this must equal feedback_size (the first model output is fed back as u).

TYPE: int

model_out_size

Feature dimension of the knowledge model's output. Only used when knowledge_model is a bare callable (to build the wrapper); ignored when a KnowledgeModel is passed (its own model_out_size is used). Defaults to feedback_size (the usual case: the expert predicts the next full state).

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

gamma

Fraction of reservoir units wired to the raw-state block u by the informed input split; 1 - gamma are wired to the K(u) block. Must lie in [0, 1]. gamma near 1 weights the reservoir toward the raw state, near 0 toward the knowledge model.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.5

input_scaling

Half-width of the informed input weights: each nonzero entry is drawn uniformly from [-input_scaling, input_scaling].

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.1

topology

Topology for the recurrent weights. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

leak_rate

Leaky-integration rate (1.0 = no leak).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

activation

Activation function ("tanh", "relu", "sigmoid", "identity").

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "tanh"

bias

Whether the reservoir uses a bias term.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

readout

A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

readout_alpha

Ridge regression regularization for the readout.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

readout_bias

Whether the readout uses a bias term.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout_name

Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

readout_kwargs

Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

**reservoir_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.ESNLayer.

TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION `resdag.core.ESNModel`

The assembled hybrid ESN, ready for training and forecasting.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If output_size is not a positive integer, or (via the informed initializer) if the wiring dimensions are inconsistent.

Notes

The reservoir's feedback_size is feedback_size + model_out_size because it consumes the concatenation [u, K(u)]; the model's input dimension stays feedback_size (K(u) is computed inside the graph). The readout in_features is reservoir_size + model_out_size (it sees [h, K(u)]). During autoregressive forecast, only the readout output is fed back as the next u; K is re-evaluated on it every step, so the physics prior stays live throughout the rollout.

Examples:

A rough Lorenz Euler step as the physics prior::

>>> import torch
>>> from resdag.models import hybrid_esn
>>> def lorenz_euler(u, dt=0.02, sigma=10.0, rho=28.0, beta=8.0 / 3.0):
...     x, y, z = u[..., 0], u[..., 1], u[..., 2]
...     dx = sigma * (y - x)
...     dy = x * (rho - z) - y
...     dz = x * y - beta * z
...     return u + dt * torch.stack([dx, dy, dz], dim=-1)
>>> model = hybrid_esn(
...     lorenz_euler,
...     reservoir_size=400,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     gamma=0.5,
... )

Training and forecasting are identical to any other premade model::

>>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
>>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
...     train_inputs=(train,),
...     targets={"output": target},
... )
>>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup, horizon=500)
See Also

KnowledgeModel : The expert wrapper used here. resdag.init.input_feedback.InformedInputInitializer : The informed input split. deep_esn : Stacked (hierarchical) reservoirs.

def hybrid_esn(
    knowledge_model: KnowledgeModel | KnowledgeFn | nn.Module,
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    *,
    model_out_size: int | None = None,
    gamma: float = 0.5,
    input_scaling: float = 0.1,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a hybrid physics-prior ESN (Pathak et al. 2018).

    Combines a reservoir with an imperfect knowledge-based expert `K`.  The
    expert's one-step-ahead prediction `K(u)` is concatenated with the raw
    input to drive the reservoir, **and** concatenated with the reservoir state
    before the readout, so the reservoir only has to learn the residual the
    expert gets wrong.

    Architecture:

    ```text
                 +---------------- K(u) --------------------+
                 |                                          |
    Input -- u --+--> Concatenate([u, K(u)]) --> Reservoir  |
                                                     |       v
                                                     +--> Concatenate([h, K(u)]) --> Readout
    ```

    The reservoir's input weights use the informed split
    (`resdag.init.input_feedback.InformedInputInitializer`): a fraction
    `gamma` of the units are wired to the raw-state block `u` and `1 - gamma`
    to the knowledge-model block `K(u)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    knowledge_model : KnowledgeModel, callable, or torch.nn.Module
        The knowledge-based expert.  A bare callable / `torch.nn.Module`
        `f(u) -> u_next` is wrapped in a `KnowledgeModel` automatically
        (using `model_out_size`, defaulting to `feedback_size`); pass a
        pre-built `KnowledgeModel` to control its declared output size.
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (the input dimension of the model, `u`).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.  For autoregressive `forecast` this must
        equal `feedback_size` (the first model output is fed back as `u`).
    model_out_size : int or None, optional
        Feature dimension of the knowledge model's output.  Only used when
        `knowledge_model` is a bare callable (to build the wrapper); ignored when
        a `KnowledgeModel` is passed (its own `model_out_size` is used).
        Defaults to `feedback_size` (the usual case: the expert predicts the
        next full state).
    gamma : float, default=0.5
        Fraction of reservoir units wired to the raw-state block `u` by the
        informed input split; `1 - gamma` are wired to the `K(u)` block.  Must
        lie in `[0, 1]`.  `gamma` near `1` weights the reservoir toward the
        raw state, near `0` toward the knowledge model.
    input_scaling : float, default=0.1
        Half-width of the informed input weights: each nonzero entry is drawn
        uniformly from `[-input_scaling, input_scaling]`.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights.  Accepts a registry name, a
        `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights.
    leak_rate : float, default=1.0
        Leaky-integration rate (1.0 = no leak).
    activation : str, default="tanh"
        Activation function (`"tanh"`, `"relu"`, `"sigmoid"`,
        `"identity"`).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the reservoir uses a bias term.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regression regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the readout uses a bias term.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        The assembled hybrid ESN, ready for training and forecasting.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `output_size` is not a positive integer, or (via the informed
        initializer) if the wiring dimensions are inconsistent.

    Notes
    -----
    The reservoir's `feedback_size` is `feedback_size + model_out_size`
    because it consumes the concatenation `[u, K(u)]`; the *model's* input
    dimension stays `feedback_size` (`K(u)` is computed inside the graph).
    The readout `in_features` is `reservoir_size + model_out_size` (it sees
    `[h, K(u)]`).  During autoregressive `forecast`, only the readout
    output is fed back as the next `u`; `K` is re-evaluated on it every step,
    so the physics prior stays live throughout the rollout.

    Examples
    --------
    A rough Lorenz Euler step as the physics prior::

    >>> import torch
    >>> from resdag.models import hybrid_esn
    >>> def lorenz_euler(u, dt=0.02, sigma=10.0, rho=28.0, beta=8.0 / 3.0):
    ...     x, y, z = u[..., 0], u[..., 1], u[..., 2]
    ...     dx = sigma * (y - x)
    ...     dy = x * (rho - z) - y
    ...     dz = x * y - beta * z
    ...     return u + dt * torch.stack([dx, dy, dz], dim=-1)
    >>> model = hybrid_esn(
    ...     lorenz_euler,
    ...     reservoir_size=400,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     gamma=0.5,
    ... )

    Training and forecasting are identical to any other premade model::

    >>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
    >>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
    >>> trainer.fit(
    ...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
    ...     train_inputs=(train,),
    ...     targets={"output": target},
    ... )
    >>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup, horizon=500)

    See Also
    --------
    KnowledgeModel : The expert wrapper used here.
    resdag.init.input_feedback.InformedInputInitializer : The informed input split.
    deep_esn : Stacked (hierarchical) reservoirs.
    """
    if not isinstance(output_size, int) or output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"hybrid_esn: output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}."
        )

    # Wrap a bare callable/Module in a KnowledgeModel; a pre-built one is used
    # as-is (its own model_out_size wins). The expert predicts the next state, so
    # model_out_size defaults to feedback_size.
    if isinstance(knowledge_model, KnowledgeModel):
        expert = knowledge_model
    else:
        expert = KnowledgeModel(
            knowledge_model,
            model_out_size=model_out_size if model_out_size is not None else feedback_size,
        )
    model_out = expert.model_out_size
    expert.to(device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device"), dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"))

    # Resolve the readout spec up front so an invalid one fails before any
    # partial construction.

    # The model input u has dimension feedback_size; K(u) is computed in-graph, so
    # it is re-evaluated on the model's own output each autoregressive step.
    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )
    k = expert(inp)  # (batch, time, model_out)

    # Pre-reservoir: drive the reservoir with [u, K(u)].
    reservoir_in = Concatenate()(inp, k)
    reservoir_feedback_size = feedback_size + model_out

    # Informed input split: the first ``feedback_size`` columns are the raw-state
    # block, the trailing ``model_out`` columns the knowledge-model block. gamma is
    # the fraction of units wired to the state block.
    feedback_initializer = (
        "informed_init",
        {"model_in_size": model_out, "gamma": gamma, "input_scaling": input_scaling},
    )

    reservoir_state = ESNLayer(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=reservoir_feedback_size,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        leak_rate=leak_rate,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )(reservoir_in)

    # Pre-readout: the readout sees [h, K(u)].
    readout_in = Concatenate()(reservoir_state, k)
    readout_in_features = reservoir_size + model_out

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device"), dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"))(readout_in)

    return ESNModel(inp, readout_layer)

def linear_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build an ESN model with no readout layer and a linear activation function.

    This model uses a linear activation function in the reservoir, which can be
    useful for studying linear dynamics or as a baseline for comparison with
    nonlinear reservoirs.

    Architecture:
        Input -> Reservoir(activation='identity') (output)

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for recurrent weights. Accepts:
        - str: Registry name (e.g., "erdos_renyi")
        - tuple: (name, params) like ("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1})
        - GraphTopology: Pre-configured object
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Desired spectral radius for recurrent weights.
    leak_rate : float, default=1.0
        Leaky integration rate (1.0 = no leak).
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for feedback weights.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether reservoir weights are trainable.
    **reservoir_kwargs
        Additional keyword arguments passed to ESNLayer.  `activation` is not
        accepted here: `linear_esn` forces `activation="identity"` by design.

    Returns
    -------
    ESNModel
        ESN model with linear reservoir activation.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `activation` is passed via `reservoir_kwargs`.  `linear_esn`
        forces a linear (identity) activation by design, so overriding it is
        not allowed.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import linear_esn
    >>> model = linear_esn(100, 1)
    >>> linear_states = model(input_data)
    """
    # Linear: reservoir output only, no readout, identity activation forced.
    # Forbid an explicit ``activation`` override rather than letting it collide
    # with the hardcoded ``activation="identity"`` below (which would otherwise
    # raise a cryptic "multiple values for keyword argument 'activation'").
    if "activation" in reservoir_kwargs:
        raise ValueError(
            "linear_esn forces activation='identity'; do not pass activation="
            f"{reservoir_kwargs['activation']!r}. Use a different premade model "
            "(e.g. headless_esn) for a nonlinear reservoir without a readout."
        )

    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=None,
        augment=None,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        leak_rate=leak_rate,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation="identity",  # Force linear activation
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

Build a spiking Liquid State Machine (LSM) model.

The reservoir is a recurrent network of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons (resdag.layers.reservoirs.lif.LIFReservoirLayer); its real-valued synaptic-trace output is concatenated with the raw input and read out by a ridge regression, following the classic-ESN wiring:

Input -> LIFReservoirLayer -> Concatenate(Input, trace) -> Readout

Important.

This is an input-driven reservoir (Maass 2002), not a closed-loop chaos forecaster — the reservoir output is a filtered spike trace, not the feedback variable, so it cannot autoregress on itself. Its use is driven regression / classification, where a readout maps the filtered liquid state to a target. For autoregressive chaotic forecasting use resdag.models.ott_esn, resdag.models.classic_esn, or resdag.models.es2n. Continuous inputs enter as injected current.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of spiking units in the liquid.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Number of input features driving the reservoir.

TYPE: int

output_size

Number of output (target) features.

TYPE: int

input_size

Dimension of an optional second driving input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver feeds the reservoir but is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout in_features stays feedback_size + reservoir_size.

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

input_initializer

Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

tau_mem

Membrane time constant \(\tau_\text{mem}\) (in units of dt). Sets the membrane decay \(\beta = e^{-\Delta t/\tau_\text{mem}}\) — longer values give longer fading memory.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 20.0

tau_syn

Synaptic time constant \(\tau_\text{syn}\). Only used when synaptic_current=True (CuBa-LIF).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 10.0

dt

Integration timestep \(\Delta t\).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

synaptic_current

If True, use the second-order current-based LIF (CuBa-LIF), which adds an explicit synaptic-current state and smoother temporal filtering.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

v_threshold

Firing threshold.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

reset

Membrane reset on a spike (soft subtract vs hard zero).

TYPE: (subtract, zero) DEFAULT: 'subtract'

surrogate_beta

Fast-sigmoid surrogate slope for the straight-through spike gradient (only matters when trainable=True).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 10.0

trace_decay

Decay \(\kappa\) of the low-pass readout trace \(r_t = \kappa r_{t-1} + s_t\) — the real-valued signal the readout regresses on.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

topology

Topology for the recurrent spike-coupling weight W_rec. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target spectral radius for W_rec (recurrent spike-coupling strength).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

feedback_initializer

Initializer for the feedback weights.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

bias

Whether to use a bias current in the reservoir.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether the reservoir weights are trainable (via the surrogate spike gradient). A frozen liquid + fitted readout is the classic LSM; set True to fine-tune the liquid with SGD.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

concat_input

Whether to concatenate the raw input with the reservoir trace before the readout.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout

def lsm(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir (LIF) params
    tau_mem: float = 20.0,
    tau_syn: float = 10.0,
    dt: float = 1.0,
    synaptic_current: bool = False,
    v_threshold: float = 1.0,
    reset: str = "subtract",
    surrogate_beta: float = 10.0,
    trace_decay: float = 0.9,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    concat_input: bool = True,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    r"""Build a spiking Liquid State Machine (LSM) model.

    The reservoir is a recurrent network of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons
    (`resdag.layers.reservoirs.lif.LIFReservoirLayer`); its real-valued
    synaptic-trace output is concatenated with the raw input and read out by a
    ridge regression, following the classic-ESN wiring:

    ```text
    Input -> LIFReservoirLayer -> Concatenate(Input, trace) -> Readout
    ```

    **Important.**

    This is an **input-driven** reservoir (Maass 2002), *not* a closed-loop
    chaos forecaster — the reservoir output is a filtered spike trace, not the
    feedback variable, so it cannot autoregress on itself. Its use is driven
    regression / classification, where a readout maps the filtered liquid
    state to a target. For autoregressive chaotic forecasting use
    `resdag.models.ott_esn`, `resdag.models.classic_esn`, or
    `resdag.models.es2n`. Continuous inputs enter as injected current.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of spiking units in the liquid.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of input features driving the reservoir.
    output_size : int
        Number of output (target) features.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional second driving input.  When given, the model
        takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver feeds the reservoir
        but is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout
        `in_features` stays `feedback_size + reservoir_size`.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when `input_size`
        is given.
    tau_mem : float, default=20.0
        Membrane time constant $\tau_\text{mem}$ (in units of `dt`).
        Sets the membrane decay $\beta = e^{-\Delta t/\tau_\text{mem}}$ —
        longer values give longer fading memory.
    tau_syn : float, default=10.0
        Synaptic time constant $\tau_\text{syn}$.  Only used when
        `synaptic_current=True` (CuBa-LIF).
    dt : float, default=1.0
        Integration timestep $\Delta t$.
    synaptic_current : bool, default=False
        If `True`, use the second-order current-based LIF (CuBa-LIF), which
        adds an explicit synaptic-current state and smoother temporal filtering.
    v_threshold : float, default=1.0
        Firing threshold.
    reset : {'subtract', 'zero'}, default='subtract'
        Membrane reset on a spike (soft subtract vs hard zero).
    surrogate_beta : float, default=10.0
        Fast-sigmoid surrogate slope for the straight-through spike gradient
        (only matters when `trainable=True`).
    trace_decay : float, default=0.9
        Decay $\kappa$ of the low-pass readout trace
        $r_t = \kappa r_{t-1} + s_t$ — the real-valued signal the readout
        regresses on.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent spike-coupling weight `W_rec`.  Accepts a
        registry name, a `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for `W_rec` (recurrent spike-coupling strength).
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias current in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable (via the surrogate spike
        gradient).  A frozen liquid + fitted readout is the classic LSM; set
        `True` to fine-tune the liquid with SGD.
    concat_input : bool, default=True
        Whether to concatenate the raw input with the reservoir trace before the
        readout.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.lif.LIFReservoirLayer` (e.g. `bias_scaling`,
        `seed`, `input_initializer`).

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured LSM model ready for driven training and inference.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `output_size` is not a positive integer, or `readout` is an
        unknown string key.
    TypeError
        If `readout` is neither a known string key nor a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import lsm
    >>> model = lsm(reservoir_size=300, feedback_size=1, output_size=1, seed=0)

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN with the same wiring.
    resdag.models.eusn : Euler State Network (another input-driven reservoir).
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.lif.LIFReservoirLayer : The spiking reservoir layer.
    """
    if output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}")

    # Resolve the readout up front so an invalid spec fails before construction.

    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )
    driver = (
        reservoir_input(
            input_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
        )
        if input_size
        else None
    )

    reservoir = LIFReservoirLayer(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        input_size=input_size,
        tau_mem=tau_mem,
        tau_syn=tau_syn,
        dt=dt,
        synaptic_current=synaptic_current,
        v_threshold=v_threshold,
        reset=reset,
        surrogate_beta=surrogate_beta,
        trace_decay=trace_decay,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        topology=topology,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    output: SymbolicTensor = reservoir(inp) if driver is None else reservoir(inp, driver)
    model_inputs = inp if driver is None else [inp, driver]

    if concat_input:
        output = Concatenate()(inp, output)
        readout_in_features = feedback_size + reservoir_size
    else:
        readout_in_features = reservoir_size

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir.weight_feedback.device, dtype=reservoir.weight_feedback.dtype)(output)

    return ESNModel(model_inputs, readout_layer)

Build Ott's ESN model with state augmentation.

This model follows the architecture proposed by Edward Ott, which augments reservoir states by squaring even-indexed units and concatenating with input. This augmentation helps capture higher-order dynamics in chaotic systems.

Architecture:

def ott_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,

) -> ESNModel:
    """
    Build Ott's ESN model with state augmentation.

    This model follows the architecture proposed by Edward Ott, which augments
    reservoir states by squaring even-indexed units and concatenating with input.
    This augmentation helps capture higher-order dynamics in chaotic systems.

    Architecture:

    ```text
    Input -> Reservoir -> SelectiveExponentiation -> Concatenate(Input, Augmented) -> Readout
    ```

    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Dimension of feedback signal (input features).

        Dimension of output signal.

        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)` and the driver feeds the
        reservoir alongside the autoregressive feedback.  The driver is kept out
        of the input concatenation, so the readout `in_features` stays
        `feedback_size + reservoir_size`.  `None` (default) builds a
        feedback-only model, unchanged from previous behavior.
    input_initializer : str, tuple, or InputFeedbackInitializer, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Same format as
        `feedback_initializer`.  Only used when `input_size` is given.
    topology : str, tuple, or TopologyInitializer, optional
        Topology for recurrent weights. Accepts:

        - str: Registry name (e.g., `"erdos_renyi"`)
        - tuple: `(name, params)` like `("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1})`
        - TopologyInitializer: Pre-configured object

    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for recurrent weights.
    leak_rate : float, default=1.0
        Leaky integration rate. 1.0 = no leaking (standard ESN).
    feedback_initializer : str, tuple, or InputFeedbackInitializer, optional
        Initializer for feedback weights. Same format as `topology`.
    activation : {'tanh', 'relu', 'sigmoid', 'identity'}, default='tanh'
        Activation function for reservoir neurons.

        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        L2 regularization strength for ridge regression in readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to include bias in readout layer.
    readout_name : str, default='output'
        Name for the readout layer. Used as target key in training.
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout constructor options, including `trainable`, `rcond`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture widths are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs
        Additional keyword arguments passed to `ESNLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    ESNModel
        Configured Ott ESN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    Basic usage:

    >>> from resdag.models import ott_esn
    >>> model = ott_esn(
    ...     reservoir_size=500,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ... )
    >>> model.summary()

    With custom topology:

    >>> from resdag.init.topology import get_topology
    >>> model = ott_esn(
    ...     reservoir_size=500,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     topology=get_topology("watts_strogatz", k=4, p=0.3),
    ...     spectral_radius=0.95,
    ... )

    Training and forecasting:

    >>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
    >>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
    >>> trainer.fit(
    ...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
    ...     train_inputs=(train,),
    ...     targets={"output": target},
    ... )
    >>> predictions = model.forecast(forecast_warmup, horizon=100)

    See Also
    --------
    classic_esn : Traditional ESN without state augmentation.
    resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting readout.
    resdag.init.topology.get_topology : Get topology by name.
    """
    # Ott augmentation: square even-indexed reservoir units, concatenate input.
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=lambda: SelectiveExponentiation(index=0, exponent=2.0),

ParallelESNModel(
    reservoir: ESNLayer,
    readout: ReadoutLayer,
    input_dim: int,
    core_width: int,
    halo: int,
)

Bases: Module

Parallel local-state reservoir for spatiotemporal forecasting.

Holds one shared-weight resdag.layers.ESNLayer (advanced batched over patches) and one weight-tied resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer (fitted once over the pooled per-patch data), plus the patch geometry (input_dim, core_width, halo). Build it with parallel_esn rather than directly.

The public workflow mirrors the rest of the library — fit then forecast — but the forecasting is spatial-autoregressive: it stitches per-patch core predictions into the full field and re-windows every step, rather than feeding a single output straight back.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir

The shared reservoir. Its feedback_size must equal core_width + 2 * halo (the per-patch input width).

TYPE: ESNLayer

readout

The weight-tied readout. Its in_features must equal the reservoir size and its out_features must equal core_width.

TYPE: ReadoutLayer

input_dim

Full spatial dimension D of the modelled field.

TYPE: int

core_width

Core width w each patch predicts (P = input_dim // core_width).

TYPE: int

halo

Halo width g (neighbouring cells read on each side of the core).

TYPE: int

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION reservoir

The shared reservoir layer.

TYPE: ESNLayer

readout

The weight-tied readout layer.

TYPE: ReadoutLayer

n_patches

Number of patches P = input_dim // core_width.

TYPE: int

parallel_esn : Factory that builds and wires this class.

def __init__(
    self,
    reservoir: ESNLayer,
    readout: ReadoutLayer,
    input_dim: int,
    core_width: int,
    halo: int,
) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    patch_index = _patch_gather_index(input_dim, core_width, halo).to(
        device=reservoir.reference_device_dtype()[0]
    )
    patch_width = core_width + 2 * halo
    if reservoir.feedback_size != patch_width:
        raise ValueError(
            f"reservoir.feedback_size ({reservoir.feedback_size}) must equal the "
            f"per-patch input width core_width + 2*halo = {patch_width}."
        )
    if readout.out_features != core_width:
        raise ValueError(
            f"readout.out_features ({readout.out_features}) must equal core_width "
            f"({core_width}) — each patch predicts only its core region."
        )
    if readout.in_features != reservoir.reservoir_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"readout.in_features ({readout.in_features}) must equal the reservoir "
            f"size ({reservoir.reservoir_size})."
        )

    self.reservoir = reservoir
    self.readout = readout
    self.input_dim = input_dim
    self.core_width = core_width
    self.halo = halo
    self.n_patches = input_dim // core_width
    # Non-persistent: rebuilt cheaply from geometry, moves with ``.to()``.
    self.register_buffer(
        "patch_index",
        patch_index,
        persistent=False,
    )

forward(series: Tensor, *, reset: bool = False) -> Tensor

Predict each timestep, preserving gradients through the model.

Accepts (batch, time, input_dim) and returns that shape. Reservoir state carries across calls; use reset=True for independent batches. This teacher-forced path composes with ordinary PyTorch modules and optimizers. Use forecast for an autonomous rollout.

def forward(self, series: torch.Tensor, *, reset: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Predict each timestep, preserving gradients through the model.

    Accepts `(batch, time, input_dim)` and returns that shape. Reservoir
    state carries across calls; use `reset=True` for independent batches.
    This teacher-forced path composes with ordinary PyTorch modules and
    optimizers. Use `forecast` for an autonomous rollout.
    """
    validate_sequence_inputs(
        (series,), feature_sizes=(self.input_dim,), reference=module_reference(self)
    )
    if reset:
        self.reset_reservoirs()
    states = self.reservoir(self.window(series))
    batch, timesteps = series.shape[:2]
    cores = cast(torch.Tensor, self.readout(states))
    return (
        cores.reshape(batch, self.n_patches, timesteps, self.core_width)
        .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
        .reshape(batch, timesteps, self.input_dim)
    )

def forward_stateless(
    self,
    *inputs: torch.Tensor,
    states: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
    compile: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ReservoirStates]:
    """Predict independently or continue explicit per-patch recurrent states.

    Pass one `(batch, time, input_dim)` field. The returned `reservoir`
    state folds the patches into its batch axis, with shape
    `(batch * n_patches, reservoir_size)`. State tensors retain gradients;
    this method leaves the model's stored streaming states untouched.
    """
    validate_sequence_inputs(
        inputs, feature_sizes=(self.input_dim,), reference=module_reference(self)
    )
    from resdag.core._hooks import call_with_states, has_execution_hooks

    if has_execution_hooks(self):
        return cast(
            tuple[torch.Tensor, ReservoirStates],
            call_with_states(self, inputs, states, {"reservoir": "reservoir"}, compile=compile),
        )
    series = inputs[0]
    patches = self.window(series)
    if states is None:
        state = self.reservoir.cell.init_state(patches.shape[0], patches.device, patches.dtype)
    else:
        if set(states) != {"reservoir"}:
            raise ValueError("Reservoir state keys must be exactly ['reservoir']")
        state = states["reservoir"]
        if not isinstance(state, torch.Tensor):
            raise TypeError("State for 'reservoir' must be a torch.Tensor")
        self.reservoir.cell.validate_state(state)
        if state.shape[0] != patches.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("State batch size must equal batch * n_patches")
        if state.device != patches.device or state.dtype != patches.dtype:
            raise ValueError("State must match the input device and dtype")
    features, final = self.reservoir.forward_stateless([patches], state, compile=compile)
    batch, timesteps = series.shape[:2]
    cores = cast(torch.Tensor, self.readout(features))
    output = (
        cores.reshape(batch, self.n_patches, timesteps, self.core_width)
        .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
        .reshape(batch, timesteps, self.input_dim)
    )
    return output, {"reservoir": final}

docs.text:
window(series: Tensor) -> Tensor

Window a full (batch, T, D) field into per-patch inputs.

Gathers, for every patch, its core_width + 2 * halo periodic cells in one indexing op, then folds the patch axis into the batch axis so the result drops straight into the shared reservoir as a batched sequence.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION series

Full field of shape (batch, T, input_dim).

TYPE: Tensor

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Tensor

Windowed input of shape (batch * P, T, core_width + 2 * halo) — the patch axis is folded into the leading (reservoir-batch) axis.

Source code in src/resdag/models/parallel_esn.py 
def window(self, series: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Window a full `(batch, T, D)` field into per-patch inputs.

    Gathers, for every patch, its `core_width + 2 * halo` periodic cells in
    one indexing op, then folds the patch axis into the batch axis so the
    result drops straight into the shared reservoir as a batched sequence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : torch.Tensor
        Full field of shape `(batch, T, input_dim)`.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Windowed input of shape `(batch * P, T, core_width + 2 * halo)` —
        the patch axis is folded into the leading (reservoir-batch) axis.
    """
    if series.dim() != 3 or series.shape[-1] != self.input_dim:
        raise ValueError(
            f"series must be 3-D (batch, T, input_dim={self.input_dim}); "
            f"got shape {tuple(series.shape)}."
        )
    # series: (B, T, D) -> gather patch cells -> (B, T, P, w+2g).
    windowed = series[..., self.patch_index]
    b, t, n_patches, patch_width = windowed.shape
    # Move patches next to the batch axis and fold them in: (B*P, T, w+2g).
    windowed = windowed.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(b * n_patches, t, patch_width)
    return windowed
