stitch(patch_cores: Tensor) -> Tensor

Assemble per-patch core predictions into the full field.

Inverse of window for the core regions: patch p owns cores [p*w : (p+1)*w] of the full field, so concatenating the patches' core predictions along the spatial axis reconstructs the whole D-wide state. With non-overlapping cores this is a contiguous reshape (no averaging needed).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION patch_cores

Per-patch core predictions of shape (batch, P, core_width).

TYPE: Tensor

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Tensor

Full field of shape (batch, input_dim).

Source code in src/resdag/models/parallel_esn.py 
def stitch(self, patch_cores: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Assemble per-patch core predictions into the full field.

    Inverse of `window` for the core regions: patch `p` owns cores
    `[p*w : (p+1)*w]` of the full field, so concatenating the patches' core
    predictions along the spatial axis reconstructs the whole `D`-wide
    state.  With non-overlapping cores this is a contiguous reshape (no
    averaging needed).

    Parameters
    ----------
    patch_cores : torch.Tensor
        Per-patch core predictions of shape `(batch, P, core_width)`.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Full field of shape `(batch, input_dim)`.
    """
    b = patch_cores.shape[0]
    return patch_cores.reshape(b, self.input_dim)

def set_state(self, states: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor], strict: bool = True) -> None:
    """Restore the named recurrent state on the model's device and dtype."""

docs.text:
fit(warmup: Tensor, train: Tensor, targets: Tensor, *, reset: bool = True) -> None

Fit the weight-tied readout over all patches in one pooled solve.

Windows warmup / train into per-patch inputs, runs them through the shared reservoir (batched over batch * P), and fits the single readout on the pooled (reservoir_state -> core_target) pairs from every patch and timestep — the weight-tied readout of Pathak et al.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION warmup

Teacher-forced warmup field of shape (batch, warmup_steps, D) used only to synchronise the reservoir states.

TYPE: Tensor

train

Training field of shape (batch, train_steps, D) whose reservoir states are regressed onto targets.

TYPE: Tensor

targets

Next-step field of shape (batch, train_steps, D) — typically train shifted one step ahead. Each patch is supervised on its own core slice of this field.

TYPE: Tensor

reset

If True, reset the reservoir states before warmup.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If any input is not 3-D, if their feature dimension is not input_dim, or if train and targets disagree on batch/length.

Source code in src/resdag/models/parallel_esn.py 
def fit(
    self,
    warmup: torch.Tensor,
    train: torch.Tensor,
    targets: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    reset: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Fit the weight-tied readout over all patches in one pooled solve.

    Windows `warmup` / `train` into per-patch inputs, runs them through
    the shared reservoir (batched over `batch * P`), and fits the single
    readout on the pooled `(reservoir_state -> core_target)` pairs from
    every patch and timestep — the weight-tied readout of Pathak et al.

    Parameters
    ----------
    warmup : torch.Tensor
        Teacher-forced warmup field of shape `(batch, warmup_steps, D)`
        used only to synchronise the reservoir states.
    train : torch.Tensor
        Training field of shape `(batch, train_steps, D)` whose reservoir
        states are regressed onto `targets`.
    targets : torch.Tensor
        Next-step field of shape `(batch, train_steps, D)` — typically
        `train` shifted one step ahead.  Each patch is supervised on its
        own core slice of this field.
    reset : bool, default=True
        If `True`, reset the reservoir states before warmup.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any input is not 3-D, if their feature dimension is not
        `input_dim`, or if `train` and `targets` disagree on
        batch/length.
    """
    for name, arr in (("warmup", warmup), ("train", train), ("targets", targets)):
        if arr.dim() != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be 3-D (batch, T, D); got shape {tuple(arr.shape)}.")
        if arr.shape[-1] != self.input_dim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} has feature dim {arr.shape[-1]}, expected input_dim={self.input_dim}."
            )
    if train.shape[:2] != targets.shape[:2]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"train and targets must share (batch, T); got {tuple(train.shape[:2])} "
            f"vs {tuple(targets.shape[:2])}."
        )
    reference = module_reference(self)
    for label, tensor in (("warmup", warmup), ("train", train), ("targets", targets)):
        validate_sequence_inputs(
            (tensor,),
            feature_sizes=(self.input_dim,),
            reference=reference,
            label=label,
            allow_empty=label == "warmup",
        )
    if warmup.shape[0] != train.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("warmup and train must have the same batch size")

    if reset:
        self.reset_reservoirs()

    with torch.no_grad():
        # Warmup: synchronise the per-patch reservoir states.
        self.reservoir(self.window(warmup))
        # Train pass: collect reservoir states for every patch and step.
        states = self.reservoir(self.window(train))  # (B*P, train_steps, N)

    # Per-patch core targets: window the target field and keep only the core
    # columns (offsets [halo, halo + core_width)).  Same (B*P, T) folding as
    # the states, so state[i] and target[i] are the same patch/step pair.
    windowed_targets = self.window(targets)  # (B*P, T, w+2g)
    core_targets = windowed_targets[..., self._cores_from_index()]  # (B*P, T, w)

    # One pooled ridge solve over all patches (weight-tied readout).  fit()
    # flattens (B*P, T, .) -> (B*P*T, .) internally.
    self.readout.fit(states, core_targets)

docs.text:
forecast(
    warmup: Tensor,
    *,
    horizon: int,
    initial_feedback: Tensor | None = None,
    reset: bool = True,
    return_warmup: bool = False,
    alignment: ForecastAlignment = "next"
) -> Tensor

Predict the next full fields after the observed warmup.

Inputs have shape (batch, time, input_dim) and results have shape (batch, horizon, input_dim). Slot zero is the final warmup prediction, estimating the immediate unseen field. Each later step feeds the previous prediction through the batched patches. horizon is a positive integer.

initial_feedback is a distinct extra field consumed after all warmup fields, shaped (batch, 1, input_dim). It also permits empty history; use reset=False to continue states with the previous final prediction as this seed. The final returned prediction has not yet been consumed.

return_warmup=True prepends historical predictions, giving length warmup_steps - 1 + horizon. Explicit seeds give warmup_steps + horizon. alignment="legacy" uses the old low-level ESN convention: omit the final warmup prediction, then generate horizon steps, giving a warmup_steps + horizon result when historical predictions are included. The default future timing already matches earlier ParallelESN releases; their return_warmup prefix contained raw observations instead.

Source code in src/resdag/models/parallel_esn.py 
def forecast(
    self,
    warmup: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    horizon: int,
    initial_feedback: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    reset: bool = True,
    return_warmup: bool = False,
    alignment: ForecastAlignment = "next",
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Predict the next full fields after the observed `warmup`.

    Inputs have shape `(batch, time, input_dim)` and results have shape
    `(batch, horizon, input_dim)`. Slot zero is the final warmup prediction,
    estimating the immediate unseen field. Each later step feeds the previous
    prediction through the batched patches. `horizon` is a positive integer.

    `initial_feedback` is a distinct extra field consumed after all warmup
    fields, shaped `(batch, 1, input_dim)`. It also permits empty history;
    use `reset=False` to continue states with the previous final prediction
    as this seed. The final returned prediction has not yet been consumed.

    `return_warmup=True` prepends historical *predictions*, giving length
    `warmup_steps - 1 + horizon`. Explicit seeds give `warmup_steps + horizon`.
    `alignment="legacy"` uses the old low-level ESN convention: omit the
    final warmup prediction, then generate `horizon` steps, giving a
    `warmup_steps + horizon` result when historical predictions are included.
    The default future timing already matches earlier ParallelESN releases;
    their `return_warmup` prefix contained raw observations instead.
    """
    inputs, _, horizon, boundary = prepare_forecast_inputs(
        warmup,
        None,
        num_inputs=1,
        horizon=horizon,
        initial_feedback=initial_feedback,
        alignment=alignment,
    )
    warmup = inputs[0]
    if warmup.shape[-1] != self.input_dim:
        raise ValueError(
            f"warmup must have input_dim={self.input_dim} features; got {warmup.shape[-1]}"
        )
    if not self.readout.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("forecast() requires a fitted readout; call fit() first.")
    from resdag.core._hooks import has_execution_hooks

    hooked = has_execution_hooks(self)
    forward = self if hooked else self.forward
    advance = (
        self._forecast_single_frame
        if not hooked and self._can_forecast_single_frame()
        else forward
    )
    with torch.no_grad():
        warmup_outputs = forward(warmup, reset=reset)
        current = (
            initial_feedback if initial_feedback is not None else warmup_outputs[:, -1:, :]
        )
        outputs = torch.empty(
            warmup.shape[0],
            horizon,
            self.input_dim,
            dtype=warmup_outputs.dtype,
            device=warmup_outputs.device,
        )
        if boundary:
            outputs[:, :1, :] = current
        for t in range(int(boundary), horizon):
            current = advance(current)
            outputs[:, t : t + 1, :] = current
        if return_warmup:
            prefix = warmup_outputs[:, :-1, :] if boundary else warmup_outputs
            return torch.cat((prefix, outputs), dim=1)
        return outputs

docs.title: parallel_esn
docs.text:
parallel_esn(
    input_dim: int,
    core_width: int,
    halo: int,
    reservoir_size: int = 500,
    *,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.6,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    input_scaling: float = 0.1,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    seed: Any = None,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 0.0001,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ParallelESNModel

Build a parallel local-state reservoir (Pathak et al. 2018).

Splits a spatially-extended field of dimension input_dim into P = input_dim / core_width overlapping patches (core width core_width, halo halo on each side, periodic boundaries), all sharing one reservoir (advanced batched over patches) and one weight-tied readout (core width core_width). See ParallelESNModel and the module docstring for the full architecture and the forecasting loop.

The defaults (spectral_radius=0.6, input_scaling=0.1, readout_alpha=1e-4) are tuned for the local-patch regime, which uses a smaller, better-conditioned reservoir per patch than a single global ESN — the classic Pathak KS settings. input_scaling=0.1 in particular is decisive: the per-patch input width (core_width + 2*halo) is large enough that an unscaled uniform(-1, 1) input map drives tanh deep into saturation, collapsing the reservoir's memory; scaling the input weights down keeps the dynamics responsive (on the canonical L=22 KS field it is the difference between a fraction of a Lyapunov time and ~4 Lyapunov times of valid prediction).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION input_dim

Full spatial dimension D of the field (e.g. the KS grid size).

TYPE: int

core_width

Core width w each patch predicts. Must divide input_dim.

TYPE: int

halo

Halo width g — neighbouring cells read on each side of the core (periodic). The per-patch reservoir input width is core_width + 2 * halo.

TYPE: int

reservoir_size

Number of units N in the shared reservoir (per patch).

TYPE: int DEFAULT: 500

topology

Topology for the recurrent weights. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.6

leak_rate

Leaky-integration rate (1.0 = no leak).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

input_scaling

Scale of the per-patch input (feedback) weights when feedback_initializer is left at its default. The weights are drawn from uniform(-input_scaling, input_scaling) (via the "random" initializer), keeping the tanh reservoir out of saturation on a wide per-patch input. Ignored when an explicit feedback_initializer is supplied (it then owns the input-weight scale).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.1

feedback_initializer

Initializer for the per-patch input weights. Same accepted forms as topology. When given, it overrides input_scaling. Left at its default (None), the factory uses ("random", {"input_scaling": input_scaling}).

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

activation

Activation function ("tanh", "relu", "sigmoid", "identity").

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "tanh"

bias

Whether the reservoir uses a bias term.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

seed

Reproducibility seed fixing every reservoir parameter.

TYPE: int or Generator DEFAULT: None

readout

A built-in readout name or a ReadoutLayer subclass, with the same solver choices as resdag.models.classic_esn.

TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

readout_alpha

Ridge regularization for the readout.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-4

readout_bias

Whether the readout uses a bias term.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout_name

Name for the readout layer.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

readout_kwargs

Additional readout constructor options. Architecture widths are fixed.

TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

**reservoir_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.ESNLayer (e.g. sparse, noise, input_initializer).

TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION ParallelESNModel

The assembled parallel reservoir, ready for ParallelESNModel.fit and ParallelESNModel.forecast.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If core_width does not divide input_dim, or if a size argument is out of range.

Examples:

Forecast a Kuramoto-Sivashinsky field with local patches::

>>> import torch
>>> from resdag import kuramoto_sivashinsky
>>> from resdag.models import parallel_esn
>>> data = kuramoto_sivashinsky(3000, n_grid=64, dtype=torch.float64)

...                      seed=0)

>>> pred = model.forecast(train[:, -100:], horizon=400)

def parallel_esn(
    input_dim: int,
    core_width: int,
    halo: int,
    reservoir_size: int = 500,
    *,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.6,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    input_scaling: float = 0.1,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    seed: Any = None,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-4,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ParallelESNModel:
    r"""Build a parallel local-state reservoir (Pathak et al. 2018).

    Splits a spatially-extended field of dimension `input_dim` into `P = input_dim / core_width` overlapping patches (core width `core_width`, halo
    `halo` on each side, periodic boundaries), all sharing **one** reservoir
    (advanced batched over patches) and **one** weight-tied readout (core width
    `core_width`).  See `ParallelESNModel` and the module docstring for
    the full architecture and the forecasting loop.

    The defaults (`spectral_radius=0.6`, `input_scaling=0.1`,
    `readout_alpha=1e-4`) are tuned for the local-patch regime, which uses a
    smaller, better-conditioned reservoir per patch than a single global ESN —
    the classic Pathak KS settings.  `input_scaling=0.1` in particular is
    decisive: the per-patch input width (`core_width + 2*halo`) is large enough
    that an unscaled `uniform(-1, 1)` input map drives `tanh` deep into
    saturation, collapsing the reservoir's memory; scaling the input weights down
    keeps the dynamics responsive (on the canonical L=22 KS field it is the
    difference between a fraction of a Lyapunov time and ~4 Lyapunov times of
    valid prediction).

    Parameters
    ----------
    input_dim : int
        Full spatial dimension `D` of the field (e.g. the KS grid size).
    core_width : int
        Core width `w` each patch predicts.  Must divide `input_dim`.
    halo : int
        Halo width `g` — neighbouring cells read on each side of the core
        (periodic).  The per-patch reservoir input width is `core_width + 2 * halo`.
    reservoir_size : int, default=500
        Number of units `N` in the shared reservoir (per patch).
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights.  Accepts a registry name, a
        `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.6
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights.
    leak_rate : float, default=1.0
        Leaky-integration rate (1.0 = no leak).
    input_scaling : float, default=0.1
        Scale of the per-patch input (feedback) weights when
        `feedback_initializer` is left at its default.  The weights are drawn
        from `uniform(-input_scaling, input_scaling)` (via the `"random"`
        initializer), keeping the `tanh` reservoir out of saturation on a
        wide per-patch input.  Ignored when an explicit `feedback_initializer`
        is supplied (it then owns the input-weight scale).
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the per-patch input weights.  Same accepted forms as
        `topology`.  When given, it overrides `input_scaling`.  Left at its
        default (`None`), the factory uses `("random", {"input_scaling": input_scaling})`.
    activation : str, default="tanh"
        Activation function (`"tanh"`, `"relu"`, `"sigmoid"`,
        `"identity"`).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the reservoir uses a bias term.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    seed : int or torch.Generator, optional
        Reproducibility seed fixing every reservoir parameter.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in readout name or a ReadoutLayer subclass, with the same
        solver choices as `resdag.models.classic_esn`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-4
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the readout uses a bias term.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer.
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Additional readout constructor options. Architecture widths are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`
        (e.g. `sparse`, `noise`, `input_initializer`).

    Returns
    -------
    ParallelESNModel
        The assembled parallel reservoir, ready for `ParallelESNModel.fit`
        and `ParallelESNModel.forecast`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `core_width` does not divide `input_dim`, or if a size argument is
        out of range.

    Examples
    --------
    Forecast a Kuramoto-Sivashinsky field with local patches::

    >>> import torch
    >>> from resdag import kuramoto_sivashinsky
    >>> from resdag.models import parallel_esn
    >>> data = kuramoto_sivashinsky(3000, n_grid=64, dtype=torch.float64)
    >>> model = parallel_esn(input_dim=64, core_width=4, halo=6, reservoir_size=400,
    ...                      seed=0)
    >>> warmup, train = data[:, :200], data[:, 200:2200]
    >>> model.fit(warmup, train[:, :-1], train[:, 1:])   # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> pred = model.forecast(train[:, -100:], horizon=400)  # doctest: +SKIP

    See Also
    --------
    ParallelESNModel : The model class this factory builds.
    resdag.datasets.kuramoto_sivashinsky : The canonical spatiotemporal benchmark.
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Single global reservoir baseline.
    """
    _patch_gather_index(input_dim, core_width, halo)
    patch_width = core_width + 2 * halo

    # Default the per-patch input map to a *scaled* random init: on a wide
    # per-patch input an unscaled ``uniform(-1, 1)`` saturates the tanh
    # reservoir (see the ``input_scaling`` docstring).  An explicit
    # ``feedback_initializer`` overrides this and owns the input-weight scale.
    if feedback_initializer is None:
        feedback_initializer = ("random", {"input_scaling": input_scaling})

    reservoir = ESNLayer(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=patch_width,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        leak_rate=leak_rate,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        seed=seed,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=reservoir_size,
        out_features=core_width,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir.weight_hh.device, dtype=reservoir.weight_hh.dtype)

    return ParallelESNModel(
        reservoir=reservoir,
        readout=readout_layer,
        input_dim=input_dim,
        core_width=core_width,
        halo=halo,
    )

    feedback_size: int,

    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

Build Power Augmented ESN model.

This model augments reservoir states by exponentiating to a power and concatenating with input. This augmentation helps capture higher-order dynamics in chaotic systems.

Architecture:

Input -> Reservoir -> Power -> Concatenate(Input, Augmented) -> Readout
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of units in the reservoir.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Dimension of feedback signal (input features).

TYPE: int

output_size

Dimension of output signal.

TYPE: int

exponent

Exponent applied to every reservoir state. Tanh reservoir states live in [-1, 1] and routinely include negative and zero values, so the exponent must be chosen with that signed range in mind (see Notes). The default 3.0 is an odd integer and therefore sign-preserving; an even exponent such as 2.0 maps every state to a non-negative value and so discards the sign of the reservoir activations.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 3.0

input_size

Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver) and the driver feeds the reservoir alongside the autoregressive feedback. The driver is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout in_features stays feedback_size + reservoir_size. None (default) builds a feedback-only model, unchanged from previous behavior.

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

input_initializer

Initializer for the driving-input weights. Same format as feedback_initializer. Only used when input_size is given.

TYPE: str, tuple, or InputFeedbackInitializer DEFAULT: None

topology

Topology for recurrent weights. Accepts:

  • str: Registry name (e.g., "erdos_renyi")
  • tuple: (name, params) like ("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1})
  • TopologyInitializer: Pre-configured object

TYPE: str, tuple, or TopologyInitializer DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target spectral radius for recurrent weights.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

leak_rate

Leaky integration rate. 1.0 = no leaking (standard ESN).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

feedback_initializer

Initializer for feedback weights. Same format as topology.

TYPE: str, tuple, or InputFeedbackInitializer DEFAULT: None

activation

Activation function for reservoir neurons.

TYPE: (tanh, relu, sigmoid, identity) DEFAULT: 'tanh'

bias

Whether to include bias in reservoir.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

If True, reservoir weights are trainable via backpropagation.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

readout

A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

readout_alpha

L2 regularization strength for ridge regression in readout.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

readout_bias

Whether to include bias in readout layer.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout_name

Name for the readout layer. Used as target key in training.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'output'

readout_kwargs

Extra readout constructor options, including trainable, rcond, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture widths are fixed.

TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

**reservoir_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments passed to ESNLayer.

TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION ESNModel

Configured Power Augmented ESN model ready for training and inference.

Notes

The augmentation applies resdag.layers.Power to the raw reservoir states, which for a tanh activation lie in [-1, 1] — negatives and zeros included. Choose exponent accordingly:

  • Even integers (2.0, 4.0, …) are always safe: every state maps to a non-negative value with no nan/inf.
  • Odd integers (3.0, 5.0, …) are safe and sign-preserving: negative states stay negative.
  • Non-integer exponents (e.g. 0.5, 1.5) applied to a negative state produce nan under the default torch.pow, silently corrupting the readout inputs. Negative exponents (e.g. -1.0) produce inf on the zeros that tanh states pass through.

If you need a non-integer exponent on signed states, wire the model by hand with Power(exponent, sign_preserving=True), which applies sign(x) * abs(x) ** exponent and stays finite for negative bases. This factory always uses the default (non-sign-preserving) Power to keep the well-established integer-exponent behaviour unchanged.

Examples:

Basic usage:

>>> from resdag.models import power_augmented
>>> model = power_augmented(
...     reservoir_size=500,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     exponent=3.0,
... )
>>> model.summary()

With custom topology:

>>> from resdag.init.topology import get_topology
>>> model = power_augmented(
...     reservoir_size=500,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     topology=get_topology("watts_strogatz", k=4, p=0.3),
...     spectral_radius=0.95,
...     exponent=3.0,
... )

Training and forecasting:

>>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
>>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
...     train_inputs=(train,),
...     targets={"output": target},
... )
>>> predictions = model.forecast(forecast_warmup, horizon=100)
See Also

classic_esn : Traditional ESN without state augmentation. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting readout. resdag.init.topology.get_topology : Get topology by name.

    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    alpha: float = 0.5,
    beta: float = 0.9,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,

    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,

    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

Build a Residual Echo State Network (ResESN) model.

ResESN (Ceni & Gallicchio, 2024) generalises ES2N by decoupling the orthogonal-skip and nonlinear branch weights:

\[ x_t = \alpha\,O\,x_{t-1} + \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + \cdots) \]

with independent coefficients \(\alpha\) (skip) and \(\beta\) (nonlinear) replacing the leak rate. \(\alpha = 1 - \beta\) recovers ES2N. This factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as resdag.models.classic_esn:

Input -> ResESN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reservoir_size

Number of units in the reservoir.

TYPE: int

feedback_size

Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).

TYPE: int

output_size

Number of output features.

TYPE: int

alpha

Scaling of the orthogonal skip (residual) branch.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.5

beta

Scaling of the nonlinear branch.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

input_size

Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver is kept out of the input concatenation. None (default) builds a feedback-only model.

TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

input_initializer

Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

topology

Topology for the recurrent weights W_r. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

spectral_radius

Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights W_r.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

orthogonal_scaling

Gain on the orthogonal skip matrix O. 1.0 keeps it exactly norm-preserving.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

feedback_initializer

Initializer for the feedback weights.

TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

activation

Activation for the nonlinear branch.

TYPE: (tanh, relu, sigmoid, identity) DEFAULT: 'tanh'

bias

Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

trainable

Whether the reservoir weights are trainable. The orthogonal skip stays frozen regardless.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

readout

A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

readout_alpha

Ridge regularization for the readout.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

readout_bias

Whether to use a bias in the readout.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

readout_name

Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

readout_kwargs

Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

**reservoir_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.reservoirs.resesn.ResESNLayer (e.g. bias_scaling, seed).

TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION `resdag.core.ESNModel`

Configured ResESN model ready for training and inference.

Examples:

>>> from resdag.models import resesn
>>> model = resesn(500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, alpha=0.6, beta=0.4)

    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    r"""Build a Residual Echo State Network (ResESN) model.

    ResESN (Ceni & Gallicchio, 2024) generalises ES2N by **decoupling** the
    orthogonal-skip and nonlinear branch weights:

    $$
    x_t = \alpha\,O\,x_{t-1} + \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + \cdots)
    $$

    with independent coefficients $\alpha$ (skip) and $\beta$
    (nonlinear) replacing the leak rate.  $\alpha = 1 - \beta$ recovers
    ES2N.  This factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as
    `resdag.models.classic_esn`:

    ```text
    Input -> ResESN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    alpha : float, default=0.5
        Scaling of the orthogonal skip (residual) branch.
    beta : float, default=0.9
        Scaling of the nonlinear branch.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver is kept out of
        the input concatenation.  `None` (default) builds a feedback-only
        model.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when
        `input_size` is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights `W_r`.  Accepts a registry name, a
        `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights `W_r`.
    orthogonal_scaling : float, default=1.0
        Gain on the orthogonal skip matrix `O`.  `1.0` keeps it exactly
        norm-preserving.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights.
    activation : {'tanh', 'relu', 'sigmoid', 'identity'}, default='tanh'
        Activation for the nonlinear branch.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.  The orthogonal skip stays
        frozen regardless.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.resesn.ResESNLayer` (e.g.
        `bias_scaling`, `seed`).

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured ResESN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import resesn
    >>> model = resesn(500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, alpha=0.6, beta=0.4)

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.es2n : Edge-of-Stability State Network (convex combination).
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.resesn.ResESNLayer : The reservoir layer.
    """
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=None,
        concat_input=True,
        input_size=input_size,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        reservoir_cls=ResESNLayer,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        readout=readout,
        readout_alpha=readout_alpha,
        readout_bias=readout_bias,
        readout_name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
        alpha=alpha,
        beta=beta,
        orthogonal_scaling=orthogonal_scaling,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

This module provides ensemble wrappers for groups of independently-trained resdag.core.ESNModel instances.

CLASS DESCRIPTION CoupledEnsembleESNModel

N independent ESN sub-models whose autoregressive forecasts are coupled through a shared averaged feedback signal at every timestep.

See Also

resdag.models.coupled_ensemble_esn : Factory function for quick construction.

docs.title: CoupledEnsembleESNModel
docs.text:
CoupledEnsembleESNModel(models: list[ESNModel], aggregator: str | Module = 'mean')

Bases: Module

Ensemble of N independently-trained ESN models with coupled feedback.

Each sub-model is a complete resdag.core.ESNModel built via the pytorch_symbolic API. The models are trained independently but coupled during forecasting: at every autoregressive step every model receives the same aggregated output (e.g. the mean across models) as its next feedback input.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION models

N pre-built ESN sub-models. Diversity comes from their independent random reservoir initialization.

TYPE: list of ESNModel

aggregator

How to combine the N per-model outputs into a single feedback tensor.

  • "mean" — arithmetic mean across models.
  • "median" — interpolated (statistical) median across models; for an even number of models the two central values are averaged.
  • Any nn.Module that accepts a stacked tensor of shape (N, batch, timesteps, features) and returns (batch, timesteps, features). E.g. resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean.

TYPE: str or Module DEFAULT: `"mean"`

Examples:

Typical use via the factory:

>>> from resdag.models import coupled_ensemble_esn
>>> ensemble = coupled_ensemble_esn(n_models=5, reservoir_size=300,
...                                feedback_size=3, output_size=3)
>>> ensemble.fit((warmup,), (train,), {"output": targets})
>>> ensemble.reset_reservoirs()
>>> preds = ensemble.forecast(forecast_warmup, horizon=200)
>>> preds.shape
torch.Size([1, 200, 3])

With a custom aggregator:

>>> from resdag.ensemble.aggregators import OutliersFilteredMean
>>> ensemble = coupled_ensemble_esn(
...     n_models=10, reservoir_size=300, feedback_size=3, output_size=3,
...     aggregate=OutliersFilteredMean(method="z_score", threshold=2.0),
... )
See Also

resdag.models.coupled_ensemble_esn : Convenience factory function. resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean : Outlier-robust aggregation layer.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION models

Sub-models. Must be non-empty.

TYPE: list of ESNModel

aggregator

Aggregation strategy. See class docstring for options.

TYPE: str or Module DEFAULT: `"mean"`

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If models is empty, if aggregator is an unknown string, if any sub-model is multi-output (multi-head), or if any sub-model's output dimension does not match its feedback (first input) dimension. Multi-output sub-models are rejected because the ensemble aggregates the members into a single shared feedback signal and has no meaningful coupled aggregation for auxiliary heads. The dimension check rejects headless / linear sub-models, whose output is the raw reservoir state rather than a feedback-dimensioned readout, since the coupled autoregressive loop feeds the aggregated output back as the next feedback input.

Source code in src/resdag/ensemble/coupled.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    models: list[ESNModel],
    aggregator: str | nn.Module = "mean",
) -> None:
    """Initialize the coupled ensemble.

    Parameters
    ----------
    models : list of ESNModel
        Sub-models.  Must be non-empty.
    aggregator : str or nn.Module, default `"mean"`
        Aggregation strategy.  See class docstring for options.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `models` is empty, if `aggregator` is an unknown string, if
        any sub-model is multi-output (multi-head), or if any sub-model's
        output dimension does not match its feedback (first input)
        dimension.  Multi-output sub-models are rejected because the
        ensemble aggregates the members into a single shared feedback signal
        and has no meaningful coupled aggregation for auxiliary heads.  The
        dimension check rejects headless / linear sub-models, whose output is
        the raw reservoir state rather than a feedback-dimensioned readout,
        since the coupled autoregressive loop feeds the aggregated output
        back as the next feedback input.
    """
    super().__init__()
    if len(models) == 0:
        raise ValueError("CoupledEnsembleESNModel requires at least one sub-model.")
    if isinstance(aggregator, str) and aggregator not in ("mean", "median"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"aggregator must be 'mean', 'median', or an nn.Module; got '{aggregator}'."
        )

    if not isinstance(aggregator, (str, nn.Module)):
        raise TypeError("aggregator must be 'mean', 'median', or an nn.Module")
    for index, model in enumerate(models):
        if not isinstance(model, ESNModel):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Sub-model {index} must be an ESNModel, got {type(model).__name__}"
            )
    self._validate_feedback_output_dims(models)
    self._validate_member_interfaces(models)

    reservoir_owners: dict[int, int] = {}
    for index, model in enumerate(models):
        for layer in model.modules():
            if isinstance(layer, BaseReservoirLayer):
                owner = reservoir_owners.get(id(layer))
                if owner is not None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Ensemble members {owner} and {index} share a reservoir layer instance. "
                        "Members require independent recurrent state. Use distinct reservoir "
                        "layer instances; their parameter tensors may still share weights."
                    )
                reservoir_owners[id(layer)] = index

    self.models = nn.ModuleList(models)

    if isinstance(aggregator, nn.Module):
        self.aggregator_module: nn.Module | None = aggregator
        self._aggregator_str: str | None = None
    else:
        self.aggregator_module = None
        self._aggregator_str = aggregator

def forward(self, *inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Run all sub-models on the same inputs and return the aggregated output.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *inputs : torch.Tensor
        Same input tensors passed to every sub-model.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Aggregated output of shape `(batch, timesteps, output_size)`.
    """
    outputs = [model(*inputs) for model in self.models]
    return self._aggregate(outputs)

docs.text:
forward_stateless(
    *inputs: Tensor, states: Mapping[str, Tensor] | None = None, compile: bool = False
) -> tuple[Tensor, ReservoirStates]

Aggregate complete member predictions with explicit recurrent state.

Omitted states start every member from zero. Otherwise use the named dictionary returned by this method, whose keys are models.<member index>.<reservoir name>. The model's stored states remain untouched; returned states retain gradients across chunks.

Source code in src/resdag/ensemble/coupled.py 
def forward_stateless(
    self,
    *inputs: torch.Tensor,
    states: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
    compile: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ReservoirStates]:
    """Aggregate complete member predictions with explicit recurrent state.

    Omitted states start every member from zero. Otherwise use the named
    dictionary returned by this method, whose keys are
    `models.<member index>.<reservoir name>`. The model's stored states
    remain untouched; returned states retain gradients across chunks.
    """
    names = {
        f"models.{index}.{name}"
        for index, model in enumerate(self._iter_models())
        for name in model._get_execution_plan().reservoir_names
    }
    if states is not None and set(states) != names:
        raise ValueError(
            "Reservoir state keys must match the model; "
            f"missing={sorted(names - set(states))}, "
            f"unexpected={sorted(set(states) - names)}"
        )
    from resdag.core._hooks import call_with_states, has_execution_hooks, state_paths

    if has_execution_hooks(self):
        paths = state_paths(self)
        if set(paths) != names:
            raise ValueError(
                "Explicit-state execution cannot thread hidden aggregator reservoirs"
            )
        return cast(
            tuple[torch.Tensor, ReservoirStates],
            call_with_states(self, inputs, states, paths, compile=compile),
        )
    outputs = []
    final: ReservoirStates = {}
    for index, model in enumerate(self._iter_models()):
        prefix = f"models.{index}."
        member_states = (
            None
            if states is None
            else {
                key.removeprefix(prefix): value
                for key, value in states.items()
                if key.startswith(prefix)
            }
        )
        output, member_final = model.forward_stateless(
            *inputs, states=member_states, compile=compile
        )
        outputs.append(cast(torch.Tensor, output))
        final.update({prefix + key: value for key, value in member_final.items()})
    return self._aggregate(outputs), final

def as_module(self, *, stateful: bool = False) -> ReservoirModelModule:

def set_state(self, states: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor], strict: bool = True) -> None:
    """Restore a named state dictionary matching `forward_stateless`."""
    names = {
        f"models.{index}.{name}"
        for index, model in enumerate(self._iter_models())
        for name, module in model.named_modules()
        if isinstance(module, BaseReservoirLayer)
    }
    if strict and set(states) != names:
        raise KeyError(
            f"Reservoir state keys must match the model; missing={sorted(names - set(states))}, "
            f"unexpected={sorted(set(states) - names)}"
        )
    for index, model in enumerate(self._iter_models()):
        prefix = f"models.{index}."
        member = {
            key.removeprefix(prefix): value
            for key, value in states.items()
            if key.startswith(prefix)
        }
        model.set_state(member, strict=strict)

def set_reservoir_states(
    self,
    states: list[dict[str, torch.Tensor]],
    strict: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Restore reservoir states in all sub-models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    states : list of dict
        One dict per sub-model as returned by `get_reservoir_states`.
    strict : bool, default=True
        Forwarded to `ESNModel.set_reservoir_states`.  When
        `True` (default), each sub-model raises on missing/unexpected
        reservoir keys.

    Raises
    ------

        If the number of dicts in `states` does not match
        `self.n_models`.

fit(
    warmup_inputs: InputStreams,
    train_inputs: InputStreams,
    targets: ReadoutTargets,
    n_workers: int = 1,
    coerce: bool = False,
) -> None

Train all sub-models independently using resdag.training.ESNTrainer.

Each sub-model is trained separately on the same warmup/train data. Ensemble diversity comes from the different random reservoir initialisations of each sub-model.

Before dispatching to resdag.training.ESNTrainer, every warmup_inputs / train_inputs tensor and every targets value is checked against the ensemble's reference device/dtype (the first sub-model's first floating-point parameter; see _reference_device_dtype). A mismatch raises a clear, named ValueError — e.g. CPU targets fed to a GPU ensemble — instead of a raw cross-device RuntimeError deep inside the readout solve. Pass coerce=True to .to()-coerce the data to the reference instead of raising.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION warmup_inputs

Warmup sequences (feedback, driver1, ...). Shape of each: (batch, warmup_steps, features).

TYPE: tuple of torch.Tensor

train_inputs

Training sequences (feedback, driver1, ...). Shape of each: (batch, train_steps, features).

TYPE: tuple of torch.Tensor

targets

Mapping from readout name to target tensor. Shape of each target: (batch, train_steps, out_features).

TYPE: dict of str to torch.Tensor

n_workers

Number of worker threads used to fit sub-models concurrently. 1 (the default) runs sequentially in the calling thread. Larger values dispatch fits through a concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor — PyTorch releases the GIL during BLAS, so threading gives a real speed-up for CPU-bound CG ridge solves without the pickling cost of multiprocessing. On GPU, all workers share one device and may interfere via the same CUDA stream; benchmark before raising n_workers above 1 in that case.

TYPE: int DEFAULT: `1`

coerce

If False (default), a device/dtype mismatch between any input or target and the ensemble's sub-models raises a clear, named ValueError. If True, such tensors are coerced with .to(device=..., dtype=...) to the reference instead.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: `False`

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If n_workers < 1, or if coerce=False and any input/target tensor's device or dtype does not match the ensemble's sub-models.

Source code in src/resdag/ensemble/coupled.py 
def fit(
    self,
    warmup_inputs: InputStreams,
    train_inputs: InputStreams,
    targets: ReadoutTargets,
    n_workers: int = 1,
    coerce: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Train all sub-models independently using `resdag.training.ESNTrainer`.

    Each sub-model is trained separately on the same warmup/train data.
    Ensemble diversity comes from the different random reservoir
    initialisations of each sub-model.

    Before dispatching to `resdag.training.ESNTrainer`, every
    `warmup_inputs` / `train_inputs` tensor and every `targets` value
    is checked against the ensemble's reference device/dtype (the first
    sub-model's first floating-point parameter; see
    `_reference_device_dtype`).  A mismatch raises a clear, named
    `ValueError` — e.g. CPU targets fed to a GPU ensemble — instead
    of a raw cross-device `RuntimeError` deep inside the readout solve.
    Pass `coerce=True` to `.to()`-coerce the data to the reference
    instead of raising.

    Parameters
    ----------
    warmup_inputs : tuple of torch.Tensor
        Warmup sequences `(feedback, driver1, ...)`.
        Shape of each: `(batch, warmup_steps, features)`.
    train_inputs : tuple of torch.Tensor
        Training sequences `(feedback, driver1, ...)`.
        Shape of each: `(batch, train_steps, features)`.
    targets : dict of str to torch.Tensor
        Mapping from readout name to target tensor.
        Shape of each target: `(batch, train_steps, out_features)`.
    n_workers : int, default `1`
        Number of worker threads used to fit sub-models concurrently.
        `1` (the default) runs sequentially in the calling thread.
        Larger values dispatch fits through a
        `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` — PyTorch releases
        the GIL during BLAS, so threading gives a real speed-up for
        CPU-bound CG ridge solves without the pickling cost of
        multiprocessing.  On GPU, all workers share one device and may
        interfere via the same CUDA stream; benchmark before raising
        `n_workers` above 1 in that case.
    coerce : bool, default `False`
        If `False` (default), a device/dtype mismatch between any input or
        target and the ensemble's sub-models raises a clear, named
        `ValueError`.  If `True`, such tensors are coerced with
        `.to(device=..., dtype=...)` to the reference instead.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `n_workers < 1`, or if `coerce=False` and any input/target
        tensor's device or dtype does not match the ensemble's sub-models.
    """
    if n_workers < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"n_workers must be >= 1, got {n_workers}.")

    warmup_inputs = ESNTrainer._input_tuple(warmup_inputs)
    train_inputs = ESNTrainer._input_tuple(train_inputs)
    if isinstance(targets, torch.Tensor):
        trainer = ESNTrainer(next(self._iter_models()))
        targets = trainer._target_dict(targets, trainer._discover_readouts())
    ref_device, ref_dtype = self._reference_device_dtype()
    warmup_inputs = tuple(
        self._coerce_tensor_to_reference(
            t, ref_device, ref_dtype, coerce=coerce, label=f"warmup_inputs[{i}]"
        )
        for i, t in enumerate(warmup_inputs)
    )
    train_inputs = tuple(
        self._coerce_tensor_to_reference(
            t, ref_device, ref_dtype, coerce=coerce, label=f"train_inputs[{i}]"
        )
        for i, t in enumerate(train_inputs)
    )
    targets = {
        name: self._coerce_tensor_to_reference(
            t, ref_device, ref_dtype, coerce=coerce, label=f"targets[{name!r}]"
        )
        for name, t in targets.items()
    }

    if n_workers == 1 or self.n_models == 1:
        for model in self._iter_models():
            ESNTrainer(model).fit(warmup_inputs, train_inputs, targets)
        return

    # Thread-pool path.  Each thread gets its own ESNTrainer over a
    # distinct sub-model, so there is no shared mutable state to guard.
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

    def _fit_one(model: ESNModel) -> None:
        ESNTrainer(model).fit(warmup_inputs, train_inputs, targets)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(n_workers, self.n_models)) as pool:
        list(pool.map(_fit_one, self.models))

docs.text:
forecast(
    warmup_inputs: tuple[Tensor, ...] | Tensor,
    forecast_inputs: tuple[Tensor, ...] | Tensor | None = None,
    *,
    horizon: int,
    initial_feedback: Tensor | None = None,
    return_warmup: bool = False,
    return_individuals: bool = False,
    reset: bool = True,
    alignment: ForecastAlignment = "next"
) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, list[Tensor]]

Forecast the immediate unseen samples using shared coupled feedback.

All members consume the same observed history. The aggregate of their final warmup predictions is slot zero, then each additional step consumes their previous aggregate. forecast_inputs contains future drivers starting immediately after history and needs horizon - 1 samples. A one-step forecast needs no future driver.

initial_feedback is a distinct extra input after all warmup inputs, shaped (batch, 1, feedback_features); when supplied, every prediction consumes a driver and an empty warmup is supported. reset=False continues saved states. alignment="legacy" reproduces the old convention which skipped the final warmup prediction and needs horizon future drivers. These semantics match ESNModel.forecast.

Results have shape (batch, horizon, output_features). With return_warmup=True, prepend historical predictions: total length is warmup_steps - 1 + horizon, or warmup_steps + horizon with an explicit seed or legacy alignment. With return_individuals=True, also return a list of member trajectories, each covering only the horizon future samples. Per-member buffers are allocated only when requested. horizon must be a positive integer; zero is rejected.

The final returned prediction has not been consumed. Continue with empty history, that prediction as initial_feedback, and reset=False.

@torch.no_grad()
def forecast(
    self,
    warmup_inputs: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] | torch.Tensor,
    forecast_inputs: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] | torch.Tensor | None = None,
    *,
    horizon: int,
    initial_feedback: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    return_warmup: bool = False,
    return_individuals: bool = False,
    reset: bool = True,
    alignment: ForecastAlignment = "next",
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, list[torch.Tensor]]:
    """Forecast the immediate unseen samples using shared coupled feedback.

    All members consume the same observed history. The aggregate of their
    final warmup predictions is slot zero, then each additional step consumes
    their previous aggregate. `forecast_inputs` contains future drivers
    starting immediately after history and needs `horizon - 1` samples.
    A one-step forecast needs no future driver.

    `initial_feedback` is a distinct extra input after all warmup inputs,
    shaped `(batch, 1, feedback_features)`; when supplied, every prediction
    consumes a driver and an empty warmup is supported. `reset=False`
    continues saved states. `alignment="legacy"` reproduces the old
    convention which skipped the final warmup prediction and needs
    `horizon` future drivers. These semantics match `ESNModel.forecast`.

    Results have shape `(batch, horizon, output_features)`. With
    `return_warmup=True`, prepend historical predictions: total length is
    `warmup_steps - 1 + horizon`, or `warmup_steps + horizon` with an
    explicit seed or legacy alignment. With `return_individuals=True`,
    also return a list of member trajectories, each covering only the
    `horizon` future samples. Per-member buffers are allocated only when
    requested. `horizon` must be a positive integer; zero is rejected.

    The final returned prediction has not been consumed. Continue with
    empty history, that prediction as `initial_feedback`, and `reset=False`.
    """
    models = list(self._iter_models())
    for model in models:
        model._get_execution_plan()
    warmup_inputs, drivers, horizon, boundary = prepare_forecast_inputs(
        warmup_inputs,
        forecast_inputs,
        num_inputs=len(models[0].inputs),
        horizon=horizon,
        initial_feedback=initial_feedback,
        alignment=alignment,
    )
    from resdag.core._hooks import has_execution_hooks

    if has_execution_hooks(self):
        return self._forecast_with_hooks(
            warmup_inputs,
            drivers,
            horizon=horizon,
            boundary=boundary,
            initial_feedback=initial_feedback,
            reset=reset,
            return_warmup=return_warmup,
            return_individuals=return_individuals,
        )
    batch_size = warmup_inputs[0].shape[0]
    device, dtype = self._reference_device_dtype()
    warmup_outputs_per_model = [
        cast(torch.Tensor, model.warmup(*warmup_inputs, return_outputs=True, reset=reset))
        for model in models
    ]
    output_size = warmup_outputs_per_model[0].shape[-1]
    forecast_outputs = torch.empty(batch_size, horizon, output_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    individual_outputs = (
        [torch.empty_like(forecast_outputs) for _ in models] if return_individuals else None
    )
    if initial_feedback is None:
        last_steps = [out[:, -1:, :] for out in warmup_outputs_per_model]
        current_feedback = self._coerce_step_for_buffer(
            self._aggregate(last_steps), device, dtype
        )
    else:
        last_steps = []
        current_feedback = self._coerce_step_for_buffer(initial_feedback, device, dtype)
    if boundary:
        forecast_outputs[:, :1, :] = current_feedback
        if individual_outputs is not None:
            for buf, out in zip(individual_outputs, last_steps):
                buf[:, :1, :] = self._coerce_step_for_buffer(out, device, dtype)

    flats: list[FlatStep] = [model._get_flat_step() for model in models]
    states_per_model = [
        self._resolve_member_states(flat, batch_size, device, dtype) for flat in flats
    ]
    for t in range(int(boundary), horizon):
        driver_idx = t - int(boundary)
        step_inputs = (current_feedback,) + tuple(
            driver[:, driver_idx : driver_idx + 1, :] for driver in drivers
        )
        step_outputs = []
        for i, flat in enumerate(flats):
            out_tuple, states_per_model[i] = flat.step(step_inputs, states_per_model[i])
            step_outputs.append(out_tuple[0])
        if individual_outputs is not None:
            for buf, out in zip(individual_outputs, step_outputs):
                buf[:, t : t + 1, :] = self._coerce_step_for_buffer(out, device, dtype)
        current_feedback = self._coerce_step_for_buffer(
            self._aggregate(step_outputs), device, dtype
        )
        forecast_outputs[:, t : t + 1, :] = current_feedback

    for flat, states in zip(flats, states_per_model):
        for reservoir, state in zip(flat.reservoir_layers, states):
            if reservoir.detach_state_between_calls and state.grad_fn is not None:
                reservoir.state = state.detach().clone()
            else:
                reservoir.state = state.clone()
    if return_warmup:
        warmup_avg = self._aggregate_stacked(torch.stack(warmup_outputs_per_model, dim=0))
        if warmup_avg.device != device:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Aggregated warmup output is on device={warmup_avg.device}, but "
                f"the forecast output buffer is on device={device}. A custom "
                "aggregator must keep its output on the sub-models' device."
            )
        warmup_avg = warmup_avg.to(dtype=dtype)
        prefix = warmup_avg[:, :-1, :] if boundary else warmup_avg
        forecast_outputs = torch.cat((prefix, forecast_outputs), dim=1)
    if individual_outputs is not None:
        return forecast_outputs, individual_outputs
    return forecast_outputs

@classmethod
def load_from_file(
    cls,
    path: str | Path,
    model: "CoupledEnsembleESNModel | None" = None,
    strict: bool = True,
    load_states: bool = False,
    map_location: Any = None,
) -> "CoupledEnsembleESNModel":
    """Restore weights into an already constructed matching ensemble."""
    if model is None:
        raise ValueError("model argument is required")
    model.load(path, strict=strict, load_states=load_states, map_location=map_location)
    return model

Aggregators expect a 4-D input of shape (samples, batch, timesteps, features) (or a list of length samples each of shape (batch, timesteps, features)) and return a 3-D tensor of shape (batch, timesteps, features).

They plug into resdag.ensemble.CoupledEnsembleESNModel via the aggregator argument.

docs.title: OutliersFilteredMean
docs.text:
OutliersFilteredMean(method: str = 'z_score', threshold: float | None = None)

Bases: Module

Mean over ensemble members after removing outlier norms.

For each (batch, timestep) location, computes the L2 norm of each member's feature vector, flags outliers via a robust modified Z-score or the IQR rule, then averages the inlier members. If every member is an outlier at a location, falls back to the plain mean.

The "z_score" method uses the modified Z-score 0.6745 * (x - median) / MAD (Iglewicz & Hoaglin, 1993), where MAD is the median absolute deviation. Unlike the classic mean/standard-deviation Z-score, the median and MAD are robust estimators: a single extreme member does not inflate the location/scale used to judge it, so a genuine outlier can be flagged even in small ensembles. (The classic non-robust Z-score saturates at sqrt(N - 1) for a lone outlier among N members, so a threshold=3.0 cutoff could never flag anything until N >= 11.)

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION method

Outlier detection rule applied to per-member norms.

TYPE: (z_score, iqr) DEFAULT: "z_score"

threshold

Detection sensitivity. For "z_score" it is the modified-Z-score cutoff; for "iqr" it is the Tukey fence multiplier. When None, a method-appropriate default is used: 3.5 for "z_score" (the conventional modified-Z-score cutoff) and 1.5 for "iqr" (the conventional Tukey fence). Pass an explicit value to override.

TYPE: float or None DEFAULT: None

Examples:

>>> layer = OutliersFilteredMean(method="z_score")
>>> x = torch.randn(10, 3, 5, 4)  # samples, batch, time, features
>>> layer(x).shape
torch.Size([3, 5, 4])
RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If method is not "z_score" or "iqr".

References

Iglewicz, B. and Hoaglin, D. C. (1993). How to Detect and Handle Outliers. ASQC Quality Press.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION method

How to label outlier members along the samples axis.

TYPE: (z_score, iqr) DEFAULT: "z_score"

threshold

Detection sensitivity (modified-Z-score bound or IQR factor). When None, defaults to 3.5 for "z_score" and 1.5 for "iqr".

TYPE: float or None DEFAULT: None

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If method is not supported.

Source code in src/resdag/ensemble/aggregators/outliers_filtered_mean.py 
def __init__(self, method: str = "z_score", threshold: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Configure outlier detection.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : {"z_score", "iqr"}, default="z_score"
        How to label outlier members along the samples axis.
    threshold : float or None, default=None
        Detection sensitivity (modified-Z-score bound or IQR factor). When
        `None`, defaults to `3.5` for `"z_score"` and `1.5` for
        `"iqr"`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If *method* is not supported.
    """
    super().__init__()

    if method not in ["z_score", "iqr"]:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported method: {method}. Choose 'z_score' or 'iqr'.")

    self.method = method
    if threshold is None:
        threshold = _DEFAULT_Z_THRESHOLD if method == "z_score" else _DEFAULT_IQR_THRESHOLD
    self.threshold = threshold

docs.text:
forward(input: Tensor | list[Tensor]) -> Tensor

Aggregate ensemble members with outlier filtering.

Outlier detection is norm-based and whole-member: each member's L2 feature-vector norm is scored at every (batch, timestep) location, and a flagged member is dropped in its entirety (the whole feature vector is excluded from that location's mean). A member that is an outlier in only one feature but normal in norm is therefore not caught, and one that is off in a single feature enough to inflate its norm is dropped wholesale rather than per feature.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION input

One of:

  • a 4-D tensor of shape (samples, batch, timesteps, features);
  • a 3-D tensor of shape (batch, timesteps, features), treated as a single-member ensemble (a samples axis of length one is inserted);
  • a list of length samples whose members are each 3-D (batch, timesteps, features) tensors.

TYPE: torch.Tensor or list of torch.Tensor

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Tensor

Shape (batch, timesteps, features).

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If input is a tensor whose rank is neither 3-D nor 4-D (for example a 2-D (samples, features) tensor, which would otherwise collapse silently to the wrong shape), or a list whose stacked members are not 4-D.

Source code in src/resdag/ensemble/aggregators/outliers_filtered_mean.py 
def forward(self, input: torch.Tensor | list[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Aggregate ensemble members with outlier filtering.

    Outlier detection is **norm-based and whole-member**: each member's L2
    feature-vector norm is scored at every `(batch, timestep)` location,
    and a flagged member is dropped in its entirety (the whole feature
    vector is excluded from that location's mean). A member that is an
    outlier in only one feature but normal in norm is therefore *not*
    caught, and one that is off in a single feature enough to inflate its
    norm is dropped wholesale rather than per feature.

    Parameters
    ----------
    input : torch.Tensor or list of torch.Tensor
        One of:

        - a 4-D tensor of shape `(samples, batch, timesteps, features)`;
        - a 3-D tensor of shape `(batch, timesteps, features)`, treated
          as a single-member ensemble (a `samples` axis of length one is
          inserted);
        - a list of length *samples* whose members are each 3-D
          `(batch, timesteps, features)` tensors.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        Shape `(batch, timesteps, features)`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If *input* is a tensor whose rank is neither 3-D nor 4-D (for
        example a 2-D `(samples, features)` tensor, which would otherwise
        collapse silently to the wrong shape), or a list whose stacked
        members are not 4-D.
    """
    if isinstance(input, list):
        input = torch.stack(input, dim=0)
        if input.dim() != 4:
            raise ValueError(
                "OutliersFilteredMean expects a list of 3D "
                "(batch, timesteps, features) tensors, but stacking the "
                f"members produced a {input.dim()}D tensor with shape "
                f"{tuple(input.shape)}"
            )
    elif input.dim() == 3:
        input = input.unsqueeze(0)
    elif input.dim() != 4:
        raise ValueError(
            "OutliersFilteredMean expects a 4D "
            "(samples, batch, timesteps, features) tensor, a 3D "
            "(batch, timesteps, features) tensor, or a list of 3D tensors, "
            f"but got a {input.dim()}D tensor with shape {tuple(input.shape)}"
        )

    norms = torch.norm(input, p=2, dim=-1)
    finite = torch.isfinite(input).all(dim=-1) & torch.isfinite(norms)
    invalid_positions = ~finite.any(dim=0)
    if invalid_positions.any():
        positions = invalid_positions.nonzero().detach().cpu().tolist()
        raise ValueError(
            f"All {input.shape[0]} ensemble members have non-finite predictions or "
            f"prediction norms at (batch, timestep) positions {positions[:5]}. "
            "Check the member forecasts before continuing coupled feedback."
        )

    if self.method == "z_score":
        mask = self._mask_modified_z_score(norms, finite)
    else:
        mask = self._mask_iqr(norms, finite)

    # Multiplication cannot remove NaN/Inf (Inf * 0 is NaN). Exclude
    # invalid members before any arithmetic, including the fallback mean.
    work = input.float() if input.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) else input
    safe_input = torch.where(finite.unsqueeze(-1), work, 0)
    plain_mean = safe_input.sum(dim=0) / finite.sum(dim=0).unsqueeze(-1)
    mask_expanded = (mask & finite).unsqueeze(-1)
    masked_input = torch.where(mask_expanded, work, 0)
    sum_inliers = masked_input.sum(dim=0)
    count_inliers = mask_expanded.sum(dim=0).expand_as(sum_inliers)

    mean_result = torch.where(
        count_inliers > 0,
        sum_inliers / count_inliers.clamp(min=1),
        plain_mean,
    )

    return mean_result.to(dtype=input.dtype)

docs.title: Training
docs.text:
ESNTrainer fits raw ESNModel graphs with each readout's configured solver. Its fit method processes the complete warmup-plus-training prefix in dependency order: a readout is fitted before its output reaches a downstream reservoir. Each reservoir consumes the continuous prefix once. Use Model.fit or ESN.fit when you also need training-only scaling, named signals and original units; see the common workflow.

For long streams, fit_stream accepts chunks and incremental ridge readouts, then finalizes their accumulated statistics. fit_force trains a single RLS head inside the autonomous feedback loop. Direct online fitting is available on RLSReadout.fit_online, not as another trainer method. See streaming and training for these distinct lifecycles.

Calibration functions change reservoir operating points using observed training inputs and return a CalibrationReport. They are explicit steps, separate from readout fitting and default model construction.

docs.text:
This module provides trainers for ESN models that fit readout layers algebraically using ridge regression, rather than stochastic gradient descent.

CLASS DESCRIPTION ESNTrainer

Trainer for fitting readout layers in ESN models.

Examples:

>>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
>>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
...     train_inputs=(train,),
...     targets={"output": target},
... )
See Also

resdag.layers.readouts.CGReadoutLayer : Readout with CG solver. resdag.core.ESNModel : ESN model class.

docs.title: ESNTrainer
docs.text:
ESNTrainer(model: ESNModel)

Trainer for ESN models with algebraic readout fitting.

This trainer fits all ReadoutLayer instances in an ESN model using algebraic methods (e.g., ridge regression) rather than gradient descent. Pre-hooks fit each readout using its supervised training rows before it evaluates the complete prefix. Downstream reservoirs therefore receive fitted upstream predictions throughout warmup and training.

The training process:

  1. Reset reservoir states
  2. Traverse the complete warmup and training prefix once per graph node
  3. Fit each readout on training rows before forwarding its full prefix
  4. Reuse branches and release feature tensors after their last consumer

Each readout handles its own fitting hyperparameters (e.g., alpha for ridge regression is set during layer construction).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION model

ESN model to train. Must contain at least one ReadoutLayer.

TYPE: ESNModel

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION model

The ESN model being trained.

TYPE: ESNModel

Examples:

Basic training workflow:

>>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
>>> from resdag.core import ESNModel
>>>
>>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup_data,),
...     train_inputs=(train_data,),
...     targets={"output": train_targets},
... )

Training with driving inputs:

>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup_feedback, warmup_driver),
...     train_inputs=(train_feedback, train_driver),
...     targets={"output": targets},
... )

Multi-readout training:

>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup_data,),
...     train_inputs=(train_data,),
...     targets={
...         "position": position_targets,
...         "velocity": velocity_targets,
...     },
... )
See Also

ESNModel : ESN model class. CGReadoutLayer : Conjugate gradient readout layer. ESNModel.forecast : Forecasting after training.

Notes
  • Warmup and training data must have the same number of input tensors.
  • Training data and targets must have the same sequence length.
  • Target keys must match readout names (user-defined or auto-generated).
